### Task 4: The reach check for a dot a maker asks for

`reach_new` and `reach_change` turn what a maker asks for into the dot's spec, the same spec without what is beyond the maker's reach, and the list of those extras, each row of the table in spec section 6. Pure but for reading the disk for folders. On a change, what the dot already holds is never an extra.

**Files:**
- Create: `crates/dots-core/src/making/mod.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/making/reach.rs`
- Modify: `crates/dots-core/src/lib.rs`
- Test: `crates/dots-core/tests/making_reach_test.rs`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `Dot`, `DotSpec`, `Preset`, `Schedule`.
- Produces: `making::reach::Wanted` (every field optional: `name`, `instructions`, `model`, `folder`, `permissions`, `uses`, `variables`, `browser: Option<bool>`, `use_user_settings`, `max_turns`, `timeout_secs`, `schedule: Option<Option<Schedule>>`; `deny_unknown_fields`); `WantedPermissions::{Maker, Preset(Preset)}` (JSON `"maker"`, `"read-only"`, `"sandboxed"`, `"trusted"`); `NO_SCHEDULE = "none"`; `Extra::{Item { item_kind, name }, Variable { consumer, name }, Preset { preset, makers }, Folder { path, below_maker }, Browser, UserSettings, MaxTurns { wanted, makers }, Timeout { wanted_secs, makers_secs }}` with `line(&self, maker: &str) -> String`; `Reach { spec: DotSpec, without: DotSpec, extras: Vec<Extra>, create_folder: Option<PathBuf> }`; `real_path`; `reach_new(maker: &Dot, wanted: &Wanted, worktrees_root: &Path) -> Result<Reach>`; `reach_change(maker: &Dot, made: &Dot, wanted: &Wanted, worktrees_root: &Path) -> Result<Reach>`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

**Create `crates/dots-core/tests/making_reach_test.rs`:**

```rust
//! The reach check (dots-make-dots design sections 6, 7.2 and 9): what a maker asks for a new
//! dot, or as a change to a dot it made, becomes the whole dot, the parts beyond the maker's
//! reach, and the dot without them. Each row of the table in section 6 and each folder rule is
//! tried within reach and beyond it.

mod common;

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use common::fake_dot;
use dots_core::context_rules::ContextRules;
use dots_core::library::{LibraryKind, Uses};
use dots_core::making::reach::{
    reach_change, reach_new, real_path, Extra, Reach, Wanted, WantedPermissions,
};
use dots_core::model::{Dot, DotSpec, EngineKind, Making, WorkspaceMode};
use dots_core::policy::{Action, Policy, Preset, Rule};
use dots_core::schedule::Schedule;
use dots_core::spend::DotCaps;
use dots_core::vault::Grants;
use dots_core::Error;
use tempfile::TempDir;

/// The folders of a test: the maker's, one outside it, and where worktree copies are made.
struct Place {
    _tmp: TempDir,
    maker_dir: PathBuf,
    outside: PathBuf,
    worktrees: PathBuf,
}

fn place() -> Place {
    let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let root = real_path(tmp.path());
    let place = Place {
        maker_dir: root.join("maker"),
        outside: root.join("outside"),
        worktrees: root.join("data").join("worktrees"),
        _tmp: tmp,
    };
    for dir in [&place.maker_dir, &place.outside, &place.worktrees] {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).unwrap();
    }
    place
}

fn text(path: &Path) -> String {
    path.to_string_lossy().into_owned()
}

/// A maker named Researcher in `place`'s folder: sandboxed, 40 turns, 30 minutes.
fn maker(place: &Place, mode: WorkspaceMode) -> Dot {
    let mut dot = fake_dot("Researcher", &place.maker_dir, mode);
    dot.spec.making.on = true;
    dot
}

fn wanted() -> Wanted {
    Wanted {
        name: Some("Blog Watcher".into()),
        instructions: Some("Watch three blogs.".into()),
        ..Wanted::default()
    }
}

fn new(maker: &Dot, wanted: &Wanted, place: &Place) -> Reach {
    reach_new(maker, wanted, &place.worktrees).unwrap()
}

fn names(list: &[&str]) -> Vec<String> {
    list.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect()
}

fn grants(pairs: &[(&str, &[&str])]) -> Grants {
    Grants(
        pairs
            .iter()
            .map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), names(v)))
            .collect(),
    )
}

fn item(kind: LibraryKind, name: &str) -> Extra {
    Extra::Item {
        item_kind: kind,
        name: name.into(),
    }
}

fn variable(consumer: &str, name: &str) -> Extra {
    Extra::Variable {
        consumer: consumer.into(),
        name: name.into(),
    }
}

fn daily() -> Schedule {
    serde_json::from_value(serde_json::json!({"rule": {"kind": "daily", "time": "09:00"}})).unwrap()
}

/// `spec` as `DotSpec::validate` takes it: a blank folder is filled when the dot is created
/// (`DotAdmin::create`), so it stands in here.
fn assert_valid(spec: &DotSpec) {
    let mut spec = spec.clone();
    if spec.workdir.is_empty() {
        spec.workdir = "C:/tmp/new".into();
    }
    spec.validate().unwrap();
}

fn invalid(result: dots_core::Result<Reach>) -> String {
    match result {
        Err(Error::Invalid(text)) => text,
        other => panic!("expected Invalid, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

/// One item of each kind.
fn uses_all() -> Uses {
    Uses {
        mcp_servers: names(&["github"]),
        skills: names(&["pdf-tools"]),
        plugins: names(&["reviewer"]),
        context: names(&["handbook"]),
        apps: names(&["blog_board"]),
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_new_dot_with_only_a_name_and_instructions_takes_the_makers_settings_and_nothing_more() {
    let place = place();
    let mut maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Worktree);
    let m = &mut maker.spec;
    m.engine = EngineKind::Local;
    m.model = "qwen3".into();
    m.endpoint_url = Some("http://127.0.0.1:1234".into());
    m.policy
        .rules
        .push(Rule::new("Bash(npm test:*)", Action::Allow));
    m.policy.preset = Preset::Custom;
    m.uses = uses_all();
    m.variables = grants(&[("shell", &["NPM_TOKEN"])]);
    m.browser = true;
    m.use_user_settings = true;
    m.max_turns = 55;
    m.timeout_secs = 999;
    m.approval_wait_secs = 100;
    m.quiet_limit_secs = Some(600);
    m.use_global_instructions = false;
    m.check_results = false;
    m.use_graph = false;
    m.context_rules = Some(ContextRules {
        enabled: true,
        compact_at: 50,
        clear_at: 70,
    });
    m.spend_cap = DotCaps {
        daily_usd: Some(2.0),
        daily_tokens: None,
    };
    m.schedule = Some(daily());
    m.enabled = false;

    let reach = new(&maker, &wanted(), &place);
    let m = &maker.spec;
    let expected = DotSpec {
        name: "Blog Watcher".into(),
        instructions: "Watch three blogs.".into(),
        engine: EngineKind::Local,
        model: "qwen3".into(),
        endpoint_url: Some("http://127.0.0.1:1234".into()),
        workdir: String::new(),
        workspace_mode: WorkspaceMode::Folder,
        schedule: None,
        policy: m.policy.clone(),
        uses: Uses::default(),
        variables: Grants::default(),
        browser: false,
        quiet_limit_secs: Some(600),
        spend_cap: DotCaps::default(),
        use_global_instructions: false,
        check_results: false,
        use_graph: false,
        context_rules: m.context_rules,
        making: Making::default(),
        use_user_settings: false,
        max_turns: 55,
        timeout_secs: 999,
        approval_wait_secs: 100,
        enabled: true,
    };
    assert_eq!(reach.spec, expected);
    assert_eq!(reach.without, expected);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.create_folder, None);
    assert!(!reach.spec.making.on);
}

#[test]
fn a_new_dot_needs_a_name_and_instructions_and_must_be_a_valid_dot() {
    let place = place();
    let maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    let mut w = wanted();
    w.name = None;
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(reach_new(&maker, &w, &place.worktrees)),
        "A new dot needs a name."
    );
    w.name = Some("  ".into());
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(reach_new(&maker, &w, &place.worktrees)),
        "A new dot needs a name."
    );
    let mut w = wanted();
    w.instructions = Some(String::new());
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(reach_new(&maker, &w, &place.worktrees)),
        "A new dot needs instructions."
    );
    // Today's rules for any dot (design section 6, notes).
    let mut w = wanted();
    w.name = Some("bad/name".into());
    assert!(invalid(reach_new(&maker, &w, &place.worktrees)).contains("1 to 64"));
    let mut w = wanted();
    w.max_turns = Some(0);
    assert!(invalid(reach_new(&maker, &w, &place.worktrees)).contains("max_turns"));
    // `Custom` is no plain preset.
    let mut w = wanted();
    w.permissions = Some(WantedPermissions::Preset(Preset::Custom));
    assert!(invalid(reach_new(&maker, &w, &place.worktrees)).contains("permissions is"));
}

#[test]
fn a_named_model_and_schedule_are_taken_as_asked() {
    let place = place();
    let maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    let mut w = wanted();
    w.model = Some("haiku".into());
    w.schedule = Some(Some(daily()));
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.model, "haiku");
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.schedule, Some(daily()));
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.spec, reach.without);
    // "No schedule" is what a new dot has anyway.
    w.schedule = Some(None);
    assert_eq!(new(&maker, &w, &place).spec.schedule, None);
}

#[test]
fn an_item_the_maker_uses_is_within_reach_and_one_it_lacks_is_an_extra() {
    let place = place();
    let mut maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    maker.spec.uses = uses_all();

    let mut w = wanted();
    w.uses = Some(uses_all());
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.uses, uses_all());
    assert_eq!(reach.spec, reach.without);

    // One more of each kind, which the maker lacks.
    let mut more = uses_all();
    more.mcp_servers.push("slack".into());
    more.skills.push("xlsx".into());
    more.plugins.push("linter".into());
    more.context.push("pricing".into());
    more.apps.push("crm".into());
    w.uses = Some(more.clone());
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(
        reach.extras,
        vec![
            item(LibraryKind::McpServer, "slack"),
            item(LibraryKind::Skill, "xlsx"),
            item(LibraryKind::Plugin, "linter"),
            item(LibraryKind::Context, "pricing"),
            item(LibraryKind::App, "crm"),
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.uses, more);
    assert_eq!(reach.without.uses, uses_all());

    // A name the maker has under another kind is not the maker's item.
    let mut w = wanted();
    w.uses = Some(Uses {
        skills: names(&["github"]),
        ..Uses::default()
    });
    assert_eq!(
        new(&maker, &w, &place).extras,
        vec![item(LibraryKind::Skill, "github")]
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_variable_is_within_reach_only_for_the_consumer_the_maker_is_granted_it_for() {
    let place = place();
    let mut maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    maker.spec.uses.mcp_servers = names(&["github"]);
    maker.spec.variables = grants(&[
        ("mcp:github", &["GITHUB_TOKEN", "GITHUB_ORG"]),
        ("shell", &["NPM_TOKEN"]),
    ]);

    let mut w = wanted();
    w.uses = Some(maker.spec.uses.clone());
    // Granted, in any case, as `Grants::allows` reads names.
    w.variables = Some(grants(&[
        ("mcp:github", &["github_token"]),
        ("shell", &["NPM_TOKEN"]),
    ]));
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.variables, w.variables.clone().unwrap());
    assert_eq!(reach.spec, reach.without);

    // Not granted at all, and granted for a different consumer only.
    w.variables = Some(grants(&[
        ("mcp:github", &["GITHUB_TOKEN", "NPM_TOKEN"]),
        ("shell", &["NPM_TOKEN", "GITHUB_TOKEN", "AWS_KEY"]),
    ]));
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(
        reach.extras,
        vec![
            variable("mcp:github", "NPM_TOKEN"),
            variable("shell", "GITHUB_TOKEN"),
            variable("shell", "AWS_KEY"),
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.variables, w.variables.clone().unwrap());
    assert_eq!(
        reach.without.variables,
        grants(&[("mcp:github", &["GITHUB_TOKEN"]), ("shell", &["NPM_TOKEN"])])
    );

    // A consumer left with no name is dropped.
    w.variables = Some(grants(&[("shell", &["AWS_KEY"])]));
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(reach.extras, vec![variable("shell", "AWS_KEY")]);
    assert_eq!(reach.without.variables, Grants::default());
}

#[test]
fn a_plain_preset_is_within_reach_when_no_stronger_than_the_makers() {
    let place = place();
    let order = [Preset::ReadOnly, Preset::Sandboxed, Preset::Trusted];
    for (m, makers) in order.iter().enumerate() {
        let mut maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
        maker.spec.policy = Policy::preset(*makers);
        for (p, preset) in order.iter().enumerate() {
            let mut w = wanted();
            w.permissions = Some(WantedPermissions::Preset(*preset));
            let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
            assert_eq!(reach.spec.policy, Policy::preset(*preset));
            if p <= m {
                assert!(reach.extras.is_empty(), "{makers:?} gives {preset:?}");
                assert_eq!(reach.spec, reach.without);
            } else {
                assert_eq!(
                    reach.extras,
                    vec![Extra::Preset {
                        preset: *preset,
                        makers: *makers
                    }],
                    "{makers:?} gives {preset:?}"
                );
                // Lowered to the maker's.
                assert_eq!(reach.without.policy, maker.spec.policy);
            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_custom_maker_gives_its_own_policy_or_read_only() {
    let place = place();
    let mut maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    maker.spec.policy = Policy::preset(Preset::Trusted);
    maker
        .spec
        .policy
        .rules
        .push(Rule::new("Bash(rm:*)", Action::Deny));
    maker.spec.policy.preset = Preset::Custom;

    let mut w = wanted();
    w.permissions = Some(WantedPermissions::Maker);
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.policy, maker.spec.policy);

    w.permissions = Some(WantedPermissions::Preset(Preset::ReadOnly));
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.policy, Policy::preset(Preset::ReadOnly));
    assert_eq!(reach.spec, reach.without);

    for preset in [Preset::Sandboxed, Preset::Trusted] {
        w.permissions = Some(WantedPermissions::Preset(preset));
        let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
        assert_eq!(
            reach.extras,
            vec![Extra::Preset {
                preset,
                makers: Preset::Custom
            }]
        );
        assert_eq!(reach.spec.policy, Policy::preset(preset));
        assert_eq!(reach.without.policy, maker.spec.policy);
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_browser_and_the_user_settings_are_within_reach_only_if_the_maker_has_them() {
    let place = place();
    let mut maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    let mut w = wanted();
    w.browser = Some(true);
    w.use_user_settings = Some(true);

    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(reach.extras, vec![Extra::Browser, Extra::UserSettings]);
    assert!(reach.spec.browser && reach.spec.use_user_settings);
    assert!(!reach.without.browser && !reach.without.use_user_settings);

    maker.spec.browser = true;
    maker.spec.use_user_settings = true;
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert!(reach.spec.browser && reach.spec.use_user_settings);
    assert_eq!(reach.spec, reach.without);

    // Asking for them off never asks.
    w.browser = Some(false);
    w.use_user_settings = Some(false);
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert!(!reach.spec.browser && !reach.spec.use_user_settings);
}

#[test]
fn a_limit_equal_to_the_makers_is_within_reach_above_is_an_extra_and_below_is_kept() {
    let place = place();
    let maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    assert_eq!((maker.spec.max_turns, maker.spec.timeout_secs), (40, 1800));

    let mut w = wanted();
    w.max_turns = Some(40);
    w.timeout_secs = Some(1800);
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!((reach.spec.max_turns, reach.spec.timeout_secs), (40, 1800));

    w.max_turns = Some(41);
    w.timeout_secs = Some(7200);
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(
        reach.extras,
        vec![
            Extra::MaxTurns {
                wanted: 41,
                makers: 40
            },
            Extra::Timeout {
                wanted_secs: 7200,
                makers_secs: 1800
            },
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!((reach.spec.max_turns, reach.spec.timeout_secs), (41, 7200));
    assert_eq!(
        (reach.without.max_turns, reach.without.timeout_secs),
        (40, 1800)
    );

    w.max_turns = Some(5);
    w.timeout_secs = Some(60);
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!((reach.spec.max_turns, reach.spec.timeout_secs), (5, 60));
    assert_eq!(reach.spec, reach.without);
}

#[test]
fn without_is_the_request_minus_every_extra_and_a_valid_dot() {
    let place = place();
    let mut maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    maker.spec.uses.skills = names(&["pdf-tools"]);
    maker.spec.variables = grants(&[("shell", &["NPM_TOKEN"])]);

    let mut w = wanted();
    w.model = Some("haiku".into());
    w.folder = Some(text(&place.outside));
    w.permissions = Some(WantedPermissions::Preset(Preset::Trusted));
    w.uses = Some(Uses {
        mcp_servers: names(&["github"]),
        skills: names(&["pdf-tools", "xlsx"]),
        ..Uses::default()
    });
    w.variables = Some(grants(&[
        ("mcp:github", &["GITHUB_TOKEN"]),
        ("shell", &["NPM_TOKEN", "AWS_KEY"]),
    ]));
    w.browser = Some(true);
    w.use_user_settings = Some(true);
    w.max_turns = Some(80);
    w.timeout_secs = Some(7200);
    w.schedule = Some(Some(daily()));

    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(
        reach.extras,
        vec![
            item(LibraryKind::McpServer, "github"),
            item(LibraryKind::Skill, "xlsx"),
            variable("mcp:github", "GITHUB_TOKEN"),
            variable("shell", "AWS_KEY"),
            Extra::Preset {
                preset: Preset::Trusted,
                makers: Preset::Sandboxed
            },
            Extra::Folder {
                path: text(&place.outside),
                below_maker: false
            },
            Extra::Browser,
            Extra::UserSettings,
            Extra::MaxTurns {
                wanted: 80,
                makers: 40
            },
            Extra::Timeout {
                wanted_secs: 7200,
                makers_secs: 1800
            },
        ]
    );

    // As asked.
    let spec = &reach.spec;
    assert_eq!(spec.workdir, text(&place.outside));
    assert_eq!(spec.workspace_mode, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    assert_eq!(spec.policy, Policy::preset(Preset::Trusted));
    assert_eq!(spec.uses, w.uses.clone().unwrap());
    assert_eq!(spec.variables, w.variables.clone().unwrap());
    assert!(spec.browser && spec.use_user_settings);
    assert_eq!((spec.max_turns, spec.timeout_secs), (80, 7200));
    assert_valid(spec);

    // The same dot with nothing asked beyond reach: what is within reach stays.
    let mut plain = w.clone();
    plain.folder = None;
    plain.permissions = None;
    plain.uses = Some(Uses {
        skills: names(&["pdf-tools"]),
        ..Uses::default()
    });
    plain.variables = Some(grants(&[("shell", &["NPM_TOKEN"])]));
    plain.browser = None;
    plain.use_user_settings = None;
    plain.max_turns = None;
    plain.timeout_secs = None;
    let within = new(&maker, &plain, &place);
    assert!(within.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.without, within.spec);
    assert_eq!(reach.without.model, "haiku");
    assert_eq!(reach.without.schedule, Some(daily()));
    assert_eq!(reach.without.workdir, "");
    assert_eq!(reach.without.policy, maker.spec.policy);
    assert_valid(&reach.without);
}

#[test]
fn a_blank_folder_is_a_new_folder_of_the_dots_own() {
    let place = place();
    for mode in [WorkspaceMode::Folder, WorkspaceMode::Worktree] {
        let maker = maker(&place, mode);
        for folder in [None, Some(String::new()), Some("  ".to_string())] {
            let mut w = wanted();
            w.folder = folder;
            let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
            assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
            assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, "");
            assert_eq!(reach.spec.workspace_mode, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
            assert_eq!(reach.create_folder, None);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_makers_own_folder_is_within_reach_in_the_makers_mode() {
    let place = place();
    for mode in [WorkspaceMode::Folder, WorkspaceMode::Worktree] {
        let maker = maker(&place, mode);
        // Named as it is, and by a relative path from itself.
        for folder in [text(&place.maker_dir), ".".to_string()] {
            let mut w = wanted();
            w.folder = Some(folder);
            let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
            assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
            assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, maker.spec.workdir);
            assert_eq!(reach.spec.workspace_mode, mode);
            assert_eq!(reach.create_folder, None);
            assert_eq!(reach.spec, reach.without);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_subfolder_of_a_folder_mode_maker_is_within_reach_and_made_when_missing() {
    let place = place();
    let maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    let there = place.maker_dir.join("research").join("blogs");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&there).unwrap();
    let missing = place.maker_dir.join("research").join("new").join("deep");

    // One that exists, given absolute and given relative.
    for folder in [
        text(&there),
        "research/blogs".to_string(),
        r"research\blogs".to_string(),
    ] {
        let mut w = wanted();
        w.folder = Some(folder);
        let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
        assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, text(&there));
        assert_eq!(reach.spec.workspace_mode, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
        assert_eq!(reach.create_folder, None);
        assert_eq!(reach.spec, reach.without);
    }

    // One that does not exist yet: the caller makes it; this check makes nothing.
    for folder in [text(&missing), "research/new/deep".to_string()] {
        let mut w = wanted();
        w.folder = Some(folder);
        let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
        assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, text(&missing));
        assert_eq!(reach.spec.workspace_mode, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
        assert_eq!(reach.create_folder, Some(missing.clone()));
        assert_eq!(reach.spec, reach.without);
        assert!(!place.maker_dir.join("research").join("new").exists());
    }

    // A worktree-mode maker's own mode does not reach a subfolder; see the test below. And a
    // file is no folder.
    std::fs::write(place.maker_dir.join("notes.txt"), "x").unwrap();
    for folder in ["notes.txt", "notes.txt/below"] {
        let mut w = wanted();
        w.folder = Some(folder.into());
        assert!(invalid(reach_new(&maker, &w, &place.worktrees)).contains("is a file"));
    }
}

#[test]
fn dot_dot_that_climbs_out_of_the_makers_folder_is_anywhere_else() {
    let place = place();
    let maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    std::fs::create_dir_all(place.maker_dir.join("research")).unwrap();

    let mut w = wanted();
    w.folder = Some("research/../../outside".into());
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(
        reach.extras,
        vec![Extra::Folder {
            path: text(&place.outside),
            below_maker: false
        }]
    );
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, text(&place.outside));
    assert_eq!(reach.without.workdir, "");

    // Through a folder that does not exist, too.
    w.folder = Some("nowhere/../../outside".into());
    assert_eq!(new(&maker, &w, &place).extras, reach.extras);

    // A `..` that stays inside is inside.
    w.folder = Some("research/../research".into());
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, text(&place.maker_dir.join("research")));
}

#[test]
fn a_subfolder_under_a_worktree_mode_maker_is_an_extra() {
    let place = place();
    let maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Worktree);
    let there = place.maker_dir.join("docs");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&there).unwrap();

    let mut w = wanted();
    w.folder = Some("docs".into());
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(
        reach.extras,
        vec![Extra::Folder {
            path: text(&there),
            below_maker: true
        }]
    );
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, text(&there));
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.workspace_mode, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    assert_eq!(reach.create_folder, None);
    assert_eq!(reach.without.workdir, "");
    assert_eq!(reach.without.workspace_mode, WorkspaceMode::Folder);

    // One still to be made is made only if the person allows it.
    let missing = place.maker_dir.join("docs").join("new");
    w.folder = Some("docs/new".into());
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(
        reach.extras,
        vec![Extra::Folder {
            path: text(&missing),
            below_maker: true
        }]
    );
    assert_eq!(reach.create_folder, Some(missing));
}

#[test]
fn a_folder_inside_a_runs_worktree_copy_is_refused() {
    let place = place();
    let copy = place.worktrees.join("01RUN");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(copy.join("src")).unwrap();
    for mode in [WorkspaceMode::Folder, WorkspaceMode::Worktree] {
        let maker = maker(&place, mode);
        for folder in [
            text(&copy),
            text(&copy.join("src")),
            text(&copy.join("not-there")),
            text(&place.worktrees),
        ] {
            let mut w = wanted();
            w.folder = Some(folder);
            let said = invalid(reach_new(&maker, &w, &place.worktrees));
            assert_eq!(
                said,
                "That folder is a run's working copy, which does not last. Leave the folder \
                 blank for a new one, or use Researcher's own folder."
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn anywhere_else_is_an_extra_when_it_exists_and_refused_when_it_does_not() {
    let place = place();
    for mode in [WorkspaceMode::Folder, WorkspaceMode::Worktree] {
        let maker = maker(&place, mode);
        let mut w = wanted();
        w.folder = Some(text(&place.outside));
        let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
        assert_eq!(
            reach.extras,
            vec![Extra::Folder {
                path: text(&place.outside),
                below_maker: false
            }]
        );
        assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, text(&place.outside));
        assert_eq!(reach.spec.workspace_mode, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
        assert_eq!(reach.create_folder, None);
        assert_eq!(reach.without.workdir, "");

        // The folder above the maker's is not the maker's.
        w.folder = Some("..".into());
        let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
        assert!(matches!(
            reach.extras[..],
            [Extra::Folder {
                below_maker: false,
                ..
            }]
        ));

        let missing = place.outside.join("not-there");
        w.folder = Some(text(&missing));
        assert_eq!(
            invalid(reach_new(&maker, &w, &place.worktrees)),
            format!(
                "The folder {} does not exist. Leave the folder blank for a new one, or name \
                 one that exists.",
                missing.display()
            )
        );
        std::fs::write(place.outside.join("file.txt"), "x").unwrap();
        w.folder = Some(text(&place.outside.join("file.txt")));
        assert!(invalid(reach_new(&maker, &w, &place.worktrees)).contains("is a file"));
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
#[test]
fn a_difference_of_case_does_not_put_an_inside_path_outside() {
    let place = place();
    let there = place.maker_dir.join("Research");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&there).unwrap();
    let mut maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    // The maker's folder as the person typed it.
    maker.spec.workdir = maker.spec.workdir.to_uppercase();

    let mut w = wanted();
    w.folder = Some(text(&there).to_lowercase());
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    // The real path, in the case the folder has.
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, text(&there));

    // Parts that do not exist yet are compared without their case as well.
    w.folder = Some(text(&place.maker_dir.join("NEW")).to_lowercase());
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.create_folder, Some(place.maker_dir.join("new")));

    // And the maker's own folder in another case is the maker's own.
    w.folder = Some(text(&place.maker_dir).to_lowercase());
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, maker.spec.workdir);
}

/// Makes `link` lead to the folder `to`: a symlink, or on Windows a junction where this PC
/// may not make symlinks. `false` when it can make neither.
fn link_dir(to: &Path, link: &Path) -> bool {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        if std::os::windows::fs::symlink_dir(to, link).is_ok() {
            return true;
        }
        std::process::Command::new("cmd")
            .args(["/c", "mklink", "/J"])
            .arg(link)
            .arg(to)
            .output()
            .is_ok_and(|out| out.status.success())
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(to, link).is_ok()
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_link_inside_the_makers_folder_that_leads_outside_is_outside() {
    let place = place();
    let maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    std::fs::create_dir_all(place.outside.join("deep")).unwrap();
    let link = place.maker_dir.join("shortcut");
    if !link_dir(&place.outside, &link) {
        eprintln!("skipped: this PC can make neither a symlink nor a junction");
        return;
    }

    for (folder, real) in [
        ("shortcut", place.outside.clone()),
        ("shortcut/deep", place.outside.join("deep")),
    ] {
        let mut w = wanted();
        w.folder = Some(folder.into());
        let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
        assert_eq!(
            reach.extras,
            vec![Extra::Folder {
                path: text(&real),
                below_maker: false
            }]
        );
        assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, text(&real));
    }

    // Outside, so it must exist.
    let mut w = wanted();
    w.folder = Some("shortcut/not-there".into());
    assert!(invalid(reach_new(&maker, &w, &place.worktrees)).contains("does not exist"));

    // A link outside that leads into the maker's folder is inside.
    let back = place.outside.join("back");
    assert!(link_dir(&place.maker_dir, &back));
    let mut w = wanted();
    w.folder = Some(text(&back));
    let reach = new(&maker, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, maker.spec.workdir);
}

/// A dot Researcher made, which the person then gave more than Researcher has.
fn made_dot(place: &Place) -> Dot {
    let dir = place.maker_dir.join("blogs");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
    let mut dot = fake_dot("Blog Watcher", &dir, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    let s = &mut dot.spec;
    s.policy = Policy::preset(Preset::Trusted);
    s.uses.skills = names(&["pdf-tools", "xlsx"]);
    s.uses.mcp_servers = names(&["slack"]);
    s.variables = grants(&[("mcp:slack", &["SLACK_TOKEN"]), ("shell", &["AWS_KEY"])]);
    s.browser = true;
    s.use_user_settings = true;
    s.max_turns = 60;
    s.timeout_secs = 3600;
    s.making = Making {
        on: true,
        per_run: 2,
        total: 5,
    };
    s.enabled = false;
    s.spend_cap = DotCaps {
        daily_usd: Some(1.5),
        daily_tokens: None,
    };
    s.schedule = Some(daily());
    dot
}

fn change(maker: &Dot, made: &Dot, wanted: &Wanted, place: &Place) -> Reach {
    reach_change(maker, made, wanted, &place.worktrees).unwrap()
}

#[test]
fn a_change_of_the_instructions_alone_changes_nothing_else_and_asks_nothing() {
    let place = place();
    let mut maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    maker.spec.uses.skills = names(&["pdf-tools"]);
    let made = made_dot(&place);

    let w = Wanted {
        instructions: Some("Watch four blogs.".into()),
        ..Wanted::default()
    };
    let reach = change(&maker, &made, &w, &place);
    let mut expected = made.spec.clone();
    expected.instructions = "Watch four blogs.".into();
    assert_eq!(reach.spec, expected);
    assert_eq!(reach.without, expected);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.create_folder, None);
    // Its own making settings, switch, cap and schedule stay as the person has them.
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.making, made.spec.making);
    assert!(!reach.spec.enabled);
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.spend_cap, made.spec.spend_cap);
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.schedule, Some(daily()));

    // Nothing named at all is no change.
    let reach = change(&maker, &made, &Wanted::default(), &place);
    assert_eq!(reach.spec, made.spec);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn a_change_names_as_an_extra_only_what_the_dot_does_not_hold_already() {
    let place = place();
    let mut maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    maker.spec.uses.skills = names(&["pdf-tools"]);
    maker.spec.variables = grants(&[("shell", &["NPM_TOKEN"])]);
    let made = made_dot(&place);

    // `xlsx` and `slack` are held already; `docx` is new and the maker lacks it.
    let mut uses = made.spec.uses.clone();
    uses.skills.push("docx".into());
    let w = Wanted {
        uses: Some(uses.clone()),
        variables: Some(grants(&[
            ("mcp:slack", &["SLACK_TOKEN", "SLACK_TEAM"]),
            ("shell", &["AWS_KEY", "NPM_TOKEN"]),
        ])),
        ..Wanted::default()
    };
    let reach = change(&maker, &made, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(
        reach.extras,
        vec![
            item(LibraryKind::Skill, "docx"),
            variable("mcp:slack", "SLACK_TEAM"),
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.uses, uses);
    assert_eq!(reach.without.uses, made.spec.uses);
    assert_eq!(
        reach.without.variables,
        grants(&[
            ("mcp:slack", &["SLACK_TOKEN"]),
            ("shell", &["AWS_KEY", "NPM_TOKEN"])
        ])
    );
    // The rest of the dot is as it was, in both.
    let mut rest = reach.spec.clone();
    rest.uses = made.spec.uses.clone();
    rest.variables = made.spec.variables.clone();
    assert_eq!(rest, made.spec);
}

#[test]
fn removing_and_lowering_never_ask() {
    let place = place();
    let maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    let made = made_dot(&place);

    let w = Wanted {
        uses: Some(Uses {
            skills: names(&["xlsx"]),
            ..Uses::default()
        }),
        variables: Some(Grants::default()),
        browser: Some(false),
        use_user_settings: Some(false),
        // Below the dot's own, above the maker's.
        max_turns: Some(50),
        timeout_secs: Some(2400),
        permissions: Some(WantedPermissions::Preset(Preset::Sandboxed)),
        schedule: Some(None),
        ..Wanted::default()
    };
    let reach = change(&maker, &made, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty(), "{:?}", reach.extras);
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.uses.skills, names(&["xlsx"]));
    assert!(reach.spec.uses.mcp_servers.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.variables, Grants::default());
    assert!(!reach.spec.browser && !reach.spec.use_user_settings);
    assert_eq!((reach.spec.max_turns, reach.spec.timeout_secs), (50, 2400));
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.policy, Policy::preset(Preset::Sandboxed));
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.schedule, None);
    assert_eq!(reach.spec, reach.without);

    // Naming what it has is no change and asks nothing.
    let w = Wanted {
        browser: Some(true),
        use_user_settings: Some(true),
        max_turns: Some(60),
        timeout_secs: Some(3600),
        permissions: Some(WantedPermissions::Preset(Preset::Trusted)),
        folder: Some(made.spec.workdir.clone()),
        ..Wanted::default()
    };
    let reach = change(&maker, &made, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty(), "{:?}", reach.extras);
    assert_eq!(reach.spec, made.spec);
}

#[test]
fn a_change_above_the_makers_reach_is_an_extra_even_where_the_dot_is_above_it_already() {
    let place = place();
    let maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    let mut made = made_dot(&place);

    // The dot has 60 turns and an hour, both above the maker's 40 and 30 minutes.
    let w = Wanted {
        max_turns: Some(80),
        timeout_secs: Some(7200),
        ..Wanted::default()
    };
    let reach = change(&maker, &made, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(
        reach.extras,
        vec![
            Extra::MaxTurns {
                wanted: 80,
                makers: 40
            },
            Extra::Timeout {
                wanted_secs: 7200,
                makers_secs: 1800
            },
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!((reach.spec.max_turns, reach.spec.timeout_secs), (80, 7200));
    // Without them the dot keeps what the person gave it.
    assert_eq!(
        (reach.without.max_turns, reach.without.timeout_secs),
        (60, 3600)
    );

    // A dot below the maker's is raised to the maker's.
    made.spec.max_turns = 10;
    made.spec.timeout_secs = 600;
    let reach = change(&maker, &made, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(reach.extras.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(
        (reach.without.max_turns, reach.without.timeout_secs),
        (40, 1800)
    );

    // The browser, the user settings and a stronger preset on a dot that lacks them.
    made.spec.browser = false;
    made.spec.use_user_settings = false;
    made.spec.policy = Policy::preset(Preset::ReadOnly);
    let w = Wanted {
        browser: Some(true),
        use_user_settings: Some(true),
        permissions: Some(WantedPermissions::Preset(Preset::Trusted)),
        ..Wanted::default()
    };
    let reach = change(&maker, &made, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(
        reach.extras,
        vec![
            Extra::Preset {
                preset: Preset::Trusted,
                makers: Preset::Sandboxed
            },
            Extra::Browser,
            Extra::UserSettings,
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.policy, Policy::preset(Preset::Trusted));
    assert!(reach.spec.browser && reach.spec.use_user_settings);
    // Without them: the maker's policy, which is within reach and above the dot's read-only.
    assert_eq!(reach.without.policy, maker.spec.policy);
    assert!(!reach.without.browser && !reach.without.use_user_settings);

    // The maker's own policy is always within reach.
    let w = Wanted {
        permissions: Some(WantedPermissions::Maker),
        ..Wanted::default()
    };
    let reach = change(&maker, &made, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.policy, maker.spec.policy);
}

#[test]
fn a_changed_folder_follows_the_folder_rules_and_stays_as_it_was_without_the_extra() {
    let place = place();
    let maker = maker(&place, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    let made = made_dot(&place);

    // Blank is not named: the dot keeps its folder.
    let w = Wanted {
        folder: Some(String::new()),
        ..Wanted::default()
    };
    let reach = change(&maker, &made, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(reach.spec, made.spec);

    // Another folder below the maker's.
    let w = Wanted {
        folder: Some("news".into()),
        ..Wanted::default()
    };
    let reach = change(&maker, &made, &w, &place);
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    let news = place.maker_dir.join("news");
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, text(&news));
    assert_eq!(reach.create_folder, Some(news));
    assert_eq!(reach.spec, reach.without);

    // One outside it.
    let w = Wanted {
        folder: Some(text(&place.outside)),
        ..Wanted::default()
    };
    let reach = change(&maker, &made, &w, &place);
    assert_eq!(
        reach.extras,
        vec![Extra::Folder {
            path: text(&place.outside),
            below_maker: false
        }]
    );
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.workdir, text(&place.outside));
    assert_eq!(reach.without, made.spec);

    // A worktree copy is refused for a change as well.
    let w = Wanted {
        folder: Some(text(&place.worktrees.join("01RUN"))),
        ..Wanted::default()
    };
    assert!(invalid(reach_change(&maker, &made, &w, &place.worktrees)).contains("working copy"));

    // A change must leave a valid dot.
    let w = Wanted {
        name: Some(String::new()),
        ..Wanted::default()
    };
    assert!(invalid(reach_change(&maker, &made, &w, &place.worktrees)).contains("1 to 64"));
}

#[test]
fn each_extra_says_itself_in_one_plain_line() {
    let lines: Vec<String> = [
        item(LibraryKind::Skill, "pdf-tools"),
        item(LibraryKind::McpServer, "github"),
        item(LibraryKind::Plugin, "reviewer"),
        item(LibraryKind::Context, "handbook"),
        item(LibraryKind::App, "blog_board"),
        variable("mcp:github", "GITHUB_TOKEN"),
        variable("shell", "NPM_TOKEN"),
        Extra::Preset {
            preset: Preset::Trusted,
            makers: Preset::Sandboxed,
        },
        Extra::Preset {
            preset: Preset::Sandboxed,
            makers: Preset::Custom,
        },
        Extra::Folder {
            path: r"C:\work\other".into(),
            below_maker: false,
        },
        Extra::Folder {
            path: r"C:\work\repo\docs".into(),
            below_maker: true,
        },
        Extra::Browser,
        Extra::UserSettings,
        Extra::MaxTurns {
            wanted: 80,
            makers: 40,
        },
        Extra::Timeout {
            wanted_secs: 7200,
            makers_secs: 1800,
        },
        Extra::Timeout {
            wanted_secs: 5400,
            makers_secs: 45,
        },
    ]
    .iter()
    .map(|extra| extra.line("Researcher"))
    .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        lines,
        [
            "The skill 'pdf-tools'",
            "The MCP server 'github'",
            "The plugin 'reviewer'",
            "The context collection 'handbook'",
            "The app 'blog_board'",
            "The variable GITHUB_TOKEN for the server 'github'",
            "The variable NPM_TOKEN for the shell",
            "The preset Trusted (Researcher has Sandboxed)",
            "The preset Sandboxed (Researcher has its own rules)",
            r"The folder C:\work\other, outside Researcher's folder",
            r"The folder C:\work\repo\docs, inside Researcher's folder (Researcher itself works in copies of it)",
            "The browser",
            "Your Claude settings",
            "A turn limit of 80 (Researcher has 40)",
            "A time limit of 2 h (Researcher has 30 min)",
            "A time limit of 1 h 30 min (Researcher has 45 s)",
        ]
    );
}

#[test]
fn extras_round_trip_as_json() {
    let extras = vec![
        item(LibraryKind::Skill, "pdf-tools"),
        variable("mcp:github", "GITHUB_TOKEN"),
        Extra::Preset {
            preset: Preset::Trusted,
            makers: Preset::Sandboxed,
        },
        Extra::Folder {
            path: r"C:\work\other".into(),
            below_maker: false,
        },
        Extra::Folder {
            path: r"C:\work\repo\docs".into(),
            below_maker: true,
        },
        Extra::Browser,
        Extra::UserSettings,
        Extra::MaxTurns {
            wanted: 80,
            makers: 40,
        },
        Extra::Timeout {
            wanted_secs: 7200,
            makers_secs: 1800,
        },
    ];
    let json = serde_json::to_value(&extras).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        json,
        serde_json::json!([
            {"kind": "item", "item_kind": "skill", "name": "pdf-tools"},
            {"kind": "variable", "consumer": "mcp:github", "name": "GITHUB_TOKEN"},
            {"kind": "preset", "preset": "trusted", "makers": "sandboxed"},
            {"kind": "folder", "path": r"C:\work\other", "below_maker": false},
            {"kind": "folder", "path": r"C:\work\repo\docs", "below_maker": true},
            {"kind": "browser"},
            {"kind": "user_settings"},
            {"kind": "max_turns", "wanted": 80, "makers": 40},
            {"kind": "timeout", "wanted_secs": 7200, "makers_secs": 1800},
        ])
    );
    let back: Vec<Extra> = serde_json::from_value(json).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(back, extras);
}

#[test]
fn wanted_round_trips_as_json_and_refuses_what_it_does_not_know() {
    let json = serde_json::json!({
        "name": "Blog Watcher",
        "instructions": "Watch three blogs.",
        "model": "haiku",
        "folder": "research/blogs",
        "permissions": "read-only",
        "uses": {"skills": ["pdf-tools"], "mcp_servers": ["github"]},
        "variables": {"mcp:github": ["GITHUB_TOKEN"], "shell": ["NPM_TOKEN"]},
        "browser": false,
        "use_user_settings": false,
        "max_turns": 20,
        "timeout_secs": 900,
        "schedule": {"rule": {"kind": "weekly", "days": ["mon"], "time": "09:00"}},
    });
    let w: Wanted = serde_json::from_value(json.clone()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(w.name.as_deref(), Some("Blog Watcher"));
    assert_eq!(w.folder.as_deref(), Some("research/blogs"));
    assert_eq!(
        w.permissions,
        Some(WantedPermissions::Preset(Preset::ReadOnly))
    );
    assert_eq!(
        w.uses,
        Some(Uses {
            skills: names(&["pdf-tools"]),
            mcp_servers: names(&["github"]),
            ..Uses::default()
        })
    );
    assert_eq!(
        w.variables,
        Some(grants(&[
            ("mcp:github", &["GITHUB_TOKEN"]),
            ("shell", &["NPM_TOKEN"])
        ]))
    );
    assert_eq!((w.browser, w.use_user_settings), (Some(false), Some(false)));
    assert_eq!((w.max_turns, w.timeout_secs), (Some(20), Some(900)));
    assert!(matches!(w.schedule, Some(Some(_))));
    let again: Wanted = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::to_value(&w).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(again, w);

    // The maker's own permissions.
    let w: Wanted = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::json!({"permissions": "maker"})).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(w.permissions, Some(WantedPermissions::Maker));
    assert_eq!(
        serde_json::to_value(&w).unwrap(),
        serde_json::json!({"permissions": "maker"})
    );
    for bad in ["custom", "admin"] {
        let err = serde_json::from_value::<Wanted>(serde_json::json!({"permissions": bad}))
            .unwrap_err()
            .to_string();
        assert!(err.contains("permissions is \"maker\""), "{err}");
    }

    // Nothing named: an empty object, and back.
    assert_eq!(
        serde_json::to_value(Wanted::default()).unwrap(),
        serde_json::json!({})
    );
    assert_eq!(
        serde_json::from_value::<Wanted>(serde_json::json!({})).unwrap(),
        Wanted::default()
    );
    // `null` is not named, for every field.
    let nulls: Wanted = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::json!({
        "name": null, "instructions": null, "model": null, "folder": null,
        "permissions": null, "uses": null, "variables": null, "browser": null,
        "use_user_settings": null, "max_turns": null, "timeout_secs": null, "schedule": null,
    }))
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(nulls, Wanted::default());

    // "No schedule" is the word "none".
    let w: Wanted = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::json!({"schedule": "none"})).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(w.schedule, Some(None));
    let json = serde_json::to_value(&w).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(json, serde_json::json!({"schedule": "none"}));
    assert_eq!(serde_json::from_value::<Wanted>(json).unwrap(), w);
    let err = serde_json::from_value::<Wanted>(serde_json::json!({"schedule": "never"}))
        .unwrap_err()
        .to_string();
    assert!(err.contains("schedule is a schedule or \"none\""), "{err}");
    assert!(serde_json::from_value::<Wanted>(
        serde_json::json!({"schedule": {"rule": {"kind": "x"}}})
    )
    .is_err());

    // A field it does not have is refused: the account, the engine, "Can make dots".
    for field in ["making", "engine", "org_id", "workspace_mode", "enabled"] {
        let err = serde_json::from_value::<Wanted>(serde_json::json!({ (field): true }))
            .unwrap_err()
            .to_string();
        assert!(err.contains("unknown field"), "{err}");
    }
}
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/src/making/reach.rs`:**

```rust
//! The reach check (dots-make-dots design section 6): given a maker as it is now and what it
//! asks for a new dot, or as a change to a dot it made, the whole dot asked for, the parts of
//! it beyond the maker's reach (the extras), and the same dot without them.
//!
//! It compares with the maker's own settings only, and writes nothing: no store, no folder. It
//! reads the file system to resolve real paths. Whether the Library has an item and the vault
//! a variable, the limits (section 10), and that the maker made the dot it changes are the
//! caller's checks.

use std::path::{Component, Path, PathBuf};

use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize, Serializer};

use crate::library::{LibraryKind, Uses};
use crate::model::{Dot, DotSpec, Making, WorkspaceMode};
use crate::policy::{Policy, Preset};
use crate::schedule::Schedule;
use crate::vault::{Consumer, Grants};
use crate::{Error, Result};

/// What `permissions` says for an exact copy of the maker's whole policy.
pub const MAKERS_PERMISSIONS: &str = "maker";
/// What `schedule` says for a dot without a schedule.
pub const NO_SCHEDULE: &str = "none";

/// What a maker asks for (design sections 7.1 and 9). Every field is optional: a new dot needs
/// `name` and `instructions`, and a change changes only the fields it names. In JSON a field
/// that is missing or `null` is not named, and a field this struct does not have is refused.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Wanted {
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub instructions: Option<String>,
    /// A model of the maker's engine; the maker's when a new dot names none.
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub model: Option<String>,
    /// The folder the dot works in: absolute, or relative to the maker's folder. Blank is as
    /// not named: a new dot gets a new folder of its own, a changed dot keeps its folder.
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub folder: Option<String>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub permissions: Option<WantedPermissions>,
    /// The whole set of Library items the dot is to use; none when a new dot names none.
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub uses: Option<Uses>,
    /// The whole set of variables the dot is to be granted, by consumer (`shell` or
    /// `mcp:<server>`); none when a new dot names none.
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub variables: Option<Grants>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub browser: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub use_user_settings: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub max_turns: Option<u32>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub timeout_secs: Option<u64>,
    /// `Some(None)` is no schedule: it clears the schedule of a changed dot. In JSON a
    /// schedule is its object and no schedule is the word `"none"`; `null` is not named, since
    /// a model writes `null` for a field it leaves out.
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none", with = "schedule_or_none")]
    pub schedule: Option<Option<Schedule>>,
}

mod schedule_or_none {
    use super::*;

    pub fn serialize<S: Serializer>(
        value: &Option<Option<Schedule>>,
        s: S,
    ) -> std::result::Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        match value {
            None => s.serialize_none(),
            Some(None) => s.serialize_str(NO_SCHEDULE),
            Some(Some(schedule)) => schedule.serialize(s),
        }
    }

    pub fn deserialize<'de, D: Deserializer<'de>>(
        d: D,
    ) -> std::result::Result<Option<Option<Schedule>>, D::Error> {
        use serde::de::Error as _;
        match serde_json::Value::deserialize(d)? {
            serde_json::Value::Null => Ok(None),
            serde_json::Value::String(word) if word == NO_SCHEDULE => Ok(Some(None)),
            serde_json::Value::String(word) => Err(D::Error::custom(format!(
                "schedule is a schedule or \"{NO_SCHEDULE}\", not {word:?}"
            ))),
            value => serde_json::from_value(value)
                .map(|schedule| Some(Some(schedule)))
                .map_err(D::Error::custom),
        }
    }
}

/// The permissions a maker asks for (design section 6, Permissions). In JSON, `"maker"` or
/// the preset's name: `"read-only"`, `"sandboxed"` or `"trusted"`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WantedPermissions {
    /// An exact copy of the maker's whole policy, as it is at that moment.
    Maker,
    /// A plain preset with no added rules. `Preset::Custom` is no plain preset and is refused.
    Preset(Preset),
}

/// What is said of a `permissions` that is neither the maker's nor a plain preset.
const PERMISSIONS_RULE: &str =
    "permissions is \"maker\", \"read-only\", \"sandboxed\" or \"trusted\"";

impl Serialize for WantedPermissions {
    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, s: S) -> std::result::Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        s.serialize_str(match self {
            Self::Maker => MAKERS_PERMISSIONS,
            Self::Preset(preset) => preset.as_str(),
        })
    }
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for WantedPermissions {
    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(d: D) -> std::result::Result<Self, D::Error> {
        use serde::de::Error as _;
        let word = String::deserialize(d)?;
        if word == MAKERS_PERMISSIONS {
            return Ok(Self::Maker);
        }
        match Preset::parse(&word) {
            Ok(preset) if preset != Preset::Custom => Ok(Self::Preset(preset)),
            _ => Err(D::Error::custom(format!(
                "{PERMISSIONS_RULE}, not {word:?}"
            ))),
        }
    }
}

/// One thing beyond the maker's reach (design section 6). It is stored as JSON with a make
/// request, and says itself in plain words on the ask card (section 7.2).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Extra {
    /// A Library item the maker does not use.
    Item {
        item_kind: LibraryKind,
        name: String,
    },
    /// A variable the maker is not granted for that consumer (`shell` or `mcp:<server>`).
    Variable { consumer: String, name: String },
    /// A plain preset stronger than the maker's (`makers`), or any but read-only when the
    /// maker's is custom.
    Preset { preset: Preset, makers: Preset },
    /// A folder outside the maker's folder, or, with `below_maker`, a folder below the folder
    /// of a maker that works in worktree copies. `path` is the real path.
    Folder {
        path: String,
        #[serde(default)]
        below_maker: bool,
    },
    /// The browser, which the maker does not have.
    Browser,
    /// The person's own Claude settings, which the maker does not use.
    UserSettings,
    /// A turn limit above the maker's.
    MaxTurns { wanted: u32, makers: u32 },
    /// A time limit above the maker's.
    Timeout { wanted_secs: u64, makers_secs: u64 },
}

/// A preset as the person reads it.
fn preset_label(preset: Preset) -> &'static str {
    match preset {
        Preset::ReadOnly => "Read-only",
        Preset::Sandboxed => "Sandboxed",
        Preset::Trusted => "Trusted",
        Preset::Custom => "Custom",
    }
}

/// A time limit as the person reads it: "30 min", "2 h", "1 h 30 min", "45 s".
fn time_label(secs: u64) -> String {
    let (hours, minutes, seconds) = (secs / 3600, secs % 3600 / 60, secs % 60);
    let mut parts = Vec::new();
    if hours > 0 {
        parts.push(format!("{hours} h"));
    }
    if minutes > 0 {
        parts.push(format!("{minutes} min"));
    }
    if seconds > 0 || parts.is_empty() {
        parts.push(format!("{seconds} s"));
    }
    parts.join(" ")
}

impl Extra {
    /// The extra as one line of the ask card (design section 7.2). `maker` is the maker's name.
    pub fn line(&self, maker: &str) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::Item { item_kind, name } => format!("The {} '{name}'", item_kind.label()),
            Self::Variable { consumer, name } => match Consumer::parse(consumer) {
                Ok(Consumer::Mcp(server)) => {
                    format!("The variable {name} for the server '{server}'")
                }
                Ok(Consumer::Shell) => format!("The variable {name} for the shell"),
                Err(_) => format!("The variable {name} for {consumer}"),
            },
            Self::Preset { preset, makers } => match makers {
                Preset::Custom => format!(
                    "The preset {} ({maker} has its own rules)",
                    preset_label(*preset)
                ),
                makers => format!(
                    "The preset {} ({maker} has {})",
                    preset_label(*preset),
                    preset_label(*makers)
                ),
            },
            Self::Folder {
                path,
                below_maker: false,
            } => format!("The folder {path}, outside {maker}'s folder"),
            Self::Folder {
                path,
                below_maker: true,
            } => format!(
                "The folder {path}, inside {maker}'s folder ({maker} itself works in copies of it)"
            ),
            Self::Browser => "The browser".to_string(),
            Self::UserSettings => "Your Claude settings".to_string(),
            Self::MaxTurns { wanted, makers } => {
                format!("A turn limit of {wanted} ({maker} has {makers})")
            }
            Self::Timeout {
                wanted_secs,
                makers_secs,
            } => format!(
                "A time limit of {} ({maker} has {})",
                time_label(*wanted_secs),
                time_label(*makers_secs)
            ),
        }
    }
}

/// What the reach check found.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Reach {
    /// The dot as asked, ready to save if the person allows the extras. A blank `workdir` is a
    /// new dot that gets a new folder of its own when it is created (`DotAdmin::create`).
    pub spec: DotSpec,
    /// The same with the extras removed (design section 7.2, "Make it without these"): the
    /// items and variables dropped, the browser and the user settings off, the permissions
    /// and the limits the maker's, the folder a new one of its own. For a change, a part that
    /// is an extra stays as the dot has it, except that a limit or a plain preset below the
    /// maker's is raised to the maker's.
    pub without: DotSpec,
    /// Empty when everything is within reach; then `spec == without`.
    pub extras: Vec<Extra>,
    /// The folder of `spec` when it lies below the maker's folder and does not exist yet: the
    /// caller creates it before saving `spec` (design section 6, folder rules). `without` needs
    /// it only when the folder is no extra.
    pub create_folder: Option<PathBuf>,
}

/// `path` without Windows' `\\?\` prefix, which `std::fs::canonicalize` adds and which git and
/// the `claude` CLI do not take. A UNC path keeps it.
fn plain(path: PathBuf) -> PathBuf {
    let text = path.to_string_lossy();
    match text.strip_prefix(r"\\?\") {
        Some(rest) if !rest.starts_with("UNC") => PathBuf::from(rest),
        _ => path,
    }
}

/// The real path of the absolute `path` (design section 6: case, `..`, links and junctions):
/// each part that exists is resolved as the file system has it, and the parts after the last
/// one that exists are kept as given, so a folder that is still to be made has a real path
/// too. A `..` leaves the real folder it follows.
pub fn real_path(path: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    let mut out = PathBuf::new();
    for part in path.components() {
        match part {
            Component::CurDir => {}
            Component::ParentDir => {
                out.pop();
            }
            Component::Normal(_) => {
                out.push(part);
                if let Ok(real) = std::fs::canonicalize(&out) {
                    out = real;
                }
            }
            // A drive alone would resolve to the current folder on it.
            Component::Prefix(_) | Component::RootDir => out.push(part),
        }
    }
    plain(out)
}

/// A real path as it is compared: Windows paths ignore case, and a part that does not exist
/// yet keeps the case it was given in.
fn folded(path: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    if cfg!(windows) {
        PathBuf::from(path.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase())
    } else {
        path.to_path_buf()
    }
}

/// Where a named folder puts the dot (design section 6, folder rules).
struct Placed {
    /// Its real path.
    real: PathBuf,
    /// The dot's `workdir`: the maker's own as the maker has it, else the real path.
    workdir: String,
    mode: WorkspaceMode,
    /// Set when the folder is beyond the maker's reach.
    extra: Option<Extra>,
    /// Set when it lies below the maker's folder and does not exist yet.
    create: Option<PathBuf>,
}

/// Applies the folder rules to `given`, a folder that is not blank: absolute, or relative to
/// the maker's folder.
fn place(maker: &Dot, given: &str, worktrees_root: &Path) -> Result<Placed> {
    let makers = real_path(Path::new(maker.spec.workdir.trim()));
    let real = real_path(&makers.join(given));
    let (key, makers_key) = (folded(&real), folded(&makers));
    // A worktree copy goes when its run is discarded or merged, so no card can allow it.
    if !worktrees_root.as_os_str().is_empty() && key.starts_with(folded(&real_path(worktrees_root)))
    {
        return Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
            "That folder is a run's working copy, which does not last. Leave the folder blank \
             for a new one, or use {}'s own folder.",
            maker.spec.name
        )));
    }
    if key == makers_key {
        // The maker's mode too, so a made dot of a worktree maker works in worktree copies.
        return Ok(Placed {
            real,
            workdir: maker.spec.workdir.clone(),
            mode: maker.spec.workspace_mode,
            extra: None,
            create: None,
        });
    }
    // The nearest part of it that exists must be a folder.
    let mut nearest = real.as_path();
    while !nearest.exists() {
        match nearest.parent() {
            Some(parent) => nearest = parent,
            None => break,
        }
    }
    if nearest.is_file() {
        return Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
            "{} is a file, not a folder.",
            nearest.display()
        )));
    }
    let missing = !real.is_dir();
    let workdir = real.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    if key.starts_with(&makers_key) {
        // A worktree maker only ever writes in worktree copies; a dot in a subfolder would
        // write straight into the person's checkout, which is more than the maker can do.
        let extra = (maker.spec.workspace_mode == WorkspaceMode::Worktree).then(|| Extra::Folder {
            path: workdir.clone(),
            below_maker: true,
        });
        return Ok(Placed {
            create: missing.then(|| real.clone()),
            real,
            workdir,
            mode: WorkspaceMode::Folder,
            extra,
        });
    }
    if missing {
        return Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
            "The folder {workdir} does not exist. Leave the folder blank for a new one, or name \
             one that exists."
        )));
    }
    Ok(Placed {
        real,
        extra: Some(Extra::Folder {
            path: workdir.clone(),
            below_maker: false,
        }),
        workdir,
        mode: WorkspaceMode::Folder,
        create: None,
    })
}

/// A plain preset's place in the order read-only, sandboxed, trusted (design section 6).
/// `None` for custom, which has no place in it.
fn rank(preset: Preset) -> Option<u8> {
    match preset {
        Preset::ReadOnly => Some(0),
        Preset::Sandboxed => Some(1),
        Preset::Trusted => Some(2),
        Preset::Custom => None,
    }
}

/// The list of `uses` that names items of `kind`.
fn names_mut(uses: &mut Uses, kind: LibraryKind) -> &mut Vec<String> {
    match kind {
        LibraryKind::McpServer => &mut uses.mcp_servers,
        LibraryKind::Skill => &mut uses.skills,
        LibraryKind::Plugin => &mut uses.plugins,
        LibraryKind::Context => &mut uses.context,
        LibraryKind::App => &mut uses.apps,
    }
}

/// Whether `grants` gives `consumer` (a key of `Grants`) the variable `name`, in any case.
fn grants(grants: &Grants, consumer: &str, name: &str) -> bool {
    grants
        .0
        .get(consumer)
        .is_some_and(|names| names.iter().any(|n| n.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name)))
}

/// `DotSpec::validate`, for a dot whose blank folder is filled when it is created.
fn validate(spec: &DotSpec) -> Result<()> {
    if !spec.workdir.trim().is_empty() {
        return spec.validate();
    }
    let mut filled = spec.clone();
    filled.workdir = ".".to_string();
    filled.validate()
}

/// Puts what `wanted` names on `base`, the dot before it: a new dot with nothing asked, or the
/// made dot as it is. A named part is within reach when the maker has it, or `base` has it
/// already.
fn check(maker: &Dot, base: &DotSpec, wanted: &Wanted, worktrees_root: &Path) -> Result<Reach> {
    let m = &maker.spec;
    let mut spec = base.clone();
    let mut without = base.clone();
    let mut extras = Vec::new();
    let mut create_folder = None;

    // The maker's to write, or not part of reach.
    if let Some(name) = &wanted.name {
        spec.name = name.clone();
        without.name = name.clone();
    }
    if let Some(instructions) = &wanted.instructions {
        spec.instructions = instructions.clone();
        without.instructions = instructions.clone();
    }
    if let Some(model) = &wanted.model {
        spec.model = model.clone();
        without.model = model.clone();
    }
    if let Some(schedule) = &wanted.schedule {
        spec.schedule = schedule.clone();
        without.schedule = schedule.clone();
    }

    if let Some(uses) = &wanted.uses {
        let mut within = Uses::default();
        for kind in LibraryKind::ALL {
            for name in uses.names(*kind) {
                if m.uses.names(*kind).contains(name) || base.uses.names(*kind).contains(name) {
                    names_mut(&mut within, *kind).push(name.clone());
                } else {
                    extras.push(Extra::Item {
                        item_kind: *kind,
                        name: name.clone(),
                    });
                }
            }
        }
        spec.uses = uses.clone();
        without.uses = within;
    }

    if let Some(variables) = &wanted.variables {
        let (mut asked, mut within) = (Grants::default(), Grants::default());
        for (consumer, names) in &variables.0 {
            // A consumer with no name is granted nothing.
            if names.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            asked.0.insert(consumer.clone(), names.clone());
            let mut kept = Vec::new();
            for name in names {
                if grants(&m.variables, consumer, name) || grants(&base.variables, consumer, name) {
                    kept.push(name.clone());
                } else {
                    extras.push(Extra::Variable {
                        consumer: consumer.clone(),
                        name: name.clone(),
                    });
                }
            }
            if !kept.is_empty() {
                within.0.insert(consumer.clone(), kept);
            }
        }
        spec.variables = asked;
        without.variables = within;
    }

    match wanted.permissions {
        None => {}
        Some(WantedPermissions::Maker) => {
            spec.policy = m.policy.clone();
            without.policy = m.policy.clone();
        }
        Some(WantedPermissions::Preset(preset)) => {
            let Some(asked) = rank(preset) else {
                return Err(Error::Invalid(format!("{PERMISSIONS_RULE}.")));
            };
            let no_stronger_than = |has: Preset| rank(has).is_some_and(|has| asked <= has);
            // `Policy::preset` carries the allow rules of Dots' own tools.
            spec.policy = Policy::preset(preset);
            // Read-only is the weakest there is, so a custom maker may give it too.
            if asked == 0
                || no_stronger_than(m.policy.preset)
                || no_stronger_than(base.policy.preset)
            {
                without.policy = spec.policy.clone();
            } else {
                extras.push(Extra::Preset {
                    preset,
                    makers: m.policy.preset,
                });
                // Lowered to the maker's own policy, unless that would take from a dot that
                // has more already, or the two cannot be ordered.
                if let (Some(makers), Some(has)) = (rank(m.policy.preset), rank(base.policy.preset))
                {
                    if makers > has {
                        without.policy = m.policy.clone();
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    let folder = wanted.folder.as_deref().map(str::trim).unwrap_or_default();
    if !folder.is_empty() {
        let placed = place(maker, folder, worktrees_root)?;
        let has = base.workdir.trim();
        let same = !has.is_empty() && folded(&real_path(Path::new(has))) == folded(&placed.real);
        // The folder the dot has already stays as it is, mode included.
        if !same {
            spec.workdir = placed.workdir;
            spec.workspace_mode = placed.mode;
            create_folder = placed.create;
            match placed.extra {
                Some(extra) => extras.push(extra),
                None => {
                    without.workdir = spec.workdir.clone();
                    without.workspace_mode = spec.workspace_mode;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if let Some(on) = wanted.browser {
        spec.browser = on;
        if on && !m.browser && !base.browser {
            extras.push(Extra::Browser);
        } else {
            without.browser = on;
        }
    }
    if let Some(on) = wanted.use_user_settings {
        spec.use_user_settings = on;
        if on && !m.use_user_settings && !base.use_user_settings {
            extras.push(Extra::UserSettings);
        } else {
            without.use_user_settings = on;
        }
    }

    if let Some(turns) = wanted.max_turns {
        let reach = m.max_turns.max(base.max_turns);
        spec.max_turns = turns;
        without.max_turns = turns.min(reach);
        if turns > reach {
            extras.push(Extra::MaxTurns {
                wanted: turns,
                makers: m.max_turns,
            });
        }
    }
    if let Some(secs) = wanted.timeout_secs {
        let reach = m.timeout_secs.max(base.timeout_secs);
        spec.timeout_secs = secs;
        without.timeout_secs = secs.min(reach);
        if secs > reach {
            extras.push(Extra::Timeout {
                wanted_secs: secs,
                makers_secs: m.timeout_secs,
            });
        }
    }

    validate(&spec)?;
    validate(&without)?;
    Ok(Reach {
        spec,
        without,
        extras,
        create_folder,
    })
}

/// For a new dot (design sections 6 and 7.1). `worktrees_root` is where runs' worktree copies
/// are made (`RunnerConfig::worktrees_dir`): the maker's settings do not say.
///
/// Asked nothing but a name and instructions, the dot has the maker's engine, endpoint, model,
/// policy and limits and the settings the table says are copied; a new folder of its own; no
/// Library item, no variable, no browser, no user settings and no schedule; "Can make dots"
/// off and no spending cap of its own; and it is enabled. Its account and workspace are the
/// maker's, which the caller passes on.
///
/// `Error::Invalid` with a plain sentence, for what no card can allow: no name or no
/// instructions, a folder inside a run's worktree copy, a folder outside the maker's that does
/// not exist, and a dot that is not valid (`DotSpec::validate`).
pub fn reach_new(maker: &Dot, wanted: &Wanted, worktrees_root: &Path) -> Result<Reach> {
    let named = |text: &Option<String>| text.as_deref().is_some_and(|t| !t.trim().is_empty());
    if !named(&wanted.name) {
        return Err(Error::Invalid("A new dot needs a name.".into()));
    }
    if !named(&wanted.instructions) {
        return Err(Error::Invalid("A new dot needs instructions.".into()));
    }
    let m = &maker.spec;
    let base = DotSpec {
        name: String::new(),
        instructions: String::new(),
        engine: m.engine,
        model: m.model.clone(),
        endpoint_url: m.endpoint_url.clone(),
        // Blank: `DotAdmin::create` makes a new folder, in folder mode.
        workdir: String::new(),
        workspace_mode: WorkspaceMode::Folder,
        schedule: None,
        policy: m.policy.clone(),
        uses: Uses::default(),
        variables: Grants::default(),
        browser: false,
        quiet_limit_secs: m.quiet_limit_secs,
        spend_cap: crate::spend::DotCaps::default(),
        use_global_instructions: m.use_global_instructions,
        check_results: m.check_results,
        use_graph: m.use_graph,
        context_rules: m.context_rules,
        making: Making::default(),
        use_user_settings: false,
        max_turns: m.max_turns,
        timeout_secs: m.timeout_secs,
        approval_wait_secs: m.approval_wait_secs,
        enabled: true,
    };
    check(maker, &base, wanted, worktrees_root)
}

/// For a change to `made`, a dot the maker made (design section 9). Only the fields `wanted`
/// names change; the rest stays, including what the person edited and the extras they allowed.
/// Only the named fields are checked, against the maker's reach now, and nothing the dot holds
/// already is an extra again: an item or a variable it has, its folder, the browser, a limit no
/// higher and a plain preset no stronger than its own. So removing and lowering never ask.
///
/// That the maker made `made` is the caller's check. Errors as `reach_new`, without the need
/// for a name and instructions.
pub fn reach_change(
    maker: &Dot,
    made: &Dot,
    wanted: &Wanted,
    worktrees_root: &Path,
) -> Result<Reach> {
    check(maker, &made.spec, wanted, worktrees_root)
}
```
