```rust
//! A maker's run makes a dot (dots-make-dots design sections 5, 7.1 and 10): a dot within the
//! maker's reach and within its limits is created at once, with who made it recorded and a
//! "made" entry in the makers' log; one beyond reach or over a limit creates nothing and comes
//! back for the person; and what could never be allowed is a plain error.

mod common;

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Arc;

use common::spec;
use dots_core::events::RuntimeEvent;
use dots_core::library::{LibraryConfig, McpServerConfig, Uses};
use dots_core::making::log::{MakingEvent, MakingEventKind};
use dots_core::making::reach::{real_path, Extra, Wanted};
use dots_core::making::service::{MakeDot, MakeOutcome, OverLimit};
use dots_core::model::{Dot, DotSpec, Making, NewRun, Run, RunStatus, TriggerKind, WorkspaceMode};
use dots_core::schedule::Schedule;
use dots_core::vault::{EntryKind, Grants, MemorySecrets};
use dots_core::{Config, Error, Runtime};
use serde_json::json;
use sqlx::sqlite::SqliteConnectOptions;
use sqlx::ConnectOptions;
use tempfile::TempDir;
use tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver;

struct T {
    dir: TempDir,
    /// Where a dot made without a folder gets one (`Config::new_dot_root`).
    root: PathBuf,
    rt: Runtime,
}

impl T {
    /// The maker's folder.
    fn work(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.dir.path().join("work")
    }
}

async fn start() -> T {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let mut cfg = Config::new(dir.path().join("data"));
    cfg.port = 0;
    cfg.claude_path = Some(PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake-claude")));
    cfg.new_dot_root = dir.path().join("Dots");
    cfg.secrets = Some(Arc::new(MemorySecrets::new()));
    // No queued run starts: the tests put a run in the running state by hand.
    cfg.max_concurrent_runs = 0;
    let root = cfg.new_dot_root.clone();
    let rt = Runtime::start(cfg).await.unwrap();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path().join("work")).unwrap();
    T { dir, root, rt }
}

/// The spec of a dot named Researcher that works in the test's `work` folder itself and may
/// make dots.
fn maker_spec(t: &T) -> DotSpec {
    let mut s = spec("Researcher");
    s.workdir = t.work().to_string_lossy().to_string();
    s.workspace_mode = WorkspaceMode::Folder;
    s.making.on = true;
    s
}

/// A maker named Researcher, created as the person creates a dot.
async fn maker(t: &T) -> Dot {
    t.rt.create_dot(maker_spec(t), None, None).await.unwrap()
}

/// A maker whose settings allow `per_run` dots in one run and `total` kept.
async fn maker_with(t: &T, per_run: u32, total: u32) -> Dot {
    let mut s = maker_spec(t);
    s.making = Making {
        on: true,
        per_run,
        total,
    };
    t.rt.create_dot(s, None, None).await.unwrap()
}

/// A run of `dot` that is running: a chat the person started with a typed message.
async fn live_run(t: &T, dot: &Dot) -> Run {
    let mut new = NewRun::new(&dot.id, TriggerKind::Chat);
    new.payload = Some(json!({"message": "watch three blogs", "typed": true}));
    let run = t.rt.store().create_run(&new).await.unwrap();
    assert!(t.rt.store().claim_run(&run.id).await.unwrap());
    t.rt.store().get_run(&run.id).await.unwrap()
}

/// What a maker asks for a dot named `name`, with nothing but what a new dot needs.
fn ask(name: &str) -> MakeDot {
    MakeDot {
        purpose: "Reads the feeds".into(),
        wanted: Wanted {
            name: Some(name.into()),
            instructions: Some("Read the three blogs and list what is new.".into()),
            ..Wanted::default()
        },
        first_job: None,
    }
}

/// Makes the dot, which must be within reach and within the limits.
async fn make(t: &T, run: &Run, name: &str) -> Dot {
    match t.rt.makers().make_dot(&run.id, ask(name)).await.unwrap() {
        MakeOutcome::Made { dot } => dot,
        other => panic!("{name} was not made: {other:?}"),
    }
}

/// The text of the refusal of `ask`.
async fn refused(t: &T, run: &Run, ask: MakeDot) -> String {
    match t.rt.makers().make_dot(&run.id, ask).await {
        Err(Error::Invalid(text) | Error::Conflict(text)) => text,
        other => panic!("expected a plain refusal, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

/// Every `minutes`, as a tool call carries it. The first slot is hours away, so nothing fires
/// during a test.
fn every(minutes: u32) -> Schedule {
    serde_json::from_value(json!({
        "rule": {"kind": "every", "minutes": minutes},
        "catch_up": true,
        "until": null
    }))
    .unwrap()
}

/// The topics named by the `MakingUpdated` events published since the last call, each with
/// the maker it names.
fn updated(rx: &mut Receiver<RuntimeEvent>) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let mut seen = Vec::new();
    while let Ok(ev) = rx.try_recv() {
        if let RuntimeEvent::MakingUpdated {
            dot_id,
            root_run_id,
        } = ev
        {
            seen.push((dot_id, root_run_id));
        }
    }
    seen
}

/// The makers' log of the topic `run` belongs to.
async fn log(t: &T, run: &Run) -> Vec<MakingEvent> {
    t.rt.store()
        .list_making_events(&run.root_run_id)
        .await
        .unwrap()
}

/// The names of the folders in `root`.
fn folders(root: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
    let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(root) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let mut names: Vec<String> = entries
        .map(|e| e.unwrap().file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .collect();
    names.sort();
    names
}

/// The names of all dots, sorted.
async fn dot_names(t: &T) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut names: Vec<String> =
        t.rt.store()
            .list_dots()
            .await
            .unwrap()
            .into_iter()
            .map(|d| d.spec.name)
            .collect();
    names.sort();
    names
}

/// Puts an MCP server named `github` in the Library whose config reads `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and the
/// variable in the Personal vault.
async fn add_github(t: &T) {
    let config = LibraryConfig::McpServer(McpServerConfig::Stdio {
        command: "node".into(),
        args: Vec::new(),
        cwd: None,
        env: [("TOKEN".to_string(), "${GITHUB_TOKEN}".to_string())].into(),
    });
    t.rt.store()
        .add_library_item("github", &config, None)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    t.rt.vault()
        .add("GITHUB_TOKEN", EntryKind::Plain, "t0ken")
        .await
        .unwrap();
}

fn uses_github() -> Uses {
    Uses {
        mcp_servers: vec!["github".into()],
        ..Uses::default()
    }
}

fn grants(consumer: &str, name: &str) -> Grants {
    Grants([(consumer.to_string(), vec![name.to_string()])].into())
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_dot_within_reach_is_made_at_once() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    let mut rx = t.rt.subscribe();
    let outcome =
        t.rt.makers()
            .make_dot(&run.id, ask("Blog Watcher"))
            .await
            .unwrap();
    let MakeOutcome::Made { dot } = outcome else {
        panic!("not made: {outcome:?}");
    };
    // It exists, on, and may not itself make dots.
    assert_eq!(t.rt.store().get_dot(&dot.id).await.unwrap(), dot);
    assert_eq!(dot.spec.name, "Blog Watcher");
    assert!(dot.spec.enabled);
    assert_eq!(dot.spec.making, Making::default());
    assert!(!dot.spec.making.on);
    // Who made it, in which run, and what for.
    let made = dot.made.clone().expect("a made dot");
    assert_eq!(made.by_dot_id.as_deref(), Some(maker.id.as_str()));
    assert_eq!(made.by_name, "Researcher");
    assert_eq!(made.run_id, run.id);
    assert_eq!(made.purpose, "Reads the feeds");
    // The maker's account and workspace, and a new folder of its own.
    assert_eq!(dot.org_id, maker.org_id);
    assert_eq!(dot.workspace_id, maker.workspace_id);
    assert_eq!(folders(&t.root), ["blog-watcher"]);
    assert!(Path::new(&dot.spec.workdir).is_dir());
    assert_eq!(dot.spec.workspace_mode, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    // The topic's log has the card's entry.
    let events = log(&t, &run).await;
    assert_eq!(events.len(), 1);
    let event = &events[0];
    assert_eq!(event.kind, MakingEventKind::Made);
    assert_eq!(event.maker_dot_id, maker.id);
    assert_eq!(event.run_id, run.id);
    assert_eq!(event.root_run_id, run.root_run_id);
    assert_eq!(event.dot_id.as_deref(), Some(dot.id.as_str()));
    assert_eq!(event.dot_name, "Blog Watcher");
    assert_eq!(event.detail, json!({"purpose": "Reads the feeds"}));
    assert_eq!(
        updated(&mut rx),
        [(maker.id.clone(), run.root_run_id.clone())]
    );
    assert_eq!(t.rt.store().count_made_in_run(&run.id).await.unwrap(), 1);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_run_that_continues_a_topic_logs_under_the_topic() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let first = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    make(&t, &first, "One").await;
    t.rt.store()
        .finish_run(&first.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, None, None)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let mut new = NewRun::new(&maker.id, TriggerKind::Chat);
    new.parent_run_id = Some(first.id.clone());
    new.root_run_id = Some(first.id.clone());
    let next = t.rt.store().create_run(&new).await.unwrap();
    assert!(t.rt.store().claim_run(&next.id).await.unwrap());
    make(&t, &next, "Two").await;
    // Oldest first, both under the topic's first run.
    let events = log(&t, &first).await;
    let names: Vec<&str> = events.iter().map(|e| e.dot_name.as_str()).collect();
    assert_eq!(names, ["One", "Two"]);
    assert_eq!(events[1].run_id, next.id);
    assert_eq!(events[1].root_run_id, first.id);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_subfolder_made_for_a_dot_that_is_not_created_is_removed() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    // The path the person's answer takes creates from a checked spec. Here the name was taken
    // in between, so the store refuses it after the folder was made.
    make(&t, &run, "Taken").await;
    let reach = dots_core::making::reach::reach_new(
        &maker,
        &Wanted {
            folder: Some("notes/blogs".into()),
            ..ask("taken").wanted
        },
        Path::new(""),
    )
    .unwrap();
    let err =
        t.rt.makers()
            .create_made(
                &maker,
                &run.id,
                &run.root_run_id,
                reach.spec,
                "Reads the feeds",
                reach.create_folder,
            )
            .await
            .unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(err, Error::Conflict(_)), "{err:?}");
    assert!(!t.work().join("notes").exists());
    assert_eq!(log(&t, &run).await.len(), 1);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_workflow_step_run_is_refused() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    // Named a step without building a workflow: the step row itself does not matter here.
    let mut conn = SqliteConnectOptions::new()
        .filename(t.dir.path().join("data").join("dots.db"))
        .foreign_keys(false)
        .connect()
        .await
        .unwrap();
    sqlx::query("UPDATE runs SET workflow_step_run_id = 'STEP' WHERE id = ?")
        .bind(&run.id)
        .execute(&mut conn)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    drop(conn);
    assert_eq!(
        refused(&t, &run, ask("Blog Watcher")).await,
        "A run that is a workflow step cannot make dots."
    );
    assert_eq!(dot_names(&t).await, ["Researcher"]);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_finished_run_is_refused() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    t.rt.store()
        .finish_run(&run.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, None, None)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        refused(&t, &run, ask("Blog Watcher")).await,
        "This run has ended, so it cannot make a dot."
    );
    // A run that does not exist is no run of a maker either.
    let err =
        t.rt.makers()
            .make_dot("no-such-run", ask("Blog Watcher"))
            .await
            .unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(err, Error::NotFound(_)), "{err:?}");
    assert_eq!(dot_names(&t).await, ["Researcher"]);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_dot_that_is_not_valid_is_a_plain_error() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    let mut nameless = ask("x");
    nameless.wanted.name = None;
    assert_eq!(refused(&t, &run, nameless).await, "A new dot needs a name.");
    for purpose in [
        "".to_string(),
        "  ".to_string(),
        "x".repeat(201),
        "one\ntwo".to_string(),
    ] {
        let mut asked = ask("Blog Watcher");
        asked.purpose = purpose;
        assert_eq!(
            refused(&t, &run, asked).await,
            "The purpose is one line of 1 to 200 characters."
        );
    }
    for job in ["".to_string(), " ".to_string(), "x".repeat(4001)] {
        let mut asked = ask("Blog Watcher");
        asked.first_job = Some(job);
        assert_eq!(
            refused(&t, &run, asked).await,
            "The first job is 1 to 4000 characters."
        );
    }
    // The longest of each is taken, and the purpose is kept without the spaces around it.
    let mut asked = ask("Blog Watcher");
    asked.purpose = format!(" {} ", "p".repeat(200));
    asked.first_job = Some("j".repeat(4000));
    let outcome = t.rt.makers().make_dot(&run.id, asked).await.unwrap();
    let MakeOutcome::Made { dot } = outcome else {
        panic!("not made: {outcome:?}");
    };
    assert_eq!(dot.made.unwrap().purpose, "p".repeat(200));
}

    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    make(&t, &run, "Blog Watcher").await;
    for name in ["Blog Watcher", "blog watcher", "Researcher"] {
        let err =
            t.rt.makers()
                .make_dot(&run.id, ask(name))
                .await
                .unwrap_err();
        match err {
            Error::Conflict(text) => assert_eq!(
                text,
                format!("A dot named {name:?} already exists. Choose another name.")
            ),
            other => panic!("{other:?}"),
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(dot_names(&t).await, ["Blog Watcher", "Researcher"]);
    assert_eq!(folders(&t.root), ["blog-watcher"]);
}

#[tokio::test]

    let mut asked = ask("Blog Watcher");
    asked.wanted.uses = Some(uses_github());
    // The maker does not use it either, so it would be an extra; but no card could allow it.
    assert_eq!(
        refused(&t, &run, asked).await,
        "the Library has no MCP server named \"github\""

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_variable_or_consumer_that_does_not_exist_is_a_plain_error() {
    let t = start().await;
    add_github(&t).await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    // No such variable in the maker's account.
    let mut asked = ask("Blog Watcher");
    asked.wanted.variables = Some(grants("shell", "NO_SUCH_KEY"));
    assert_eq!(
        refused(&t, &run, asked).await,
        "There is no variable named NO_SUCH_KEY. Name one that exists, or leave it out and \
         tell the person it is missing."
    );
    // A server the Library does not have, and one the dot would not use.
    for server in ["ghost", "github"] {
        let mut asked = ask("Blog Watcher");
        asked.wanted.variables = Some(grants(&format!("mcp:{server}"), "GITHUB_TOKEN"));
        assert_eq!(
            refused(&t, &run, asked).await,
            format!(
                "The dot would not use an MCP server named '{server}', so it cannot be given \
                 variables for it. Name the server in uses, or leave those variables out."
            )
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(dot_names(&t).await, ["Researcher"]);
    // A variable that exists, beyond the maker's reach, is for the person to decide.
    let mut asked = ask("Blog Watcher");
    asked.wanted.variables = Some(grants("shell", "GITHUB_TOKEN"));
    let outcome = t.rt.makers().make_dot(&run.id, asked).await.unwrap();
    let MakeOutcome::NeedsPerson { reach, over } = outcome else {
        panic!("made: {outcome:?}");
    };
    assert_eq!(over, None);
    assert_eq!(
        reach.extras,
        [Extra::Variable {
            consumer: "shell".into(),
            name: "GITHUB_TOKEN".into()
        }]
    );
}

    assert!(updated(&mut rx).is_empty());
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_fourth_dot_of_a_run_needs_the_person() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker_with(&t, 3, 10).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    for name in ["One", "Two", "Three"] {
        make(&t, &run, name).await;
    }
    let outcome = t.rt.makers().make_dot(&run.id, ask("Four")).await.unwrap();
    let MakeOutcome::NeedsPerson { reach, over } = outcome else {
        panic!("made: {outcome:?}");
    };
    assert_eq!(over, Some(OverLimit::PerRun { nth: 4, limit: 3 }));
    // Nothing of it is beyond reach: only the limit is passed.
    assert!(reach.extras.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(reach.spec.name, "Four");
    assert_eq!(dot_names(&t).await, ["One", "Researcher", "Three", "Two"]);
    assert_eq!(folders(&t.root), ["one", "three", "two"]);
    assert_eq!(log(&t, &run).await.len(), 3);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn deleting_a_made_dot_does_not_give_the_run_a_place_back() {
    let t = start().await;

    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    make(&t, &run, "One").await;
    make(&t, &run, "Two").await;
    let three = make(&t, &run, "Three").await;
    t.rt.delete_dot(&three.id).await.unwrap();
    // Two exist now, of three it may keep; but this run made three.
    let outcome = t.rt.makers().make_dot(&run.id, ask("Four")).await.unwrap();
    let MakeOutcome::NeedsPerson { over, .. } = outcome else {
        panic!("made: {outcome:?}");
    };
    assert_eq!(over, Some(OverLimit::PerRun { nth: 4, limit: 3 }));
    // The entry of the deleted dot stays in the log, without the dot.
    let events = log(&t, &run).await;
    assert_eq!(events.len(), 3);
    assert_eq!(events[2].dot_name, "Three");
    assert_eq!(events[2].dot_id, None);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_made_dot_never_can_make_dots() {
    // The ask cannot even name the switch: a field `Wanted` does not have is refused.
    for field in ["making", "can_make_dots", "enabled", "org_id", "engine"] {
        let mut call = json!({
            "name": "Blog Watcher",
            "instructions": "Read the blogs.",
            "purpose": "Reads the feeds",
        });
        call[field] = json!(true);
        let err = serde_json::from_value::<MakeDot>(call).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.to_string().contains(field), "{field}: {err}");
    }
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    let dot = make(&t, &run, "Blog Watcher").await;
    assert!(!dot.spec.making.on);
    // Nor does a spec that says otherwise get through the path the person's answer takes.
    let mut spec = dot.spec.clone();
    spec.name = "Second".into();
    spec.workdir = String::new();
    spec.making.on = true;
    spec.enabled = false;
    let second =
        t.rt.makers()
            .create_made(&maker, &run.id, &run.root_run_id, spec, "Another", None)
            .await
            .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(second.spec.making, Making::default());
    assert!(second.spec.enabled);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_made_dots_grants_are_exactly_what_was_asked() {
    let t = start().await;
    add_github(&t).await;
    // The person's dot is granted the variable its server reads.
    let mut s = maker_spec(&t);
    s.uses = uses_github();
    let maker = t.rt.create_dot(s, None, None).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(maker.spec.variables, grants("mcp:github", "GITHUB_TOKEN"));
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    // The made dot uses the server and names no variables: it holds none.
    let mut asked = ask("Plain");
    asked.wanted.uses = Some(uses_github());
    let outcome = t.rt.makers().make_dot(&run.id, asked).await.unwrap();
    let MakeOutcome::Made { dot } = outcome else {
        panic!("not made: {outcome:?}");
    };
    assert_eq!(dot.spec.uses, uses_github());
    assert_eq!(dot.spec.variables, Grants::default());
    // Named, it holds exactly that.
    let mut asked = ask("Granted");
    asked.wanted.uses = Some(uses_github());
    asked.wanted.variables = Some(grants("mcp:github", "GITHUB_TOKEN"));
    let outcome = t.rt.makers().make_dot(&run.id, asked).await.unwrap();
    let MakeOutcome::Made { dot } = outcome else {
        panic!("not made: {outcome:?}");
    };
    assert_eq!(dot.spec.variables, grants("mcp:github", "GITHUB_TOKEN"));
}

#[test]
fn a_tool_calls_json_reads_as_an_ask() {
    let call = json!({
        "name": "Blog Watcher",
        "instructions": "Read the three blogs and list what is new.",
        "purpose": "Watches three blogs for new posts",
        "folder": "blogs",
        "permissions": "read-only",
        "uses": {"mcp_servers": ["fetch"]},
        "variables": {"mcp:fetch": ["FETCH_KEY"]},
        "max_turns": 20,
        "schedule": {"rule": {"kind": "every", "minutes": 60}, "catch_up": true, "until": null},
        "first_job": "Read them now and tell me what is new."
    });
    let asked: MakeDot = serde_json::from_value(call.clone()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(asked.purpose, "Watches three blogs for new posts");
    assert_eq!(
        asked.first_job.as_deref(),
        Some("Read them now and tell me what is new.")
    );
    assert_eq!(asked.wanted.name.as_deref(), Some("Blog Watcher"));
    assert_eq!(asked.wanted.folder.as_deref(), Some("blogs"));
    assert_eq!(asked.wanted.max_turns, Some(20));
    assert_eq!(
        asked.wanted.variables,
        Some(grants("mcp:fetch", "FETCH_KEY"))
    );
    assert!(matches!(asked.wanted.schedule, Some(Some(_))));
    // It is written as it is read: one flat object.
    let written = serde_json::to_value(&asked).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(written["name"], "Blog Watcher");
    assert_eq!(written["purpose"], "Watches three blogs for new posts");
    assert_eq!(written["permissions"], "read-only");
    assert_eq!(serde_json::from_value::<MakeDot>(written).unwrap(), asked);
    // The least a call carries; a model writes `null` for what it leaves out.
    let least: MakeDot = serde_json::from_value(json!({
        "name": "Blog Watcher",
        "instructions": "Read the blogs.",
        "purpose": "Reads the feeds",
        "first_job": null,
        "folder": null
    }))
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(least.first_job, None);
    assert_eq!(least.wanted.folder, None);
    // The purpose is needed, and is text.
    for purpose in [json!(null), json!(7)] {
        let mut call = call.clone();
        call["purpose"] = purpose;
        let err = serde_json::from_value::<MakeDot>(call).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("purpose"), "{err}");
    }
    let mut call = call.clone();
    call.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("purpose");
    let err = serde_json::from_value::<MakeDot>(call).unwrap_err();
    assert!(err.to_string().contains("purpose"), "{err}");
    assert!(serde_json::from_value::<MakeDot>(json!(["Blog Watcher"])).is_err());
}

#[test]
fn a_passed_limit_says_itself_in_one_line() {
    assert_eq!(
        OverLimit::PerRun { nth: 4, limit: 3 }.line(),
        "4th dot in this run; the limit is 3"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        OverLimit::Total { nth: 11, limit: 10 }.line(),
        "11th made dot kept; the limit is 10"
    );
    let nth = |nth| OverLimit::PerRun { nth, limit: 1 }.line();
    assert!(nth(2).starts_with("2nd dot"));
    assert!(nth(3).starts_with("3rd dot"));
    assert!(nth(12).starts_with("12th dot"));
    assert!(nth(21).starts_with("21st dot"));
    // As it is stored with a make request.
    assert_eq!(
        serde_json::to_value(OverLimit::PerRun { nth: 4, limit: 3 }).unwrap(),
        json!({"limit": "per_run", "nth": 4, "max": 3})
    );
    assert_eq!(
        serde_json::from_value::<OverLimit>(json!({"limit": "total", "nth": 11, "max": 10}))
            .unwrap(),
        OverLimit::Total { nth: 11, limit: 10 }
    );
}
```

```sql
-- The makers' log (dots-make-dots design sections 10 and 11): what a maker's run did, one row
-- per card of the maker's chat topic. `kind` is `made` for a dot it made; `detail` is JSON per
-- kind (for `made`: {"purpose": ..}). `run_id` is the maker's run and `root_run_id` its chat
-- topic; neither is a foreign key, as in `instruction_proposals`. `dot_id` is the made dot and
-- becomes NULL when it is deleted; `dot_name` keeps its name. The `made` rows of a run are what
-- the run's limit counts, so deleting a made dot does not give the run a place back.
CREATE TABLE making_events (
    id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    maker_dot_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dots(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    run_id        TEXT NOT NULL,
    root_run_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind          TEXT NOT NULL,
    dot_id        TEXT REFERENCES dots(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    dot_name      TEXT NOT NULL,
    detail        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX making_events_topic ON making_events(root_run_id, created_at);
CREATE INDEX making_events_run ON making_events(run_id, kind);
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/src/making/service.rs`:**

```rust
//! What a maker's run does (dots-make-dots design sections 7 to 10), for the tools both engines
//! offer it. The tools reach it through the check-ins (`CheckIns::makers`), so the reach check
//! and the limits are enforced here, in the core, and not in the prompt (section 12).

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::{Arc, Weak};

use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize};
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use tokio::sync::Mutex;

use super::log::{MakingEventKind, NewMakingEvent};
use super::reach::{reach_new, Reach, Wanted};
use crate::dot_admin::DotAdmin;
use crate::events::{Bus, RuntimeEvent};
use crate::model::{Dot, DotSpec, Made, Making, Run};
use crate::store::Store;
use crate::vault::{Consumer, GrantState, Vault};
use crate::{Error, Result};

/// The most characters of a made dot's purpose.
pub const MAX_PURPOSE: usize = 200;
/// The most characters of a job (design section 8).
pub const MAX_JOB: usize = 4000;
/// What is said of a purpose that is not one line of 1 to `MAX_PURPOSE` characters.
pub const PURPOSE_RULE: &str = "The purpose is one line of 1 to 200 characters.";
/// What is said of a first job that is not 1 to `MAX_JOB` characters.
pub const FIRST_JOB_RULE: &str = "The first job is 1 to 4000 characters.";
/// What a workflow step's run is told (design section 5).
pub const NOT_IN_A_STEP: &str = "A run that is a workflow step cannot make dots.";
/// What a run that has ended is told.
pub const RUN_ENDED: &str = "This run has ended, so it cannot make a dot.";

/// What a maker's run asks for with `make_dot` (design section 7.1). In JSON it is one flat
/// object: `purpose`, `first_job` and the fields of `Wanted`. A field none of them has is
/// refused, so a call can not name "Can make dots", the account or the engine.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct MakeDot {
    /// One line on what the dot is for, 1 to 200 characters, shown on cards and lists.
    pub purpose: String,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub wanted: Wanted,
    /// A first job for the new dot (design section 8), 1 to 4,000 characters when given. It is
    /// checked here and not started yet.
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub first_job: Option<String>,
}

// By hand: serde's `flatten` and `deny_unknown_fields` do not combine. The two fields of its
// own are taken out, and `Wanted` reads the rest and refuses what it does not have.
impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for MakeDot {
    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(d: D) -> std::result::Result<Self, D::Error> {
        use serde::de::Error as _;
        let mut fields = serde_json::Map::<String, Value>::deserialize(d)?;
        let purpose = match fields.remove("purpose") {
            Some(Value::String(purpose)) => purpose,
            Some(Value::Null) | None => return Err(D::Error::missing_field("purpose")),
            Some(other) => return Err(D::Error::custom(format!("purpose is text, not {other}"))),
        };
        // A model writes `null` for a field it leaves out.
        let first_job = match fields.remove("first_job") {
            Some(Value::String(job)) => Some(job),
            Some(Value::Null) | None => None,
            Some(other) => return Err(D::Error::custom(format!("first_job is text, not {other}"))),
        };
        let wanted = serde_json::from_value(Value::Object(fields)).map_err(D::Error::custom)?;
        Ok(MakeDot {
            purpose,
            wanted,
            first_job,
        })
    }
}

/// What came of a `make_dot`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]
pub enum MakeOutcome {
    /// Created at once.
    Made { dot: Dot },
    /// Beyond the maker's reach (`reach.extras`) or over a limit (`over`), or both: nothing
    /// was created, and the person is to answer (design sections 7.1 and 10).
    NeedsPerson {
        reach: Reach,
        over: Option<OverLimit>,
    },
}

/// Which limit a make would pass (design section 10), with the numbers the ask card's line
/// needs. In JSON the limit's number is `max`, since `limit` says which limit it is.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "limit", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum OverLimit {
    /// It would be the `nth` dot this run of the maker made.
    PerRun {
        nth: u32,
        #[serde(rename = "max")]
        limit: u32,
    },
    /// It would be the `nth` made dot of the maker that exists.
    Total {
        nth: u32,
        #[serde(rename = "max")]
        limit: u32,
    },
}

/// `n` as "1st", "2nd", "3rd", "4th", "11th", "21st".
fn ordinal(n: u32) -> String {
    let suffix = match (n % 10, n % 100) {
        (_, 11..=13) => "th",
        (1, _) => "st",
        (2, _) => "nd",
        (3, _) => "rd",
        _ => "th",
    };
    format!("{n}{suffix}")
}

impl OverLimit {
    /// The limit as one line of the ask card (design section 7.2).
    pub fn line(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::PerRun { nth, limit } => {
                format!("{} dot in this run; the limit is {limit}", ordinal(*nth))
            }
            Self::Total { nth, limit } => {
                format!("{} made dot kept; the limit is {limit}", ordinal(*nth))
            }
        }
    }
}

/// `purpose` as it is kept, without the spaces around it, or `PURPOSE_RULE`.
pub(crate) fn checked_purpose(purpose: &str) -> Result<String> {
    let purpose = purpose.trim();
    if purpose.is_empty() || purpose.chars().count() > MAX_PURPOSE || purpose.contains(['\n', '\r'])
    {
        return Err(Error::Invalid(PURPOSE_RULE.into()));
    }
    Ok(purpose.to_string())
}

struct Parts {
    store: Store,
    bus: Bus,
    dot_admin: DotAdmin,
    vault: Vault,
    /// Where runs' worktree copies are made (`RunnerConfig::worktrees_dir`).
    worktrees_root: PathBuf,
    /// Held from counting a maker's dots until the new one is stored, so two calls of one run
    /// cannot both take the last place.
    one_at_a_time: Mutex<()>,
}

/// Everything a maker does to other dots, for the tools of both engines. Cheap to clone; the
/// clones are one service. The runtime makes it once, at start.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Makers {
    parts: Arc<Parts>,
}

/// A `Makers` that does not keep it alive: what the check-ins hold, since the makers hold the
/// dot admin, which holds the runner, which holds the check-ins.
pub(crate) struct WeakMakers(Weak<Parts>);

impl WeakMakers {
    /// The makers, while the runtime that made them exists.
    pub(crate) fn upgrade(&self) -> Option<Makers> {
        self.0.upgrade().map(|parts| Makers { parts })
    }
}

impl Makers {
    pub(crate) fn new(
        store: Store,
        bus: Bus,
        dot_admin: DotAdmin,
        vault: Vault,
        worktrees_root: PathBuf,
    ) -> Makers {
        Makers {
            parts: Arc::new(Parts {
                store,
                bus,
                dot_admin,
                vault,
                worktrees_root,
                one_at_a_time: Mutex::new(()),
            }),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn downgrade(&self) -> WeakMakers {
        WeakMakers(Arc::downgrade(&self.parts))
    }

    /// Where runs' worktree copies are made: no dot a maker makes may work in one (design
    /// section 6, folder rules).
    pub fn worktrees_root(&self) -> &Path {
        &self.parts.worktrees_root
    }

    /// A maker's run asks for a new dot (design section 7.1). `run_id` is the run that calls;
    /// its dot is the maker.
    ///
    /// `Made` when everything asked is within the maker's reach and its limits: the dot
    /// exists, in the maker's account and workspace, with who made it recorded, and the
    /// topic's log has a `made` entry. `NeedsPerson` when something is beyond reach or a limit
    /// would be passed: nothing was created.
    ///
    /// An error, with a sentence the model can act on, for what no answer of the person could
    /// allow: a dot that may not make dots, a workflow step's run, a run that has ended
    /// (`Invalid`), a dot that is not valid (`reach_new`), a Library item, variable or
    /// consumer that does not exist (`check_exists`), a name another dot has (`Conflict`), and
    /// a refusal of this PC's role in the maker's account (`NotAllowed`).
    pub async fn make_dot(&self, run_id: &str, ask: MakeDot) -> Result<MakeOutcome> {
        let p = &self.parts;
        let run = p.store.get_run(run_id).await?;
        let maker = p.store.get_dot(&run.dot_id).await?;
        may_make(&maker, &run)?;
        let purpose = checked_purpose(&ask.purpose)?;
        if let Some(job) = &ask.first_job {
            let job = job.trim();
            if job.is_empty() || job.chars().count() > MAX_JOB {
                return Err(Error::Invalid(FIRST_JOB_RULE.into()));
            }
        }
        let reach = reach_new(&maker, &ask.wanted, &p.worktrees_root)?;
        let _one_at_a_time = p.one_at_a_time.lock().await;
        // Before the limits and the extras: no request is kept for what can never be made.
        self.check_exists(&maker, &reach.spec).await?;
        self.check_name_free(&reach.spec.name).await?;
        let over = self.over_limit(&maker, &run.id).await?;
        if over.is_some() || !reach.extras.is_empty() {
            return Ok(MakeOutcome::NeedsPerson { reach, over });
        }
        let Reach {
            spec,
            create_folder,
            ..
        } = reach;
        let dot = self
            .create_made(
                &maker,
                &run.id,
                &run.root_run_id,
                spec,
                &purpose,
                create_folder,
            )
            .await?;
        // The first job is not started here: `ask.first_job` is checked above and goes no
        // further yet (design section 8).
        Ok(MakeOutcome::Made { dot })
    }

    /// Refuses what `spec`, a dot a maker asks for, names that does not exist (design section
    /// 7.1): a Library item, a consumer and a variable. It is run again when the person
    /// answers a request, against the Library and the vault as they are then (section 7.2).
    ///
    /// A consumer exists when it is the shell or an MCP server the dot would use, named in its
    /// `uses` or come with a plugin it names. A variable is refused only when the vault says
    /// for sure that the maker's account has none of that name; when it cannot say (the account
    /// is offline, say), the name passes, as it does when a person saves a dot.
    pub(crate) async fn check_exists(&self, maker: &Dot, spec: &DotSpec) -> Result<()> {
        let p = &self.parts;
        p.store.check_uses_exist(&spec.uses).await?;
        if spec.variables.0.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let used: Vec<String> = p
            .store
            .used_mcp_servers(&spec.uses)
            .await?
            .into_iter()
            .map(|server| server.name)
            .collect();
        for key in spec.variables.0.keys() {
            if let Consumer::Mcp(server) = Consumer::parse(key)? {
                if !used.contains(&server) {
                    return Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                        "The dot would not use an MCP server named '{server}', so it cannot be \
                         given variables for it. Name the server in uses, or leave those \
                         variables out."
                    )));
                }
            }
        }
        // The grants as the maker's account and workspace would resolve them: the made dot is
        // in both.
        let mut probe = maker.clone();
        probe.spec.variables = spec.variables.clone();
        for grant in p.vault.grant_statuses(&probe).await? {
            if grant.status == GrantState::NotDefined {
                return Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                    "There is no variable named {}. Name one that exists, or leave it out and \
                     tell the person it is missing.",
                    grant.name
                )));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Refuses a name another dot has, in any letter case (`Conflict`).
    pub(crate) async fn check_name_free(&self, name: &str) -> Result<()> {
        if self.parts.store.dot_name_taken(name.trim()).await? {
            return Err(Error::Conflict(format!(
                "A dot named {:?} already exists. Choose another name.",
                name.trim()
            )));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The limit one more dot of `maker`, made by its run `run_id`, would pass (design section
    /// 10); the run's limit first when it would pass both. The run's count is of the dots the
    /// run made, deleted ones too; the total is of the made dots that exist now.
    pub(crate) async fn over_limit(&self, maker: &Dot, run_id: &str) -> Result<Option<OverLimit>> {
        let store = &self.parts.store;
        let Making { per_run, total, .. } = maker.spec.making;
        let in_run = store.count_made_in_run(run_id).await?;
        if in_run >= per_run {
            return Ok(Some(OverLimit::PerRun {
                nth: in_run + 1,
                limit: per_run,
            }));
        }
        let kept = store.count_made_dots(&maker.id).await?;
        if kept >= total {
            return Ok(Some(OverLimit::Total {
                nth: kept + 1,
                limit: total,
            }));
        }
        Ok(None)
    }

    /// Creates the dot `spec` as one `maker` made in its run `run_id` of the topic
    /// `root_run_id`, writes the `made` entry of the log and publishes `MakingUpdated`. `spec`
    /// is already checked: within reach, or allowed by the person (design section 7.2); the
    /// limits are the caller's too. `purpose` is as `checked_purpose` gives it.
    ///
    /// Whatever `spec` says, the dot may not make dots and is enabled (section 6). It goes
    /// through `DotAdmin::create`, so the name, the Library items and this PC's rights in the
    /// maker's account are checked as for a dot the person creates. `create_folder` (of
    /// `Reach`) is made first, and removed again when the dot is not created.
    pub async fn create_made(
        &self,
        maker: &Dot,
        run_id: &str,
        root_run_id: &str,
        mut spec: DotSpec,
        purpose: &str,
        create_folder: Option<PathBuf>,
    ) -> Result<Dot> {
        let p = &self.parts;
        spec.making = Making::default();
        spec.enabled = true;
        // The folders that are made for it, deepest last.
        let mut new_folders: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
        if let Some(folder) = &create_folder {
            let mut missing = folder.as_path();
            while !missing.exists() {
                new_folders.push(missing.to_path_buf());
                match missing.parent() {
                    Some(parent) => missing = parent,
                    None => break,
                }
            }
            new_folders.reverse();
            tokio::fs::create_dir_all(folder).await?;
        }
        let made = Made {
            by_dot_id: Some(maker.id.clone()),
            by_name: maker.spec.name.clone(),
            run_id: run_id.to_string(),
            purpose: purpose.to_string(),
        };
        let created = p
            .dot_admin
            .create(
                spec,
                maker.org_id.clone(),
                Some(maker.workspace_id.clone()),
                Some(made),
            )
            .await;
        let dot = match created {
            Ok(dot) => dot,
            Err(e) => {
                // Only removes an empty folder, so nothing put there in between is lost.
                for folder in new_folders.iter().rev() {
                    let _ = tokio::fs::remove_dir(folder).await;
                }
                return Err(e);
            }
        };
        // The dot exists whether or not its entry could be written, so a failure here is
        // logged and the make still succeeds.
        let logged = p
            .store
            .add_making_event(&NewMakingEvent {
                maker_dot_id: &maker.id,
                run_id,
                root_run_id,
                kind: MakingEventKind::Made,
                dot_id: Some(&dot.id),
                dot_name: &dot.spec.name,
                detail: json!({ "purpose": purpose }),
            })
            .await;
        if let Err(e) = logged {
            tracing::error!(dot = %dot.id, run = %run_id, "the made dot was not logged: {e}");
        }
        self.updated(&maker.id, root_run_id);
        Ok(dot)
    }

    /// Says that the log of the topic `root_run_id` of the maker `maker_id` changed.
    pub(crate) fn updated(&self, maker_id: &str, root_run_id: &str) {
        let _ = self.parts.bus.send(RuntimeEvent::MakingUpdated {
            dot_id: maker_id.to_string(),
            root_run_id: root_run_id.to_string(),
        });
    }
}

/// Whether `run`, a run of `maker`, may use the tools for making dots (design section 5): the
/// dot's switch is on, the run is no workflow step's, and it has not ended. What the dot's
/// policy says of `MakeDots` is checked where the tool is called.
pub(crate) fn may_make(maker: &Dot, run: &Run) -> Result<()> {
    if !maker.spec.making.on {
        return Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
            "{} may not make dots. The person turns that on in the dot's settings.",
            maker.spec.name
        )));
    }
    // As for `propose_instructions` and `start_workflow`: a step's chat ends with the step, so
    // a wake or a card answer would have nowhere to land.
    if run.workflow_step_run_id.is_some() {
        return Err(Error::Invalid(NOT_IN_A_STEP.into()));
    }
    if run.status.is_terminal() {
        return Err(Error::Invalid(RUN_ENDED.into()));
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

```rust
//! The makers' log, and what a make is checked against before anything is saved (dots-make-dots
//! design sections 7.1, 10 and 11).

use sqlx::sqlite::SqliteRow;
use sqlx::Row;

use super::library::check_uses;
use super::Store;
use crate::library::Uses;
use crate::making::log::{MakingEvent, MakingEventKind, NewMakingEvent};
use crate::util::{new_id, now};
use crate::Result;

const COLUMNS: &str =
    "id, maker_dot_id, run_id, root_run_id, kind, dot_id, dot_name, detail, created_at";

fn event_from_row(row: &SqliteRow) -> Result<MakingEvent> {
    Ok(MakingEvent {
        id: row.try_get("id")?,
        maker_dot_id: row.try_get("maker_dot_id")?,
        run_id: row.try_get("run_id")?,
        root_run_id: row.try_get("root_run_id")?,
        kind: MakingEventKind::parse(&row.try_get::<String, _>("kind")?)?,
        dot_id: row.try_get("dot_id")?,
        dot_name: row.try_get("dot_name")?,
        detail: serde_json::from_str(&row.try_get::<String, _>("detail")?)?,
        created_at: row.try_get("created_at")?,
    })
}

impl Store {
    /// Writes one entry of the makers' log, as of now.
    pub async fn add_making_event(&self, new: &NewMakingEvent<'_>) -> Result<MakingEvent> {
        let event = MakingEvent {
            id: new_id(),
            maker_dot_id: new.maker_dot_id.to_string(),
            run_id: new.run_id.to_string(),
            root_run_id: new.root_run_id.to_string(),
            kind: new.kind,
            dot_id: new.dot_id.map(str::to_string),
            dot_name: new.dot_name.to_string(),
            detail: new.detail.clone(),
            created_at: now(),
        };
        sqlx::query(&format!(
            "INSERT INTO making_events ({COLUMNS}) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)"
        ))
        .bind(&event.id)
        .bind(&event.maker_dot_id)
        .bind(&event.run_id)
        .bind(&event.root_run_id)
        .bind(event.kind.as_str())
        .bind(&event.dot_id)
        .bind(&event.dot_name)
        .bind(serde_json::to_string(&event.detail)?)
        .bind(&event.created_at)
        .execute(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        Ok(event)
    }

    /// The log of one chat topic of a maker, oldest first: its cards in the order things
    /// happened (dots-make-dots design section 11). Of two written in the same millisecond, the
    /// one stored first comes first (`rowid`).
    pub async fn list_making_events(&self, root_run_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<MakingEvent>> {
        let rows = sqlx::query(&format!(
            "SELECT {COLUMNS} FROM making_events WHERE root_run_id = ? \
             ORDER BY created_at, rowid"
        ))
        .bind(root_run_id)
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        rows.iter().map(event_from_row).collect()
    }

    /// How many dots the run `run_id` made: what a maker's limit for one run counts
    /// (dots-make-dots design section 10). It counts the log, not the dots, so a made dot that
    /// was deleted since still counts.
    pub async fn count_made_in_run(&self, run_id: &str) -> Result<u32> {
        let n: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM making_events WHERE run_id = ? AND kind = 'made'",
        )
        .bind(run_id)
        .fetch_one(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        Ok(n as u32)
    }

    /// Refuses a name of `uses` that the Library does not have, as saving a dot with them
    /// would (`Invalid`), without saving anything: so a make that could never be allowed is
    /// refused before a request for it is kept (dots-make-dots design section 7.1).
    pub async fn check_uses_exist(&self, uses: &Uses) -> Result<()> {
        let mut conn = self.pool.acquire().await?;
        check_uses(&mut conn, uses).await
    }

    /// Whether a dot has `name`, in any letter case: what saving a new dot of that name would
    /// refuse.
    pub async fn dot_name_taken(&self, name: &str) -> Result<bool> {
        Ok(
            sqlx::query("SELECT 1 FROM dots WHERE name = ? COLLATE NOCASE")
                .bind(name)
                .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
                .await?
                .is_some(),
        )
    }
}
```

### Task 6: A maker's topic is woken once, and the wake waits while it is busy

A wake is a message Dots sends into a maker's chat topic: a run that continues the topic. It is stored first, delivered when the topic is free, and delivered once even when two deliveries race or Dots restarts (spec section 8: "If the maker is busy, the wake queues").

**Files:**
- Create: `crates/dots-core/migrations/0049_making_wakes.sql`, `crates/dots-core/src/making/wake.rs`
- Modify: `crates/dots-core/src/making/mod.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/making/service.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/runtime.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/store/making.rs`
- Test: `crates/dots-core/tests/making_wake_test.rs`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 5's `Makers`; `checkins::continuation`, `FollowUps::thread_lock`.
- Produces: `making::wake::{MakingWake, WAKE_ID}` (`WAKE_ID = "wake_id"`); `Makers::wake(&self, maker_dot_id: &str, root_run_id: &str, message: &str) -> Result<()>` (takes the topic's lock; the caller must not hold it); `Makers::deliver_wakes(&self) -> Result<()>`; `Makers::spawn_wakes(&self, shutdown)` (a pass at start, then after each terminal `RunUpdated`, and every 30 s). The wake's run: a continuation, payload `{"message", "wake_id"}`, not typed. `Makers::new(store, bus, dot_admin, vault, worktrees_root, follow_ups, runner)`. Table `making_wakes`. `Store::{add_making_wake, get_making_wake, waiting_making_wakes, deliver_making_wake, drop_making_wake}`; `deliver_making_wake(id, &NewRun)` marks the wake delivered and creates its run in one transaction.

**Create `crates/dots-core/tests/making_wake_test.rs`:**

```rust
//! Waking a maker (dots-make-dots design sections 7.2 and 8): a wake becomes one new run of the
//! maker in its chat topic, with the wake's message, exactly once; it waits while the topic is
//! busy and across a restart; and it goes with a topic or a maker that is gone.

mod common;

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use common::{is_not_found, spec, wait_status};
use dots_core::making::wake::{MakingWake, WAKE_ID};
use dots_core::model::{Dot, NewRun, Run, RunStatus, TriggerKind, WorkspaceMode};
use dots_core::{Config, Runtime};
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use tempfile::TempDir;

struct T {
    dir: TempDir,
    rt: Runtime,
}

/// A runtime on the data folder below `dir`. With `runs` its queued runs start, each with the
/// fake CLI, which waits `slow_ms` before it ends; without, none starts, and a test puts its
/// runs in the state it needs by hand, so no end of a run sets the wakes' loop going.
async fn runtime(dir: &Path, runs: bool, slow_ms: u64) -> Runtime {
    let mut cfg = Config::new(dir.join("data"));
    cfg.port = 0;
    cfg.claude_path = Some(PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake-claude")));
    if !runs {
        cfg.max_concurrent_runs = 0;
    }
    if slow_ms > 0 {
        let script = json!([
            {"emit": {"type": "system", "subtype": "init", "session_id": "$SESSION"}},
            {"sleep_ms": slow_ms},
            {"emit": {"type": "result", "subtype": "success", "is_error": false,
                      "result": "fake done", "usage": {"input_tokens": 1, "output_tokens": 1}}},
        ]);
        let p = dir.join("script.json");
        std::fs::write(&p, script.to_string()).unwrap();
        cfg.claude_env
            .push(("FAKE_CLAUDE_SCRIPT".into(), p.to_string_lossy().to_string()));
    }
    Runtime::start(cfg).await.unwrap()
}

/// A runtime whose runs do not start.
async fn quiet() -> T {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let rt = runtime(dir.path(), false, 0).await;
    T { dir, rt }
}

/// A runtime whose runs start and take `slow_ms` each.
async fn running(slow_ms: u64) -> T {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let rt = runtime(dir.path(), true, slow_ms).await;
    T { dir, rt }
}

/// A maker named `name` that works in the test's folder itself.
async fn maker(t: &T, name: &str) -> Dot {
    let mut s = spec(name);
    s.workdir = t.dir.path().to_string_lossy().to_string();
    s.workspace_mode = WorkspaceMode::Folder;
    s.making.on = true;
    t.rt.create_dot(s, None, None).await.unwrap()
}

/// A chat topic of `dot` whose first run is running, put there by hand.
async fn working_topic(t: &T, dot: &Dot) -> Run {
    let mut new = NewRun::new(&dot.id, TriggerKind::Chat);
    new.payload = Some(json!({"message": "watch three blogs", "typed": true}));
    let run = t.rt.store().create_run(&new).await.unwrap();
    assert!(t.rt.store().claim_run(&run.id).await.unwrap());
    t.rt.store()
        .set_session(&run.id, "session-1")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    t.rt.store().get_run(&run.id).await.unwrap()
}

/// Ends `run` by hand, as a run that finished its work.
async fn end(t: &T, run: &Run) -> Run {
    t.rt.store()
        .finish_run(&run.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, Some("done"), None)
        .await
        .unwrap()
}

/// A chat topic of `dot` that has ended, put there by hand: it is free.
async fn free_topic(t: &T, dot: &Dot) -> Run {
    let run = working_topic(t, dot).await;
    end(t, &run).await
}

fn message(run: &Run) -> &str {
    run.payload.as_ref().unwrap()["message"].as_str().unwrap()
}

/// The wake the run `run` delivered, as its payload names it.
async fn wake_of(t: &T, run: &Run) -> MakingWake {
    let id = run.payload.as_ref().unwrap()[WAKE_ID]
        .as_str()
        .expect("the run names its wake");
    t.rt.store().get_making_wake(id).await.unwrap()
}

/// The runs of the topic `root`, oldest first.
async fn thread(t: &T, root: &Run) -> Vec<Run> {
    t.rt.store().list_thread(&root.id).await.unwrap()
}

/// The messages of the wakes that wait.
async fn waiting(t: &T) -> Vec<String> {
    let wakes = t.rt.store().waiting_making_wakes().await.unwrap();
    wakes.into_iter().map(|w| w.message).collect()
}

/// Polls until the topic `root` has `n` runs, and returns them.
async fn thread_of(t: &T, root: &Run, n: usize) -> Vec<Run> {
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(30);
    loop {
        let runs = thread(t, root).await;
        if runs.len() >= n {
            assert_eq!(runs.len(), n, "{runs:#?}");
            return runs;
        }
        assert!(
            Instant::now() < deadline,
            "the topic did not reach {n} runs: {runs:#?}"
        );
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_wake_of_a_free_topic_starts_a_run_in_that_topic_with_the_message() {
    let t = running(0).await;
    let dot = maker(&t, "Researcher").await;
    let chat = t.rt.chat(&dot.id, "watch three blogs", None).await.unwrap();
    let chat = wait_status(t.rt.store(), &chat.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 15).await;
    assert!(chat.session_id.is_some());

    t.rt.makers()
        .wake(&dot.id, &chat.id, "Blog Watcher was made as you asked.")
        .await
        .unwrap();

    // Delivered at once: the topic was free.
    assert!(waiting(&t).await.is_empty());
    let runs = thread(&t, &chat).await;
    assert_eq!(runs.len(), 2, "{runs:#?}");
    let run = &runs[1];
    // A chat run that goes on in the topic's session, as after a decided card, with Dots' own
    // words: not a message the person typed.
    assert_eq!(run.dot_id, dot.id);
    assert_eq!(run.trigger, TriggerKind::Chat);
    assert_eq!(run.parent_run_id.as_deref(), Some(chat.id.as_str()));
    assert_eq!(run.root_run_id, chat.id);
    assert_eq!(run.session_id, chat.session_id);
    assert_eq!(message(run), "Blog Watcher was made as you asked.");
    assert!(!dots_core::prompt::is_typed(run));
    assert_eq!(run.payload.as_ref().unwrap().get("typed"), None);
    assert_eq!(run.payload.as_ref().unwrap().get("answer"), None);
    let wake = wake_of(&t, run).await;
    assert_eq!(wake.maker_dot_id, dot.id);
    assert_eq!(wake.root_run_id, chat.id);
    assert_eq!(wake.run_id.as_deref(), Some(run.id.as_str()));
    assert!(wake.delivered_at.is_some());
    // The run is a run like any other of the dot: it starts and ends.
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &run.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 15).await;
    assert_eq!(thread(&t, &chat).await.len(), 2);
    t.rt.shutdown();
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_wake_of_a_busy_topic_waits_and_is_delivered_when_the_run_ends() {
    let t = running(3000).await;
    let dot = maker(&t, "Researcher").await;
    let chat = t.rt.chat(&dot.id, "watch three blogs", None).await.unwrap();
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &chat.id, RunStatus::Running, 15).await;

    t.rt.makers()
        .wake(&dot.id, &chat.id, "Blog Watcher finished.")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    // The maker is still working on the topic: nothing continues it yet.
    assert_eq!(waiting(&t).await, ["Blog Watcher finished."]);
    assert_eq!(thread(&t, &chat).await.len(), 1);

    // Nobody calls anything: the end of the run delivers the wake.
    let runs = thread_of(&t, &chat, 2).await;
    let chat = t.rt.store().get_run(&chat.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(chat.status, RunStatus::Succeeded);
    let run = &runs[1];
    assert_eq!(run.parent_run_id.as_deref(), Some(chat.id.as_str()));
    assert_eq!(run.session_id, chat.session_id);
    assert_eq!(message(run), "Blog Watcher finished.");
    assert_eq!(
        wake_of(&t, run).await.run_id.as_deref(),
        Some(run.id.as_str())
    );
    assert!(waiting(&t).await.is_empty());
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &run.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 15).await;
    t.rt.shutdown();
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn two_wakes_of_a_busy_topic_are_delivered_oldest_first() {
    let t = running(3000).await;
    let dot = maker(&t, "Researcher").await;
    let chat = t.rt.chat(&dot.id, "watch three blogs", None).await.unwrap();
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &chat.id, RunStatus::Running, 15).await;
    t.rt.makers()
        .wake(&dot.id, &chat.id, "Blog Watcher finished.")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    t.rt.makers()
        .wake(&dot.id, &chat.id, "Feed Reader finished.")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        waiting(&t).await,
        ["Blog Watcher finished.", "Feed Reader finished."]
    );

    // One at a time, each as a run of its own: the older wake's run makes the topic busy again,
    // so the newer one waits for its end.
    let runs = thread_of(&t, &chat, 2).await;
    assert_eq!(message(&runs[1]), "Blog Watcher finished.");
    assert_eq!(waiting(&t).await, ["Feed Reader finished."]);

    let runs = thread_of(&t, &chat, 3).await;
    assert_eq!(message(&runs[2]), "Feed Reader finished.");
    assert_eq!(runs[2].parent_run_id.as_deref(), Some(runs[1].id.as_str()));
    let first = t.rt.store().get_run(&runs[1].id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(first.status, RunStatus::Succeeded);
    assert!(waiting(&t).await.is_empty());
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &runs[2].id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 15).await;
    // Each wake has its own run.
    assert_ne!(
        wake_of(&t, &runs[1]).await.id,
        wake_of(&t, &runs[2]).await.id
    );
    assert_eq!(thread(&t, &chat).await.len(), 3);
    t.rt.shutdown();
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn a_wake_is_delivered_once_when_delivery_runs_twice_at_the_same_time() {
    let t = quiet().await;
    let dot = maker(&t, "Researcher").await;
    for round in 0..5 {
        let chat = free_topic(&t, &dot).await;
        // Stored and not delivered yet, as a wake that waited.
        let wake =
            t.rt.store()
                .add_making_wake(&dot.id, &chat.id, &format!("Job {round} finished."))
                .await
                .unwrap();
        let passes: Vec<_> = (0..4)
            .map(|_| {
                let makers = t.rt.makers().clone();
                tokio::spawn(async move { makers.deliver_wakes().await })
            })
            .collect();
        for pass in passes {
            pass.await.unwrap().unwrap();
        }
        let runs = thread(&t, &chat).await;
        assert_eq!(runs.len(), 2, "round {round}: {runs:#?}");
        let wake = t.rt.store().get_making_wake(&wake.id).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(wake.run_id.as_deref(), Some(runs[1].id.as_str()));
        assert_eq!(runs[1].status, RunStatus::Queued);
        // Once delivered, it stays delivered.
        t.rt.makers().deliver_wakes().await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(thread(&t, &chat).await.len(), 2);
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_wake_waiting_at_startup_is_delivered() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let rt = runtime(dir.path(), false, 0).await;
    let t = T { dir, rt };
    let dot = maker(&t, "Researcher").await;
    let chat = free_topic(&t, &dot).await;
    // Dots closes while the wake waits.
    t.rt.shutdown();
    let wake =
        t.rt.store()
            .add_making_wake(&dot.id, &chat.id, "Blog Watcher finished.")
            .await
            .unwrap();
    let T { dir, rt } = t;
    drop(rt);

    let rt = runtime(dir.path(), false, 0).await;
    let t = T { dir, rt };
    let runs = thread_of(&t, &chat, 2).await;
    assert_eq!(message(&runs[1]), "Blog Watcher finished.");
    assert_eq!(runs[1].parent_run_id.as_deref(), Some(chat.id.as_str()));
    assert_eq!(runs[1].session_id.as_deref(), Some("session-1"));
    assert_eq!(wake_of(&t, &runs[1]).await.id, wake.id);
    assert!(waiting(&t).await.is_empty());
    t.rt.shutdown();
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_wake_of_a_topic_that_is_gone_is_dropped() {
    let t = quiet().await;
    let dot = maker(&t, "Researcher").await;
    let other = maker(&t, "Writer").await;
    let others = free_topic(&t, &other).await;

    // A topic whose runs are gone, and one that is not the maker's.
    let gone =
        t.rt.store()
            .add_making_wake(&dot.id, "no-such-run", "Blog Watcher finished.")
            .await
            .unwrap();
    let not_its_own =
        t.rt.store()
            .add_making_wake(&dot.id, &others.id, "Feed Reader finished.")
            .await
            .unwrap();
    t.rt.makers().deliver_wakes().await.unwrap();

    // Neither waits, and neither started a run: there is no chat of the maker to say it in.
    assert!(waiting(&t).await.is_empty());
    for wake in [gone, not_its_own] {
        let wake = t.rt.store().get_making_wake(&wake.id).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(wake.run_id, None);
        assert!(wake.delivered_at.is_some());
    }
    let runs = t.rt.store().list_runs(Some(&dot.id), 10).await.unwrap();
    assert!(runs.is_empty(), "{runs:#?}");
    assert_eq!(thread(&t, &others).await.len(), 1);
    // `wake` itself does the same, and does not fail its caller.
    t.rt.makers()
        .wake(&dot.id, "no-such-run", "Blog Watcher finished.")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert!(waiting(&t).await.is_empty());
    t.rt.makers().deliver_wakes().await.unwrap();
    let runs = t.rt.store().list_runs(Some(&dot.id), 10).await.unwrap();
    assert!(runs.is_empty(), "{runs:#?}");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn deleting_the_maker_discards_its_wakes() {
    let t = quiet().await;
    let dot = maker(&t, "Researcher").await;
    let kept = maker(&t, "Writer").await;
    let chat = free_topic(&t, &dot).await;
    let kept_chat = working_topic(&t, &kept).await;
    // Stored and not delivered, as wakes that wait.
    let mut wakes = Vec::new();
    for message in ["Blog Watcher finished.", "Blog Watcher failed."] {
        let wake = t.rt.store().add_making_wake(&dot.id, &chat.id, message);
        wakes.push(wake.await.unwrap());
    }
    t.rt.store()
        .add_making_wake(&kept.id, &kept_chat.id, "Feed Reader finished.")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(waiting(&t).await.len(), 3);

    t.rt.delete_dot(&dot.id).await.unwrap();

    for wake in &wakes {
        let gone = t.rt.store().get_making_wake(&wake.id).await.unwrap_err();
        assert!(is_not_found(&gone), "{gone}");
    }
    // Another maker's wake is untouched, and a pass finds nothing of the deleted one.
    t.rt.makers().deliver_wakes().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(waiting(&t).await, ["Feed Reader finished."]);
    assert_eq!(thread(&t, &kept_chat).await.len(), 1);
    // A wake for a maker that is gone is not stored, and its caller is told.
    let refused =
        t.rt.makers()
            .wake(&dot.id, &chat.id, "Blog Watcher finished.");
    assert!(refused.await.is_err());
    assert_eq!(waiting(&t).await, ["Feed Reader finished."]);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn wakes_of_two_topics_of_one_maker_do_not_wait_for_each_other() {
    let t = quiet().await;
    let dot = maker(&t, "Researcher").await;
    let busy = working_topic(&t, &dot).await;
    let free = free_topic(&t, &dot).await;

    t.rt.makers()
        .wake(&dot.id, &busy.id, "Blog Watcher finished.")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    t.rt.makers()
        .wake(&dot.id, &free.id, "Feed Reader finished.")
        .await
        .unwrap();

    // The free topic's wake is not held by the older wake of the busy one, nor by the maker's
    // run in the other topic: its run is queued, and the runner starts it in its turn.
    assert_eq!(waiting(&t).await, ["Blog Watcher finished."]);
    let runs = thread(&t, &free).await;
    assert_eq!(runs.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(message(&runs[1]), "Feed Reader finished.");
    assert_eq!(runs[1].status, RunStatus::Queued);
    assert_eq!(runs[1].root_run_id, free.id);
    assert_eq!(thread(&t, &busy).await.len(), 1);

    // The busy topic ends while the other topic's wake run is still queued: its wake is
    // delivered all the same, into its own topic.
    end(&t, &busy).await;
    t.rt.makers().deliver_wakes().await.unwrap();
    assert!(waiting(&t).await.is_empty());
    let runs = thread(&t, &busy).await;
    assert_eq!(runs.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(message(&runs[1]), "Blog Watcher finished.");
    assert_eq!(runs[1].root_run_id, busy.id);
    assert_eq!(runs[1].session_id.as_deref(), Some("session-1"));
    // A second wake of a topic whose wake run is queued waits for it.
    t.rt.makers()
        .wake(&dot.id, &free.id, "Feed Reader failed.")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(waiting(&t).await, ["Feed Reader failed."]);
    assert_eq!(thread(&t, &free).await.len(), 2);
}

/// What a wake's payload holds: the message and the wake's id, and nothing that marks it as
/// typed by the person or as an answer of theirs.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_wake_run_says_it_is_a_wake_and_not_the_persons_message() {
    let t = quiet().await;
    let dot = maker(&t, "Researcher").await;
    let chat = free_topic(&t, &dot).await;
    t.rt.makers()
        .wake(
            &dot.id,
            &chat.id,
            "The person chose not to make Blog Watcher.",
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let runs = thread(&t, &chat).await;
    let wake = wake_of(&t, &runs[1]).await;
    let expected: Value = json!({
        "message": "The person chose not to make Blog Watcher.",
        "wake_id": wake.id,
    });
    assert_eq!(runs[1].payload, Some(expected));
}
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/migrations/0049_making_wakes.sql`:**

```sql
-- The wakes of makers (dots-make-dots design sections 7.2 and 8): a message Dots has for a
-- maker's chat topic, delivered by one new run of the maker in that topic, exactly once. A wake
-- waits while its topic is busy, and across a restart. `root_run_id` is the maker's chat topic
-- and no foreign key, as in `making_events`. `delivered_at` is NULL while the wake waits;
-- `run_id` is the run that delivered it, written with the run in one transaction, and stays
-- NULL for a wake that was dropped because its topic is gone. Deleting the maker discards its
-- wakes.
CREATE TABLE making_wakes (
    id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    maker_dot_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dots(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    root_run_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
    message       TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
    run_id        TEXT,
    delivered_at  TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX making_wakes_waiting ON making_wakes(created_at) WHERE delivered_at IS NULL;
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/src/making/wake.rs`:**

```rust
//! Waking a maker (dots-make-dots design sections 7.2 and 8): a message Dots has for a maker's
//! chat topic, the person's answer to a make request or the end of a job, becomes one new run
//! of the maker in that topic. A wake is stored first and delivered by exactly one run. While
//! the topic is busy it waits, since nothing continues a thread that has not ended; the loop
//! here delivers it when a run ends, and once at start for what waited across a restart.

use std::collections::HashSet;

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use tokio::sync::broadcast::error::RecvError;
use tokio::task::JoinHandle;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use super::service::Makers;
use crate::events::RuntimeEvent;
use crate::scheduler::ERROR_WAIT;
use crate::{Error, Result};

/// The key of a wake's run's payload that holds the wake's id: the run's message is Dots' own,
/// not one the person typed, as `follow_up_id` says of a follow-up's.
pub const WAKE_ID: &str = "wake_id";

/// One wake: a message for the chat topic `root_run_id` of the maker `maker_dot_id`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct MakingWake {
    pub id: String,
    /// The maker.
    pub maker_dot_id: String,
    /// The maker's chat topic the wake is for, as it was when the wake was stored. The wake
    /// follows that run when the person moves it or merges its topic into another.
    pub root_run_id: String,
    /// What the maker's new run is told.
    pub message: String,
    pub created_at: String,
    /// The run that delivered it. `None` while it waits, and for a wake that was dropped.
    pub run_id: Option<String>,
    /// When it was delivered or dropped; `None` while it waits.
    pub delivered_at: Option<String>,
}

/// What came of trying one waiting wake.
enum Tried {
    /// Its run is stored and announced.
    Delivered,
    /// Its topic has a run that has not ended: it waits for the end of that run.
    Busy,
    /// Its topic is adding an app the person accepted, which ends with no run of its own when
    /// the adding fails: it is tried again after a wait.
    Deciding,
    /// Its topic is gone, or another pass had delivered it since the list was read.
    Done,
    /// An earlier wake of its topic was tried in this pass.
    Later,
}

impl Makers {
    /// Queues a wake of the maker's chat topic and delivers it now if the topic is free
    /// (design sections 7.2 and 8). Returns once the wake is stored: delivery never fails the
    /// caller.
    ///
    /// `root_run_id` is any run that is still in the topic, by rule its first one. An error
    /// means the wake was not stored: the maker is deleted, or the store failed. It takes the
    /// thread lock (`FollowUps::thread_lock`), so the caller must not hold it.
    pub async fn wake(&self, maker_dot_id: &str, root_run_id: &str, message: &str) -> Result<()> {
        let wake = self
            .parts
            .store
            .add_making_wake(maker_dot_id, root_run_id, message)
            .await?;
        tracing::debug!(wake = %wake.id, maker = %maker_dot_id, "a wake was stored");
        if let Err(e) = self.wake_pass().await {
            tracing::warn!(wake = %wake.id, "the wake waits; delivering it failed: {e}");
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Delivers waiting wakes of every topic that is free now, oldest first, one per topic per
    /// pass. Called when a run ends, at startup, and by `wake`.
    ///
    /// Two passes at once deliver a wake once: each wake is tried under the thread lock, and
    /// its row is marked in the transaction that stores its run. A wake whose run could not be
    /// stored stays waiting, and the error of the first such wake is returned after the other
    /// topics were tried.
    pub async fn deliver_wakes(&self) -> Result<()> {
        self.wake_pass().await.map(|_| ())
    }

    /// One pass. `true` when a wake waits for something whose end no event tells (`Deciding`):
    /// the loop then tries again after a wait.
    async fn wake_pass(&self) -> Result<bool> {
        let mut tried_topics = HashSet::new();
        let mut again = false;
        let mut failed = None;
        for wake in self.parts.store.waiting_making_wakes().await? {
            match self.deliver_wake(&wake, &mut tried_topics).await {
                Ok(Tried::Deciding) => again = true,
                Ok(_) => {}
                Err(e) => {
                    tracing::warn!(wake = %wake.id, "the wake's run could not be started: {e}");
                    failed.get_or_insert(e);
                }
            }
        }
        match failed {
            Some(e) => Err(e),
            None => Ok(again),
        }
    }

    /// Tries one waiting wake, under the thread lock, as `Runtime::decide_instruction_proposal`
    /// continues a chat: the topic's end is read, and a topic with a run that has not ended is
    /// left alone. Here that is no refusal: the wake waits. `tried_topics` are the topics an
    /// earlier wake of this pass was tried for; the wake's own is added, so of several wakes
    /// of one topic the oldest goes first, also when its run could not be stored.
    async fn deliver_wake(
        &self,
        wake: &MakingWake,
        tried_topics: &mut HashSet<String>,
    ) -> Result<Tried> {
        let p = &self.parts;
        let lock = p.follow_ups.thread_lock();
        let one_at_a_time = lock.lock().await;
        // The topic the wake's run is in now: the person may have moved it or merged its topic
        // into another since.
        let first = match p.store.get_run(&wake.root_run_id).await {
            Ok(run) if run.dot_id == wake.maker_dot_id => run,
            Ok(_) | Err(Error::NotFound(_)) => {
                // History was pruned or the topic deleted: there is no chat to say it in.
                if p.store.drop_making_wake(&wake.id).await? {
                    tracing::warn!(
                        wake = %wake.id, maker = %wake.maker_dot_id, topic = %wake.root_run_id,
                        "a wake was dropped because its chat topic is gone"
                    );
                }
                return Ok(Tried::Done);
            }
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        };
        let topic = first.root_run_id.clone();
        if !tried_topics.insert(topic.clone()) {
            return Ok(Tried::Later);
        }
        if p.follow_ups.deciding(&topic) {
            return Ok(Tried::Deciding);
        }
        let thread = p.store.list_thread(&topic).await?;
        if thread.iter().any(|r| !r.status.is_terminal()) {
            tracing::debug!(wake = %wake.id, "topic busy: the wake waits");
            return Ok(Tried::Busy);
        }
        let end = thread.last().unwrap_or(&first);
        let mut new = crate::checkins::continuation(&first, end, wake.message.clone(), None);
        if let Some(payload) = new.payload.as_mut() {
            payload[WAKE_ID] = wake.id.clone().into();
        }
        let Some(run) = p.store.deliver_making_wake(&wake.id, &new).await? else {
            return Ok(Tried::Done);
        };
        drop(one_at_a_time);
        tracing::info!(wake = %wake.id, run = %run.id, "a maker was woken");
        p.runner.enqueued(&run);
        Ok(Tried::Delivered)
    }

    /// Runs the wakes' loop until `shutdown`, or until the runtime that made the makers is
    /// gone: a pass at once, for the wakes that waited across a restart, then one after the end
    /// of each run, which is what frees a topic. After a pass that failed, or that left a wake
    /// waiting for a topic that is adding an app, the next comes after `ERROR_WAIT` at the
    /// latest. It does not keep the makers alive.
    pub(crate) fn spawn_wakes(&self, shutdown: CancellationToken) -> JoinHandle<()> {
        let makers = self.downgrade();
        // Subscribed before the first pass, so no end of a run is missed.
        let mut events = self.parts.bus.subscribe();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            loop {
                let Some(this) = makers.upgrade() else { break };
                let again = match this.wake_pass().await {
                    Ok(again) => again,
                    Err(e) => {
                        tracing::error!("wake loop error: {e}");
                        true
                    }
                };
                drop(this);
                let wait = async {
                    if again {
                        tokio::time::sleep(ERROR_WAIT.to_std().unwrap_or_default()).await
                    } else {
                        std::future::pending().await
                    }
                };
                tokio::select! {
                    biased;
                    _ = shutdown.cancelled() => break,
                    open = run_ended(&mut events) => if !open { break },
                    _ = wait => {}
                }
            }
        })
    }
}

/// Returns `true` when a run has ended (its `RunUpdated`) or when events were lost and one may
/// have; `false` when no more events come.
async fn run_ended(events: &mut tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver<RuntimeEvent>) -> bool {
    loop {
        match events.recv().await {
            Ok(RuntimeEvent::RunUpdated { run }) if run.status.is_terminal() => return true,
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(RecvError::Lagged(_)) => return true,
            Err(RecvError::Closed) => return false,
        }
    }
}
```
