```rust
//! Jobs (dots-make-dots design section 8): a maker gives a job to a dot it made, which starts a
//! chat run of that dot, and is woken once when the job ends. One job covers the run it starts,
//! the runs that resume that run after approvals, and, when a run ends its turn by asking the
//! person a question, the run that carries their answer, and so on until a run ends with no
//! question waiting. Follow-ups the made dot schedules for later are not part of it.
//!
//! A job is followed from the store alone (`Makers::settle_jobs`): each pass reads where every
//! open job's last run stands and moves, parks or ends the job. So nothing is lost when Dots
//! restarts or an event is missed, and a pass may run any number of times.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::json;

use super::log::{MakingEventKind, NewMakingEvent};
use super::service::{Makers, MAX_JOB};
use crate::limits::{run_is_background, BACKGROUND, STOPPED_BY_LIMIT};
use crate::model::{Dot, NewRun, Run, RunStatus, TriggerKind};
use crate::prompt::{is_typed, JOB_FROM};
use crate::spend::STOPPED_BY_CAP;
use crate::util::new_id;
use crate::{Error, Result};

/// The most characters of a job's final text a wake carries (design section 8); a longer one
/// is cut there, with `RESULT_CUT` after it.
pub const MAX_JOB_RESULT: usize = 8000;
/// The most jobs given in one chat topic of a maker between two messages the person typed
/// (design section 8, the loop guard). First jobs count.
pub const MAX_JOBS_BETWEEN_TYPED: u32 = 6;
/// The key of a job run's payload that holds the job's id: the run's message is a maker's, not
/// one the person typed.
pub const JOB_ID: &str = "job_id";
/// What `give_job` is told for a job that is not 1 to `MAX_JOB` characters.
pub const JOB_RULE: &str = "The job is 1 to 4000 characters.";
/// What follows a final text that was cut at `MAX_JOB_RESULT` characters.
pub const RESULT_CUT: &str = "[cut: the full text is in the run]";
/// What a wake says of a job whose last run left no final text.
pub const NO_FINAL_TEXT: &str = "It left no final message.";
/// What `list_made_dots` says of a made dot with an open job from the conversation that asks.
pub const JOB_WORKING: &str = "working on a job from this conversation";
/// What `list_made_dots` says of a made dot whose job from the conversation that asks waits
/// for the person's answer.
pub const JOB_WAITING: &str = "waiting for the person's answer";
/// What a first job that started adds to the tool's text and to the wake with the person's
/// answer (design sections 7.1 and 7.2).
pub const FIRST_JOB_STARTED: &str =
    " Its first job has started; you will be woken with the result.";

/// The most characters of a failed run's error a wake carries.
const MAX_ERROR: usize = 300;
/// The most runs one pass follows a job through: far more than a turn has.
const MAX_HOPS: usize = 200;

str_enum!(JobStatus {
    // Its run is queued, running or awaiting an approval.
    Working => "working",
    // Its last run ended with a question waiting for the person.
    WaitingAnswer => "waiting_answer",
    // It ended; the maker's wake is stored.
    Ended => "ended",
});

str_enum!(JobEnd {
    // Its last run finished.
    Succeeded => "succeeded",
    // Its last run failed: an error, the time limit, a spending cap, Claude's usage limit.
    Failed => "failed",
    // The person stopped its run, or dismissed the question it waited on.
    Cancelled => "cancelled",
    // Its maker deleted the made dot before it ended.
    Deleted => "deleted",
});

/// One job, as stored.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct MakingJob {
    pub id: String,
    /// The maker that gave it.
    pub maker_dot_id: String,
    /// The maker's run that gave it; for a first job, the run that asked for the dot.
    pub maker_run_id: String,
    /// The maker's chat topic it was given in, where its cards show and the wake goes.
    pub maker_root_run_id: String,
    /// The made dot.
    pub dot_id: String,
    /// The made dot's chat topic the job runs in, as it was when the job started.
    pub dot_root_run_id: Option<String>,
    /// The run the job started.
    pub first_run_id: Option<String>,
    /// The run the job is at: it moves forward as the job goes on.
    pub last_run_id: Option<String>,
    pub message: String,
    pub status: JobStatus,
    /// How it ended; `None` until it has.
    pub ended_how: Option<JobEnd>,
    pub created_at: String,
    pub ended_at: Option<String>,
    /// The wake that tells the maker, stored when the job ends.
    pub wake_id: Option<String>,
}

/// Input for `Store::start_making_job`. The job is stored `working`, as of now.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct NewMakingJob<'a> {
    /// The job's id, made beforehand: its run's payload names it.
    pub id: &'a str,
    pub maker_dot_id: &'a str,
    pub maker_run_id: &'a str,
    pub maker_root_run_id: &'a str,
    pub dot_id: &'a str,
    pub message: &'a str,
}

/// What came of the first job given with a dot (design sections 7.1 and 8). The dot is made
/// either way.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]
pub enum FirstJob {
    Started(MakingJob),
    /// Why it was not started, in a sentence for the maker: the loop guard, or what failed.
    NotStarted(String),
}

impl FirstJob {
    /// What it adds to the tool's text and to the wake with the person's answer: it starts
    /// with a space.
    pub fn sentence(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::Started(_) => FIRST_JOB_STARTED.to_string(),
            Self::NotStarted(why) => format!(" Its first job was not started: {why}"),
        }
    }
}

/// What the job past the loop guard is told (design section 8). `maker` is the maker's name.
pub fn guard_refusal(maker: &str) -> String {
    format!(
        "{maker} has given {MAX_JOBS_BETWEEN_TYPED} jobs since the person last wrote here. Stop \
         and report to the person what is done and what is left; they can tell you to carry on."
    )
}

/// What `give_job` tells the maker's run when the job was taken (design section 8).
pub fn gave_text(dot: &str) -> String {
    format!(
        "Gave the job to \"{dot}\". It has started (or waits behind its current run). Do not \
         wait for it: carry on with other work or end your turn, and you will be woken with its \
         result."
    )
}

/// What a wake says of a job whose made dot the maker deleted before it ended.
pub fn deleted_message(dot: &str) -> String {
    format!("\"{dot}\" was deleted before the job ended.")
}

/// How a job whose last run is `run`, which has ended, ended: for the store, in words for the
/// maker, and whether the run's error says more than the words do.
fn run_end(run: &Run) -> (JobEnd, &'static str, bool) {
    let error = run.error.as_deref().unwrap_or_default();
    match run.status {
        RunStatus::Cancelled => (JobEnd::Cancelled, "was stopped", false),
        RunStatus::Failed if run.quiet_stopped => {
            (JobEnd::Failed, "was stopped after it went quiet", false)
        }
        RunStatus::Failed if error.starts_with(STOPPED_BY_CAP) => {
            (JobEnd::Failed, "was stopped by a spend cap", false)
        }
        RunStatus::Failed if error.starts_with(STOPPED_BY_LIMIT) => {
            (JobEnd::Failed, "was stopped by Claude's usage limit", false)
        }
        RunStatus::Failed => (JobEnd::Failed, "failed", true),
        // A run that parked on an approval the person refused ends as succeeded too.
        _ => (JobEnd::Succeeded, "finished the job", false),
    }
}

/// What the maker is woken with when a job ends (design section 8): the made dot's name and
/// how the job ended, a failed run's `error` cut short, then the last run's final text, cut at
/// `MAX_JOB_RESULT` characters with a note, or that there is none.
pub fn ended_message(
    dot: &str,
    how: &str,
    error: Option<&str>,
    final_text: Option<&str>,
) -> String {
    let mut message = format!("\"{dot}\" {how}.");
    let error = error
        .map(|e| e.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" "))
        .filter(|e| !e.is_empty());
    if let Some(error) = error {
        message.push_str(" The error: ");
        message.extend(error.chars().take(MAX_ERROR));
        if error.chars().count() > MAX_ERROR {
            message.push('…');
        }
    }
    message.push_str("\n\n");
    match final_text.map(str::trim).filter(|text| !text.is_empty()) {
        Some(text) => {
            message.push_str("Its final message:\n");
            message.extend(text.chars().take(MAX_JOB_RESULT));
            if text.chars().count() > MAX_JOB_RESULT {
                message.push('\n');
                message.push_str(RESULT_CUT);
            }
        }
        None => message.push_str(NO_FINAL_TEXT),
    }
    message
}

impl Makers {
    /// A maker's run gives a job to a dot it made (design section 8). `run_id` is the run that
    /// calls; its dot is the maker. `dot_name` names the made dot, in any letter case.
    /// Returns what the tool tells the run, at once: the job's run is queued, and the maker is
    /// woken when the job ends.
    ///
    /// An error, with a sentence the model can act on: what `make_dot` refuses a run for, a
    /// dot the maker did not make (the same sentence for any other dot), a job that is not 1 to
    /// 4,000 characters, a made dot that is switched off, and what `start_job` refuses.
    pub async fn give_job(&self, run_id: &str, dot_name: &str, message: &str) -> Result<String> {
        let p = &self.parts;
        let (run, maker) = self.caller(run_id).await?;
        // With the makes: two jobs of one run cannot both take the last place of the guard.
        let _one_at_a_time = p.one_at_a_time.lock().await;
        let made = self.made_dot(&maker, dot_name).await?;
        let message = message.trim();
        if message.is_empty() || message.chars().count() > MAX_JOB {
            return Err(Error::Invalid(JOB_RULE.into()));
        }
        // A chat run of a dot that is off would start as any other: the person switched it
        // off, so a maker does not run it.
        if !made.spec.enabled {
            return Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                "\"{}\" is switched off. The person turns it on.",
                made.spec.name
            )));
        }
        self.start_job(&maker, &run.id, &run.root_run_id, &made, message)
            .await?;
        Ok(gave_text(&made.spec.name))
    }

    /// Starts a job for the dot `made` of `maker`, given by the maker's run `maker_run_id` in
    /// its chat topic `maker_root_run_id`: for `give_job`, and for a first job when `make_dot`
    /// or an allowed request carried one. `message` is trimmed and within `MAX_JOB`. The caller
    /// holds the service's lock, so the guard's count and the new job are one step.
    ///
    /// The job's run is a chat run of the made dot that is not typed; its payload names the
    /// job (`JOB_ID`) and the maker (`prompt::JOB_FROM`), so its prompt says who sent it. It is
    /// background for the usage holds when the maker's run was (`limits::BACKGROUND`). Jobs
    /// from one topic of the maker go to one topic of the made dot: the run goes on where the
    /// last job from this topic ended, as the person's next message there would; when there is
    /// none, or that topic is gone or busy with something else, it starts a topic of its own.
    /// The run, the job and the `job_started` entry of the log are stored in one transaction,
    /// under the thread lock every writer that continues a chat holds.
    ///
    /// Refused (`Invalid`) for the job past the loop guard, and while the last job from this
    /// topic to this dot has not ended: a topic is one line of runs, so the next job cannot be
    /// queued behind it. Refused (`NotAllowed`) when this PC's role may not run the made dot.
    pub(crate) async fn start_job(
        &self,
        maker: &Dot,
        maker_run_id: &str,
        maker_root_run_id: &str,
        made: &Dot,
        message: &str,
    ) -> Result<MakingJob> {
        let p = &self.parts;
        let name = &made.spec.name;
        if self.jobs_since_typed(maker_root_run_id).await? >= MAX_JOBS_BETWEEN_TYPED {
            return Err(Error::Invalid(guard_refusal(&maker.spec.name)));
        }
        p.runner.require_run(made).await?;
        // As the maker's run counted; a run that is gone gave the job in the person's sight.
        let background = match p.store.get_run(maker_run_id).await {
            Ok(run) => run_is_background(&run),
            Err(Error::NotFound(_)) => false,
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        };
        let lock = p.follow_ups.thread_lock();
        let one_thread = lock.lock().await;
        let earlier = p
            .store
            .latest_making_job(maker_root_run_id, &made.id)
            .await?;
        match earlier.as_ref().map(|job| job.status) {
            Some(JobStatus::Working) => {
                return Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                    "\"{name}\" is still working on the last job from this conversation. You \
                     will be woken when it ends."
                )))
            }
            Some(JobStatus::WaitingAnswer) => {
                return Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                    "\"{name}\" is waiting for the person's answer on the last job from this \
                     conversation. You will be woken when it ends."
                )))
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        let mut new = match self.topic_to_go_on(made, earlier.as_ref()).await? {
            Some((first, end)) => {
                crate::checkins::continuation(&first, &end, message.to_string(), None)
            }
            None => {
                let mut new = NewRun::new(&made.id, TriggerKind::Chat);
                new.payload = Some(json!({ "message": message }));
                new
            }
        };
        let id = new_id();
        if let Some(payload) = new.payload.as_mut() {
            payload[JOB_ID] = id.clone().into();
            payload[JOB_FROM] = maker.spec.name.clone().into();
            if background {
                payload[BACKGROUND] = true.into();
            }
        }
        let job = NewMakingJob {
            id: &id,
            maker_dot_id: &maker.id,
            maker_run_id,
            maker_root_run_id,
            dot_id: &made.id,
            message,
        };
        let (job, run) = p.store.start_making_job(&job, name, &new).await?;
        drop(one_thread);
        tracing::info!(job = %job.id, run = %run.id, maker = %maker.id, "a job was given");
        p.runner.enqueued(&run);
        self.updated(&maker.id, maker_root_run_id);
        Ok(job)
    }

    /// The first job given with the dot `made`, started when it is given: what came of it, or
    /// `None` without one. The dot stays made whatever comes of the job.
    pub(super) async fn start_first_job(
        &self,
        maker: &Dot,
        maker_run_id: &str,
        maker_root_run_id: &str,
        made: &Dot,
        message: Option<&str>,
    ) -> Option<FirstJob> {
        let message = message?.trim();
        let started = self
            .start_job(maker, maker_run_id, maker_root_run_id, made, message)
            .await;
        Some(match started {
            Ok(job) => FirstJob::Started(job),
            Err(Error::Invalid(why) | Error::Conflict(why) | Error::NotAllowed(why)) => {
                FirstJob::NotStarted(why)
            }
            Err(e) => {
                tracing::warn!(dot = %made.id, run = %maker_run_id, "the first job was not started: {e}");
                FirstJob::NotStarted(format!("{e}. Give it the job with give_job."))
            }
        })
    }

    /// How many jobs were started in the maker's chat topic `root_run_id` since the person
    /// last typed a message in it (design section 8): since the newest run of the topic that
    /// carries a typed message was queued, or since the topic's start when it has none, as a
    /// topic a schedule or another background trigger started. Answers to questions and to
    /// cards, and wakes, are not typed.
    async fn jobs_since_typed(&self, root_run_id: &str) -> Result<u32> {
        let store = &self.parts.store;
        let thread = store.list_thread(root_run_id).await?;
        let since = thread
            .iter()
            .filter(|run| is_typed(run))
            .map(|run| run.queued_at.as_str())
            .max();
        store.count_jobs_started(root_run_id, since).await
    }

    /// The topic of `made` the next job from a topic of the maker goes on in, as its first run
    /// and its end: the topic the job `earlier`, the last from there, ran in, while that topic
    /// exists, is the made dot's, has no run going and is not adding an app. The caller holds
    /// the thread lock.
    async fn topic_to_go_on(
        &self,
        made: &Dot,
        earlier: Option<&MakingJob>,
    ) -> Result<Option<(Run, Run)>> {
        let p = &self.parts;
        let Some(topic) = earlier.and_then(|job| job.dot_root_run_id.as_deref()) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        // The topic that run is in now: the person may have moved it since.
        let first = match p.store.get_run(topic).await {
            Ok(run) if run.dot_id == made.id => run,
            Ok(_) | Err(Error::NotFound(_)) => return Ok(None),
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        };
        if p.follow_ups.deciding(&first.root_run_id) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let mut thread = p.store.list_thread(&first.root_run_id).await?;
        if thread.iter().any(|run| !run.status.is_terminal()) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let end = thread.pop().unwrap_or_else(|| first.clone());
        Ok(Some((first, end)))
    }

    /// Follows every job that has not ended (design section 8). Called when a run ends, when
    /// the person answers or dismisses a question, at startup, and by tests. For each open job,
    /// by where its last run stands:
    ///
    /// - It has not ended (queued, running, awaiting an approval): nothing.
    /// - It ended and a run goes on with its work in the same turn (`Store::run_continued_by`):
    ///   the job moves to that run.
    /// - It ended and the newest question a run of the job asked waits for the person: the job
    ///   waits (`waiting_answer`, a `job_waiting` entry), and the maker is not woken.
    /// - That question was answered by a run the job has not been at: the job moves to it.
    /// - That question was dismissed: the job ends as stopped.
    /// - Otherwise the job ends as its last run did.
    ///
    /// Ending a job stores its wake in the same transaction (`Store::end_making_job`), so of
    /// any number of passes one ends it and the maker is woken once. One pass runs at a time.
    /// The error of the first job that could not be followed is returned after the others were.
    pub async fn settle_jobs(&self) -> Result<()> {
        let p = &self.parts;
        let mut ended = false;
        let mut failed = None;
        {
            let _one_pass = p.settling.lock().await;
            for job in p.store.open_making_jobs(None).await? {
                let id = job.id.clone();
                match self.settle_job(job).await {
                    Ok(has_ended) => ended |= has_ended,
                    Err(e) => {
                        tracing::warn!(job = %id, "the job could not be followed: {e}");
                        failed.get_or_insert(e);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // After the pass's lock is released: delivery takes the thread lock.
        if ended {
            if let Err(e) = self.deliver_wakes().await {
                tracing::warn!("a job's wake waits; delivering it failed: {e}");
            }
        }
        match failed {
            Some(e) => Err(e),
            None => Ok(()),
        }
    }

    /// One open job of a pass (`settle_jobs`). `true` when it ended here.
    async fn settle_job(&self, mut job: MakingJob) -> Result<bool> {
        let store = &self.parts.store;
        let dot = match store.get_dot(&job.dot_id).await {
            Ok(dot) => dot,
            // The made dot went since the list was read, and the job with it.
            Err(Error::NotFound(_)) => return Ok(false),
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        };
        let name = dot.spec.name.as_str();
        for _ in 0..MAX_HOPS {
            let last = match job.last_run_id.as_deref() {
                Some(id) => match store.get_run(id).await {
                    Ok(run) => Some(run),
                    Err(Error::NotFound(_)) => None,
                    Err(e) => return Err(e),
                },
                None => None,
            };
            let Some(last) = last else {
                // Runs go only with their dot, and the job with them; kept so that a job
                // without a run still ends.
                let gone = ended_message(name, "failed", Some("its run no longer exists"), None);
                return self.end_job(&job, name, JobEnd::Failed, &gone).await;
            };
            if !last.status.is_terminal() {
                return Ok(false);
            }
            if let Some(next) = store.run_continued_by(&last.id).await? {
                if !store.move_making_job(&job.id, &last.id, &next.id).await? {
                    return Ok(false);
                }
                job.last_run_id = Some(next.id);
                job.status = JobStatus::Working;
                continue;
            }
            // The questions of the job's runs: those the topic's runs asked since the job's
            // first run was queued.
            let since = match job.first_run_id.as_deref() {
                Some(id) => store.get_run(id).await.ok().map(|run| run.queued_at),
                None => None,
            }
            .unwrap_or_else(|| job.created_at.clone());
            let asked = store
                .latest_question_since(&last.root_run_id, &since)
                .await?;
            let final_text = last.summary.as_deref();
            match asked {
                Some(question) if question.waits() => {
                    if job.status == JobStatus::Working
                        && store.set_making_job_waiting(&job.id).await?
                    {
                        let detail = json!({ "job_id": job.id, "run_id": last.id });
                        self.log_job(
                            &job,
                            MakingEventKind::JobWaiting,
                            Some(&dot.id),
                            name,
                            detail,
                        )
                        .await;
                    }
                    return Ok(false);
                }
                Some(question) if question.dismissed_at.is_some() => {
                    // Nothing can answer it any more, so nothing would end the job.
                    let said = ended_message(name, "was stopped", None, final_text);
                    return self.end_job(&job, name, JobEnd::Cancelled, &said).await;
                }
                Some(question) => {
                    let answer = match question.answer_run_id.as_deref() {
                        Some(id) if !self.was_at(&last, id).await? => store.get_run(id).await.ok(),
                        _ => None,
                    };
                    if let Some(answer) = answer {
                        if !store.move_making_job(&job.id, &last.id, &answer.id).await? {
                            return Ok(false);
                        }
                        job.last_run_id = Some(answer.id);
                        job.status = JobStatus::Working;
                        continue;
                    }
                }
                None => {}
            }
            let (how, words, with_error) = run_end(&last);
            let error = last.error.as_deref().filter(|_| with_error);
            let said = ended_message(name, words, error, final_text);
            return self.end_job(&job, name, how, &said).await;
        }
        Err(Error::Other(format!(
            "job {} went through {MAX_HOPS} runs in one pass",
            job.id
        )))
    }

    /// Whether the job that is at the run `last` has been at the run `run_id`: `last` itself,
    /// or a run before it in its line. A run that sends a message again comes after the run
    /// whose message it sends (`retry_of`); any other after its parent.
    async fn was_at(&self, last: &Run, run_id: &str) -> Result<bool> {
        let store = &self.parts.store;
        let mut at = last.clone();
        for _ in 0..MAX_HOPS {
            if at.id == run_id {
                return Ok(true);
            }
            let Some(before) = at.retry_of.clone().or(at.parent_run_id.clone()) else {
                return Ok(false);
            };
            at = match store.get_run(&before).await {
                Ok(run) => run,
                Err(Error::NotFound(_)) => return Ok(false),
                Err(e) => return Err(e),
            };
        }
        Ok(false)
    }

    /// Ends the open `job` of the made dot named `dot_name` as `how` and stores the wake that
    /// tells the maker `said`, then writes the `job_ended` entry of the log. `false` when
    /// another pass had ended it.
    async fn end_job(
        &self,
        job: &MakingJob,
        dot_name: &str,
        how: JobEnd,
        said: &str,
    ) -> Result<bool> {
        let store = &self.parts.store;
        let Some(ended) = store.end_making_job(&job.id, how, said).await? else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        tracing::info!(job = %job.id, how = how.as_str(), "a job ended");
        let detail = json!({
            "job_id": ended.id,
            "run_id": ended.last_run_id,
            "how": how.as_str(),
        });
        self.log_job(
            &ended,
            MakingEventKind::JobEnded,
            Some(&ended.dot_id),
            dot_name,
            detail,
        )
        .await;
        Ok(true)
    }

    /// Writes an entry about `job` to the log of the maker's topic it was given in, as the
    /// run's that gave it, and publishes `MakingUpdated`. The job stands as it is whether or
    /// not the entry could be written, so a failure is only logged.
    pub(super) async fn log_job(
        &self,
        job: &MakingJob,
        kind: MakingEventKind,
        dot_id: Option<&str>,
        dot_name: &str,
        detail: serde_json::Value,
    ) {
        let logged = self
            .parts
            .store
            .add_making_event(&NewMakingEvent {
                maker_dot_id: &job.maker_dot_id,
                run_id: &job.maker_run_id,
                root_run_id: &job.maker_root_run_id,
                kind,
                dot_id,
                dot_name,
                detail,
            })
            .await;
        if let Err(e) = logged {
            tracing::error!(job = %job.id, kind = kind.as_str(), "the job's entry was not logged: {e}");
        }
        self.updated(&job.maker_dot_id, &job.maker_root_run_id);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn ended_run(status: RunStatus, error: Option<&str>, quiet_stopped: bool) -> Run {
        serde_json::from_value(json!({
            "id": "R", "dot_id": "D", "root_run_id": "R", "parent_run_id": null,
            "trigger": "chat", "payload": null, "status": status.as_str(),
            "session_id": null, "workspace_path": null, "branch": null, "base_commit": null,
            "summary": null, "error": error, "tokens_in": 0, "tokens_out": 0,
            "queued_at": "2026-11-11T09:00:00.000Z", "started_at": null, "ended_at": null,
            "reviewed_at": null, "retry_of": null, "cost_usd": null, "hold_released": false,
            "workflow_step_run_id": null, "tokens_cache_read": 0, "quiet_since": null,
            "quiet_limit_secs": null, "quiet_stopped": quiet_stopped,
        }))
        .unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn each_way_a_run_ends_has_its_words() {
        let cases = [
            (
                RunStatus::Succeeded,
                None,
                false,
                JobEnd::Succeeded,
                "finished the job",
                false,
            ),
            (
                RunStatus::Cancelled,
                None,
                false,
                JobEnd::Cancelled,
                "was stopped",
                false,
            ),
            (
                RunStatus::Failed,
                Some("boom"),
                false,
                JobEnd::Failed,
                "failed",
                true,
            ),
            (
                RunStatus::Failed,
                Some("timeout after 600s"),
                false,
                JobEnd::Failed,
                "failed",
                true,
            ),
            (
                RunStatus::Failed,
                Some("stopped: Blog Watcher reached its $1.00 daily cap"),
                false,
                JobEnd::Failed,
                "was stopped by a spend cap",
                false,
            ),
            (
                RunStatus::Failed,
                Some("stopped: no output for 20 min"),
                true,
                JobEnd::Failed,
                "was stopped after it went quiet",
                false,
            ),
            (
                RunStatus::Failed,
                Some("stopped by Claude's usage limit: rejected"),
                false,
                JobEnd::Failed,
                "was stopped by Claude's usage limit",
                false,
            ),
        ];
        for (status, error, quiet, how, words, with_error) in cases {
            let run = ended_run(status, error, quiet);
            assert_eq!(
                run_end(&run),
                (how, words, with_error),
                "{status:?} {error:?}"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_wake_names_the_dot_how_it_ended_and_its_final_text() {
        assert_eq!(
            ended_message(
                "Blog Watcher",
                "finished the job",
                None,
                Some("  Three new posts.\n")
            ),
            "\"Blog Watcher\" finished the job.\n\nIts final message:\nThree new posts."
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ended_message("Blog Watcher", "was stopped", None, Some("  ")),
            "\"Blog Watcher\" was stopped.\n\nIt left no final message."
        );
        // An error is one line, cut short.
        let long = format!("first line\nsecond {}", "x".repeat(400));
        let said = ended_message("Blog Watcher", "failed", Some(&long), None);
        let error = format!("first line second {}", "x".repeat(400));
        let cut: String = error.chars().take(300).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            said,
            format!("\"Blog Watcher\" failed. The error: {cut}…\n\nIt left no final message.")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ended_message("Blog Watcher", "failed", Some(" "), None),
            "\"Blog Watcher\" failed.\n\nIt left no final message."
        );
    }
}
```

```rust
/// The key `Makers::start_job` sets in a chat run's payload: the run carries a job a maker gave

         to {maker}."
```

```rust
const JOB_COLUMNS: &str = "id, maker_dot_id, maker_run_id, maker_root_run_id, dot_id, \
     dot_root_run_id, first_run_id, last_run_id, message, status, ended_how, created_at, \
     ended_at, wake_id";

fn job_from_row(row: &SqliteRow) -> Result<MakingJob> {
    let ended_how: Option<String> = row.try_get("ended_how")?;
    Ok(MakingJob {
        id: row.try_get("id")?,
        maker_dot_id: row.try_get("maker_dot_id")?,
        maker_run_id: row.try_get("maker_run_id")?,
        maker_root_run_id: row.try_get("maker_root_run_id")?,
        dot_id: row.try_get("dot_id")?,
        dot_root_run_id: row.try_get("dot_root_run_id")?,
        first_run_id: row.try_get("first_run_id")?,
        last_run_id: row.try_get("last_run_id")?,
        message: row.try_get("message")?,
        status: JobStatus::parse(&row.try_get::<String, _>("status")?)?,
        ended_how: ended_how.as_deref().map(JobEnd::parse).transpose()?,
        created_at: row.try_get("created_at")?,
        ended_at: row.try_get("ended_at")?,
        wake_id: row.try_get("wake_id")?,
    })
}

/// The jobs makers give to the dots they made (dots-make-dots design section 8).
impl Store {
    /// Starts a job: stores `run`, the made dot's run that carries it, the job itself, at that
    /// run and `working`, and the `job_started` entry of the maker's log, in one transaction.
    /// So a job has its run from the start, and the log, which the loop guard counts, has every
    /// job that was started. `new.id` is the job's id, which the run's payload names already;
    /// `dot_name` is the made dot's name, for the log. Returns the job and its run.
    pub async fn start_making_job(
        &self,
        new: &NewMakingJob<'_>,
        dot_name: &str,
        run: &NewRun,
    ) -> Result<(MakingJob, Run)> {
        let created_at = now();
        let mut tx = self.pool.begin().await?;
        let run_id = insert_run(&mut tx, run).await?;
        let root = run.root_run_id.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| run_id.clone());
        sqlx::query(&format!(
            "INSERT INTO making_jobs ({JOB_COLUMNS}) \
             VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, ?, NULL, NULL)"
        ))
        .bind(new.id)
        .bind(new.maker_dot_id)
        .bind(new.maker_run_id)
        .bind(new.maker_root_run_id)
        .bind(new.dot_id)
        .bind(&root)
        .bind(&run_id)
        .bind(&run_id)
        .bind(new.message)
        .bind(JobStatus::Working.as_str())
        .bind(&created_at)
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?;
        let detail = serde_json::json!({
            "job_id": new.id,
            "message": new.message,
            "run_id": run_id,
        });
        sqlx::query(&format!(
            "INSERT INTO making_events ({COLUMNS}) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)"
        ))
        .bind(new_id())
        .bind(new.maker_dot_id)
        .bind(new.maker_run_id)
        .bind(new.maker_root_run_id)
        .bind(MakingEventKind::JobStarted.as_str())
        .bind(new.dot_id)
        .bind(dot_name)
        .bind(detail.to_string())
        .bind(&created_at)
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?;
        tx.commit().await?;
        Ok((
            self.get_making_job(new.id).await?,
            self.get_run(&run_id).await?,
        ))
    }

    /// The job `id`, ended or not.
    pub async fn get_making_job(&self, id: &str) -> Result<MakingJob> {
        let row = sqlx::query(&format!(
            "SELECT {JOB_COLUMNS} FROM making_jobs WHERE id = ?"
        ))
        .bind(id)
        .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
        .await?
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::NotFound(format!("job {id}")))?;
        job_from_row(&row)
    }

    /// The jobs given in the maker's chat topic `maker_root_run_id`, oldest first; of two
    /// stored in the same millisecond, the one stored first comes first (`rowid`).
    pub async fn making_jobs_of_topic(&self, maker_root_run_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<MakingJob>> {
        let rows = sqlx::query(&format!(
            "SELECT {JOB_COLUMNS} FROM making_jobs WHERE maker_root_run_id = ? \
             ORDER BY created_at, rowid"
        ))
        .bind(maker_root_run_id)
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        rows.iter().map(job_from_row).collect()
    }

    /// The jobs that have not ended, of every maker, oldest first; with `dot_id`, only those
    /// given to that made dot.
    pub async fn open_making_jobs(&self, dot_id: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<MakingJob>> {
        let rows = sqlx::query(&format!(
            "SELECT {JOB_COLUMNS} FROM making_jobs \
             WHERE status != 'ended' AND (?1 IS NULL OR dot_id = ?1) ORDER BY created_at, rowid"
        ))
        .bind(dot_id)
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        rows.iter().map(job_from_row).collect()
    }

    /// The newest job given to the made dot `dot_id` in the maker's chat topic
    /// `maker_root_run_id`, ended or not: the next job from that topic goes on in its topic of
    /// the made dot (dots-make-dots design section 8).
    pub async fn latest_making_job(
        &self,
        maker_root_run_id: &str,
        dot_id: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<MakingJob>> {
        let row = sqlx::query(&format!(
            "SELECT {JOB_COLUMNS} FROM making_jobs WHERE maker_root_run_id = ? AND dot_id = ? \
             ORDER BY created_at DESC, rowid DESC LIMIT 1"
        ))
        .bind(maker_root_run_id)
        .bind(dot_id)
        .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        row.as_ref().map(job_from_row).transpose()
    }

    /// How many jobs were started in the maker's chat topic `maker_root_run_id` at or after
    /// `since`, or ever with `None`: what the loop guard counts (dots-make-dots design section
    /// 8). It counts the log, not the jobs, so a job whose made dot was deleted still counts.
    pub async fn count_jobs_started(
        &self,
        maker_root_run_id: &str,
        since: Option<&str>,
    ) -> Result<u32> {
        let n: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM making_events WHERE root_run_id = ?1 \
             AND kind = 'job_started' AND (?2 IS NULL OR created_at >= ?2)",
        )
        .bind(maker_root_run_id)
        .bind(since)
        .fetch_one(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        Ok(n as u32)
    }

    /// Moves the open job `id` on from its run `from` to the run `to`, which continues it, and
    /// marks it `working`. `false`, with nothing written, when the job has ended or is no
    /// longer at `from`.
    pub async fn move_making_job(&self, id: &str, from: &str, to: &str) -> Result<bool> {
        let res = sqlx::query(
            "UPDATE making_jobs SET last_run_id = ?, status = 'working' \
             WHERE id = ? AND status != 'ended' AND last_run_id = ?",
        )
        .bind(to)
        .bind(id)
        .bind(from)
        .execute(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        Ok(res.rows_affected() > 0)
    }

    /// Marks the working job `id` as waiting for the person's answer. `false`, with nothing
    /// written, when it was not `working`.
    pub async fn set_making_job_waiting(&self, id: &str) -> Result<bool> {
        let res = sqlx::query(
            "UPDATE making_jobs SET status = 'waiting_answer' WHERE id = ? AND status = 'working'",
        )
        .bind(id)
        .execute(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        Ok(res.rows_affected() > 0)
    }

    /// Ends the open job `id` as `how` and stores the wake that tells its maker, `message`
    /// for the maker's topic the job was given in, in one transaction: a job that has ended
    /// has exactly one wake. The guarded update goes first, so of two that end one job the
    /// second finds it ended. `None`, with nothing written, when the job had ended or is gone.
    pub async fn end_making_job(
        &self,
        id: &str,
        how: JobEnd,
        message: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<MakingJob>> {
        let ended_at = now();
        let wake_id = new_id();
        let mut tx = self.pool.begin().await?;
        let res = sqlx::query(
            "UPDATE making_jobs SET status = 'ended', ended_how = ?, ended_at = ?, wake_id = ? \
             WHERE id = ? AND status != 'ended'",
        )
        .bind(how.as_str())
        .bind(&ended_at)
        .bind(&wake_id)
        .bind(id)
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?;
        if res.rows_affected() == 0 {
            tx.rollback().await?;
            return Ok(None);
        }
        sqlx::query(
            "INSERT INTO making_wakes (id, maker_dot_id, root_run_id, message, created_at) \
             SELECT ?, maker_dot_id, maker_root_run_id, ?, ? FROM making_jobs WHERE id = ?",
        )
        .bind(&wake_id)
        .bind(message)
        .bind(&ended_at)
        .bind(id)
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?;
        tx.commit().await?;
        self.get_making_job(id).await.map(Some)
    }

    /// The run that goes on with the work of the ended run `run_id` in the same turn, if there
    /// is one: the run that resumes it after an approval (`resume_parked` stores it as it
    /// closes the parked run), or the run that sends its message again (`retry_of`). The
    /// newest, when a message was sent again more than once.
    pub async fn run_continued_by(&self, run_id: &str) -> Result<Option<Run>> {
        let row = sqlx::query(&format!(
            "SELECT {RUN_COLUMNS} FROM runs \
             WHERE (parent_run_id = ?1 AND trigger_kind = 'resume') OR retry_of = ?1 \
             ORDER BY queued_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1"
        ))
        .bind(run_id)
        .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        row.as_ref().map(run_from_row).transpose()
    }

    /// The newest question a run of the chat topic `root_run_id` asked the person, among the
    /// runs queued at or after `since`: the question a job that runs in that topic since then
    /// waits on, answered, dismissed or open.
    pub async fn latest_question_since(
        &self,
        root_run_id: &str,
        since: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<Message>> {
        let id: Option<String> = sqlx::query_scalar(
            "SELECT m.id FROM messages m JOIN runs r ON r.id = m.run_id \
             WHERE m.kind = 'question' AND r.root_run_id = ? AND r.queued_at >= ? \
             ORDER BY m.created_at DESC, m.rowid DESC LIMIT 1",
        )
        .bind(root_run_id)
        .bind(since)
        .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        match id {
            Some(id) => self.get_message(&id).await.map(Some),
            None => Ok(None),
        }
    }
}
```

### Task 10: A made dot's spend counts toward its makers' caps and survives its deletion

A run of a dot is held or stopped when its own cap is reached by its shared total (its own runs, the runs of the living dots below it, and what was kept for it), or when any maker's cap up the chain is reached by that maker's shared total (spec section 6). Deleting a dot writes its runs' spend for the month so far into `made_spend_kept` for every maker above it, in the transaction that deletes it, so a delete never lowers a cap's total.

- Test: `crates/dots-core/tests/making_spend_test.rs`

**Create `crates/dots-core/tests/making_spend_test.rs`:**

```rust
//! Shared spend (dots-make-dots design section 6, Spend; proof 10 of section 13): what a made dot
//! spends counts toward the daily caps of its maker, and of that dot's maker, up the chain, as
//! well as its own; a reached cap holds and stops the runs of the maker and of every dot below
//! it as a capped dot's runs are held and stopped; and the spend of a deleted dot still counts
//! toward its makers for the rest of the day, and toward every dot together for the month.

mod common;

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

use chrono::{DateTime, Local, TimeDelta, Utc};
use common::{spec, temp_store, wait_status};
use dots_core::engine::scripted::{ScriptedEngine, Step};
use dots_core::engine::{Engine, EngineEvent};
use dots_core::events::new_bus;
use dots_core::making::reach::Wanted;
use dots_core::making::service::{MakeDot, MakeOutcome};
use dots_core::model::{
    Dot, DotSpec, EngineKind, Made, NewRun, Run, RunStatus, TriggerKind, WaitReason, WorkspaceMode,
};
use dots_core::runner::{Runner, RunnerConfig};
use dots_core::settings::Settings;
use dots_core::spend::{
    day_bounds_in, month_bounds_in, CapScope, DotCaps, DotSpend, Ledger, Spend, SHARED_WITH_MADE,
};
use dots_core::store::Store;
use dots_core::util::timestamp;
use dots_core::vault::MemorySecrets;
use dots_core::{Config, Error, Runtime};
use serde_json::json;
use tempfile::TempDir;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

fn utc(s: &str) -> DateTime<Utc> {
    DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(s).unwrap().with_timezone(&Utc)
}

fn spent(cost_usd: f64, tokens: i64) -> Spend {
    Spend { cost_usd, tokens }
}

const NONE: Spend = Spend {
    cost_usd: 0.0,
    tokens: 0,
};

fn usd_cap(daily_usd: f64) -> DotCaps {
    DotCaps {
        daily_usd: Some(daily_usd),
        daily_tokens: None,
    }
}

/// Who made a dot `maker` made.
fn made_by(maker: &Dot) -> Made {
    Made {
        by_dot_id: Some(maker.id.clone()),
        by_name: maker.spec.name.clone(),
        run_id: "run".into(),
        purpose: "Reads the feeds".into(),
    }
}

/// A dot a person made, with `caps`.
async fn dot(store: &Store, name: &str, caps: DotCaps) -> Dot {
    let mut s = spec(name);
    s.spend_cap = caps;
    store.create_dot(&s, None, "default").await.unwrap()
}

/// A dot `maker` made, with `caps`.
async fn made(store: &Store, maker: &Dot, name: &str, caps: DotCaps) -> Dot {
    let mut s = spec(name);
    s.spend_cap = caps;
    store
        .create_made_dot(&s, None, "default", &made_by(maker))
        .await
        .unwrap()
}

/// A finished run of `dot` started at `at` that reported `tokens` (in + out) and cost `cost`.
async fn run_at(store: &Store, dot: &Dot, at: DateTime<Utc>, cost: f64, tokens: i64) -> Run {
    let r = store
        .create_run(&NewRun::new(&dot.id, TriggerKind::Schedule))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    store
        .set_run_times(&r.id, &timestamp(at), Some(&timestamp(at)))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    store
        .finish_run(&r.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, Some("ok"), None)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    store
        .add_usage(&r.id, tokens, 0, 0, Some(cost))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    store.get_run(&r.id).await.unwrap()
}

/// The words of the first cap reached for a run of `dot` at `now`, with the caps of the stored
/// Settings.
async fn hit(store: &Store, dot: &Dot, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> Option<String> {
    let settings = store.get_settings().await.unwrap();
    Ledger::new(&settings, now)
        .hit_for(store, &dot.id)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .map(|h| h.text)
}

/// What counts toward the caps of `dot` on the local day of `now`.
async fn shared(store: &Store, dot: &Dot, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> Spend {
    let (start, end) = day_bounds_in(now, &Local);
    store
        .shared_spend_between(&dot.id, &start, &end)
        .await
        .unwrap()
}

/// The first moment of the local day after the one of `now`.
fn next_day(now: DateTime<Utc>) -> DateTime<Utc> {
    utc(&day_bounds_in(now, &Local).1)
}

/// The first moment of the local month after the one of `now`.
fn next_month(now: DateTime<Utc>) -> DateTime<Utc> {
    utc(&month_bounds_in(now, &Local).1)
}

/// The row of `dot` in today's spend.
fn row<'a>(dots: &'a [DotSpend], dot: &Dot) -> &'a DotSpend {
    dots.iter()
        .find(|d| d.dot_id == dot.id)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{} is not in {dots:#?}", dot.spec.name))
}

// The ledger: whose cap is reached, and how it is named.

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_made_dots_spend_reaches_its_makers_cap_for_all_of_them() {
    let (_d, store) = temp_store().await;
    let maker = dot(&store, "Researcher", usd_cap(2.0)).await;
    let one = made(&store, &maker, "Blog Watcher", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let two = made(&store, &maker, "Feed Reader", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let other = dot(&store, "Other", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let now = Utc::now();
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &maker, now).await, None);
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &one, now).await, None);

    run_at(&store, &one, now, 1.5, 100).await;
    // Under the cap: the maker's own spend comes on top.
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &maker, now).await, None);
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &maker, now).await, spent(1.5, 100));
    run_at(&store, &maker, now, 0.5, 10).await;
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &maker, now).await, spent(2.0, 110));
    // What a made dot spent is its own alone: its maker's and its sibling's are not below it.
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &one, now).await, spent(1.5, 100));
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &two, now).await, NONE);

    // The maker's own run reads as any capped dot's does.
    assert_eq!(
        hit(&store, &maker, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("Researcher reached its $2.00 daily cap")
    );
    // A made dot's run names the maker, whose cap it is: the one that spent, and its sibling.
    let theirs = "Researcher reached its $2.00 daily cap, shared with the dots it made";
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &one, now).await.as_deref(), Some(theirs));
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &two, now).await.as_deref(), Some(theirs));
    assert_eq!(
        theirs,
        format!("Researcher reached its $2.00 daily cap{SHARED_WITH_MADE}")
    );
    // It is a dot's cap, not the one for every dot.
    let settings = Settings::default();
    let held = Ledger::new(&settings, now)
        .hit(&store, &one)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(held.scope, CapScope::Dot);
    // A dot outside the tree is not held.
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &other, now).await, None);
    // Tomorrow nothing of it counts.
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &one, next_day(now)).await, None);
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &maker, next_day(now)).await, None);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_made_dots_own_cap_holds_it_alone() {
    let (_d, store) = temp_store().await;
    let maker = dot(&store, "Researcher", usd_cap(10.0)).await;
    let one = made(&store, &maker, "Blog Watcher", usd_cap(1.0)).await;
    let two = made(&store, &maker, "Feed Reader", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let now = Utc::now();
    // A made dot starts with no cap; this one was given its own by the person.
    assert_eq!(two.spec.spend_cap, DotCaps::default());

    run_at(&store, &one, now, 1.0, 100).await;
    // Its own cap, in the words of any capped dot.
    assert_eq!(
        hit(&store, &one, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("Blog Watcher reached its $1.00 daily cap")
    );
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &maker, now).await, None);
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &two, now).await, None);
    // The maker's spend does not count toward the made dot's cap.
    let other = made(&store, &maker, "Capped", usd_cap(1.0)).await;
    run_at(&store, &maker, now, 5.0, 100).await;
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &other, now).await, None);
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &other, now).await, NONE);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn spend_counts_up_the_whole_chain() {
    let (_d, store) = temp_store().await;
    let a = dot(&store, "A", usd_cap(5.0)).await;
    let b = made(&store, &a, "B", usd_cap(3.0)).await;
    let c = made(&store, &b, "C", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let now = Utc::now();
    assert_eq!(
        store
            .makers_of(&c.id)
            .await
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .map(|d| d.spec.name.as_str())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        ["B", "A"]
    );
    assert!(store.makers_of(&a.id).await.unwrap().is_empty());

    run_at(&store, &c, now, 3.0, 100).await;
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &b, now).await, spent(3.0, 100));
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &a, now).await, spent(3.0, 100));
    // B's cap is reached by what C spent; A's is not yet.
    assert_eq!(
        hit(&store, &c, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("B reached its $3.00 daily cap, shared with the dots it made")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        hit(&store, &b, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("B reached its $3.00 daily cap")
    );
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &a, now).await, None);

    run_at(&store, &c, now, 2.0, 100).await;
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &a, now).await, spent(5.0, 200));
    assert_eq!(
        hit(&store, &a, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("A reached its $5.00 daily cap")
    );
    // The nearest maker's cap is named first.
    assert_eq!(
        hit(&store, &c, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("B reached its $3.00 daily cap, shared with the dots it made")
    );
    // Without B's cap, C and B are held by A's, two makers up for C.
    let mut s = b.spec.clone();
    s.spend_cap = DotCaps::default();
    store.update_dot(&b.id, &s).await.unwrap();
    let of_a = "A reached its $5.00 daily cap, shared with the dots it made";
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &c, now).await.as_deref(), Some(of_a));
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &b, now).await.as_deref(), Some(of_a));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_token_cap_is_shared_as_the_cost_cap_is() {
    let (_d, store) = temp_store().await;
    let caps = DotCaps {
        daily_usd: None,
        daily_tokens: Some(1000),
    };
    let maker = dot(&store, "Researcher", caps).await;
    let one = made(&store, &maker, "Blog Watcher", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let now = Utc::now();
    run_at(&store, &one, now, 0.0, 600).await;
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &one, now).await, None);
    run_at(&store, &maker, now, 0.0, 400).await;
    assert_eq!(
        hit(&store, &maker, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("Researcher reached its 1,000-token daily cap")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        hit(&store, &one, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("Researcher reached its 1,000-token daily cap, shared with the dots it made")
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_dot_that_made_nothing_and_has_no_maker_reads_as_before() {
    let (_d, store) = temp_store().await;
    let caps = DotCaps {
        daily_usd: Some(2.0),
        daily_tokens: Some(200_000),
    };
    let scout = dot(&store, "Scout", caps).await;
    let now = Utc::now();
    let (start, end) = day_bounds_in(now, &Local);
    run_at(&store, &scout, now, 1.25, 1210).await;
    run_at(&store, &scout, now, 0.5, 42).await;

    let own = store
        .spend_between(Some(&scout.id), &start, &end)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(own, spent(1.75, 1252));
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &scout, now).await, own);
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &scout, now).await, None);
    run_at(&store, &scout, now, 0.25, 0).await;
    assert_eq!(
        hit(&store, &scout, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("Scout reached its $2.00 daily cap")
    );

    let today = dots_core::spend::today(&store, now).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        today.dots,
        [DotSpend {
            dot_id: scout.id.clone(),
            dot_name: "Scout".into(),
            today: spent(2.0, 1252),
            caps,
            shared_today: None,
        }]
    );
    assert_eq!(today.today, spent(2.0, 1252));
    // Deleted by the person, its spend goes with its runs, as before.
    store.delete_dot_if_idle(&scout.id).await.unwrap();
    let today = dots_core::spend::today(&store, now).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!((today.today, today.month), (NONE, NONE));
    assert_eq!(
        store.kept_spend_between(None, &start, &end).await.unwrap(),
        NONE
    );
}

// What a deleted dot spent.

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_deleted_made_dots_spend_still_counts_for_the_day() {
    let (_d, store) = temp_store().await;
    let maker = dot(&store, "Researcher", usd_cap(2.0)).await;
    let one = made(&store, &maker, "Blog Watcher", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let two = made(&store, &maker, "Feed Reader", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let now = Utc::now();
    let (start, end) = day_bounds_in(now, &Local);
    run_at(&store, &one, now, 1.5, 100).await;
    run_at(&store, &one, now, 0.5, 20).await;
    // A run that spent nothing, and one of the month before, leave nothing behind.
    run_at(&store, &one, now, 0.0, 0).await;
    let last_month = utc(&month_bounds_in(now, &Local).0) - TimeDelta::minutes(1);
    run_at(&store, &one, last_month, 9.0, 900).await;
    let before = shared(&store, &maker, now).await;
    assert_eq!(before, spent(2.0, 120));

    store.delete_dot_if_idle(&one.id).await.unwrap();

    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &maker, now).await, before);
    assert_eq!(
        store
            .kept_spend_between(Some(&maker.id), &start, &end)
            .await
            .unwrap(),
        before
    );
    assert_eq!(
        hit(&store, &maker, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("Researcher reached its $2.00 daily cap")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        hit(&store, &two, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("Researcher reached its $2.00 daily cap, shared with the dots it made")
    );
    // The next day it counts no more.
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &maker, next_day(now)).await, NONE);
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &maker, next_day(now)).await, None);
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &two, next_day(now)).await, None);
    // Nothing older than this month was kept.
    assert_eq!(
        store
            .kept_spend_between(Some(&maker.id), "2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", &start)
            .await
            .unwrap(),
        NONE
    );

    // What was kept for the maker goes with the maker.
    store.delete_dot_if_idle(&two.id).await.unwrap();
    store.delete_dot_if_idle(&maker.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        store
            .kept_spend_between(Some(&maker.id), &start, &end)
            .await
            .unwrap(),
        NONE
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn deleting_the_middle_of_a_chain_keeps_what_it_and_its_deleted_dot_spent() {
    let (_d, store) = temp_store().await;
    let a = dot(&store, "A", usd_cap(3.0)).await;
    let b = made(&store, &a, "B", usd_cap(2.0)).await;
    let c = made(&store, &b, "C", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let now = Utc::now();
    run_at(&store, &c, now, 1.0, 100).await;
    run_at(&store, &b, now, 0.5, 10).await;

    store.delete_dot_if_idle(&c.id).await.unwrap();
    // It counts toward both makers above it.
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &b, now).await, spent(1.5, 110));
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &a, now).await, spent(1.5, 110));

    store.delete_dot_if_idle(&b.id).await.unwrap();
    // What B held for C and what B spent itself still count toward A, once each.
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &a, now).await, spent(1.5, 110));
    run_at(&store, &a, now, 1.5, 0).await;
    assert_eq!(
        hit(&store, &a, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("A reached its $3.00 daily cap")
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn deleting_a_maker_keeps_what_the_dots_below_it_spent_so_far() {
    let (_d, store) = temp_store().await;
    let a = dot(&store, "A", usd_cap(3.0)).await;
    let b = made(&store, &a, "B", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let c = made(&store, &b, "C", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let now = Utc::now();
    run_at(&store, &c, now, 1.0, 100).await;
    run_at(&store, &b, now, 0.5, 10).await;
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &a, now).await, spent(1.5, 110));

    // B goes while C lives: A cannot shed what C spent by deleting the dot between them.
    store.delete_dot_if_idle(&b.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &a, now).await, spent(1.5, 110));
    // C has no maker now: what it spends from here on is its own alone.
    let c_now = store.get_dot(&c.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(c_now.made.unwrap().by_dot_id, None);
    run_at(&store, &c, now, 4.0, 400).await;
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &a, now).await, spent(1.5, 110));
    assert_eq!(shared(&store, &c, now).await, spent(5.0, 500));
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &c, now).await, None);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_deleted_made_dots_spend_still_counts_for_every_dot_together() {
    let (_d, store) = temp_store().await;
    store
        .put_settings(&Settings {
            spend_daily_usd: Some(2.0),
            spend_monthly_usd: Some(2.0),
            ..Settings::default()
        })
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let maker = dot(&store, "Researcher", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let b = made(&store, &maker, "B", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let c = made(&store, &b, "C", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let other = dot(&store, "Other", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let now = Utc::now();
    run_at(&store, &c, now, 2.0, 100).await;
    let before = dots_core::spend::today(&store, now).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        (before.today, before.month),
        (spent(2.0, 100), spent(2.0, 100))
    );

    // Two makers above it: it is counted once for every dot together.
    store.delete_dot_if_idle(&c.id).await.unwrap();

    let after = dots_core::spend::today(&store, now).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!((after.today, after.month), (before.today, before.month));
    assert_eq!(
        hit(&store, &other, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("All dots reached the $2.00 daily cap")
    );
    // The next day the daily cap is free; the monthly one is not, until the month ends.
    let tomorrow = next_day(now);
    if tomorrow < next_month(now) {
        assert_eq!(
            hit(&store, &other, tomorrow).await.as_deref(),
            Some("All dots reached the $2.00 monthly cap")
        );
        let then = dots_core::spend::today(&store, tomorrow).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!((then.today, then.month), (NONE, spent(2.0, 100)));
    }
    assert_eq!(hit(&store, &other, next_month(now)).await, None);
    // It stays counted when its makers go too.
    store.delete_dot_if_idle(&b.id).await.unwrap();
    store.delete_dot_if_idle(&maker.id).await.unwrap();
    let after = dots_core::spend::today(&store, now).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!((after.today, after.month), (before.today, before.month));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn todays_spend_shows_what_a_maker_shares() {
    let (_d, store) = temp_store().await;
    let maker = dot(&store, "Researcher", usd_cap(5.0)).await;
    let one = made(&store, &maker, "Blog Watcher", DotCaps::default()).await;
    let now = Utc::now();
    run_at(&store, &one, now, 1.5, 100).await;
    run_at(&store, &maker, now, 0.5, 10).await;

    let today = dots_core::spend::today(&store, now).await.unwrap();
    let of_maker = row(&today.dots, &maker);
    assert_eq!(of_maker.today, spent(0.5, 10));
    assert_eq!(of_maker.shared_today, Some(spent(2.0, 110)));
    // A made dot that made nothing shares nothing of its own.
    let of_one = row(&today.dots, &one);
    assert_eq!((of_one.today, of_one.shared_today), (spent(1.5, 100), None));
    assert_eq!(today.today, spent(2.0, 110));

    // With the made dot gone the maker's row still shows it.
    store.delete_dot_if_idle(&one.id).await.unwrap();
    let today = dots_core::spend::today(&store, now).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(today.dots.len(), 1);
    let of_maker = row(&today.dots, &maker);
    assert_eq!(of_maker.today, spent(0.5, 10));
    assert_eq!(of_maker.shared_today, Some(spent(2.0, 110)));
    assert_eq!(today.today, spent(2.0, 110));
    // The next day there is nothing to share.
    let then = dots_core::spend::today(&store, next_day(now))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(row(&then.dots, &maker).shared_today, None);
}

#[test]
fn a_dots_spend_without_the_shared_total_reads_as_none() {
    let v = json!({
        "dot_id": "d",
        "dot_name": "Scout",
        "today": {"cost_usd": 1.0, "tokens": 5},
        "caps": {"daily_usd": null, "daily_tokens": null},
    });
    let row: DotSpend = serde_json::from_value(v).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(row.shared_today, None);
}

// The runner: runs wait and are stopped.

fn usage(cost: f64) -> Step {
    Step::Emit(EngineEvent::Usage {
        tokens_in: 100,
        tokens_out: 10,
        cache_read: 0,
        cost_usd: Some(cost),
    })
}

fn finished() -> Step {
    Step::Emit(EngineEvent::Finished {
        summary: "done".into(),
    })
}

struct Env {
    dir: TempDir,
    store: Store,
    runner: Arc<Runner>,
}

async fn env(steps: Vec<Step>) -> Env {
    let (dir, store) = temp_store().await;
    let mut engines: HashMap<EngineKind, Arc<dyn Engine>> = HashMap::new();
    engines.insert(EngineKind::Claude, Arc::new(ScriptedEngine::new(steps)));
    let runner = Runner::new(
        store.clone(),
        new_bus(),
        engines,
        RunnerConfig {
            max_concurrent: 2,
            mcp_url: "http://127.0.0.1:1/mcp".into(),
            worktrees_dir: dir.path().join("wt"),
            cancel_grace: Duration::from_millis(200),
            plugins_dir: dir.path().join("plugins"),
            quiet_unit: Duration::from_secs(1),
        },
    );
    runner.spawn_dispatcher(CancellationToken::new());
    Env { dir, store, runner }
}

impl Env {
    fn spec(&self, name: &str, daily_usd: Option<f64>) -> DotSpec {
        let mut s = spec(name);
        s.workdir = self.dir.path().to_string_lossy().to_string();
        s.workspace_mode = WorkspaceMode::Folder;
        s.spend_cap = DotCaps {
            daily_usd,
            daily_tokens: None,
        };
        s
    }

    async fn dot(&self, name: &str, daily_usd: Option<f64>) -> Dot {
        self.store
            .create_dot(&self.spec(name, daily_usd), None, "default")
            .await
            .unwrap()
    }

    async fn made(&self, maker: &Dot, name: &str) -> Dot {
        self.store
            .create_made_dot(&self.spec(name, None), None, "default", &made_by(maker))
            .await
            .unwrap()
    }

    /// A finished run of `dot` started now that cost `cost`. The queue is held while the run
    /// is made and ended: a dispatch pass in between would run it.
    async fn spent(&self, dot: &Dot, cost: f64) {
        self.runner.set_held(true).await;
        run_at(&self.store, dot, Utc::now(), cost, 1100).await;
        self.runner.set_held(false).await;
    }

    async fn queue(&self, dot: &Dot) -> String {
        self.runner
            .enqueue(NewRun::new(&dot.id, TriggerKind::Schedule))
            .await
            .unwrap()
            .id
    }

    async fn settle(&self) {
        self.runner.nudge();
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
    }

    async fn status(&self, id: &str) -> RunStatus {
        self.store.get_run(id).await.unwrap().status
    }

    /// Why the queued run `id` waits.
    async fn waits_for(&self, id: &str) -> (Option<WaitReason>, Option<String>) {
        let mut runs = vec![self.store.get_run(id).await.unwrap()];
        self.runner.fill_wait_reasons(&mut runs).await.unwrap();
        (runs[0].wait_reason, runs[0].wait_detail.clone())
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn runs_of_the_maker_and_its_made_dots_wait_at_the_shared_cap() {
    let e = env(vec![finished()]).await;
    let maker = e.dot("Researcher", Some(2.0)).await;
    let one = e.made(&maker, "Blog Watcher").await;
    let two = e.made(&maker, "Feed Reader").await;
    e.spent(&one, 2.0).await;

    let of_maker = e.queue(&maker).await;
    let of_one = e.queue(&one).await;
    let of_two = e.queue(&two).await;
    e.settle().await;
    for id in [&of_maker, &of_one, &of_two] {
        assert_eq!(e.status(id).await, RunStatus::Queued);
    }
    // Each says why it waits; a made dot's names the maker.
    assert_eq!(
        e.waits_for(&of_maker).await,
        (
            Some(WaitReason::SpendCap),
            Some("Researcher reached its $2.00 daily cap".into())
        )
    );
    let theirs = "Researcher reached its $2.00 daily cap, shared with the dots it made";
    for id in [&of_one, &of_two] {
        assert_eq!(
            e.waits_for(id).await,
            (Some(WaitReason::SpendCap), Some(theirs.into()))
        );
        let run = e.store.get_run(id).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(e.runner.cap_hold(&run).await.unwrap().unwrap().text, theirs);
    }
    // A dot outside the tree runs.
    let other = e.dot("Other", None).await;
    let free = e.queue(&other).await;
    wait_status(&e.store, &free, RunStatus::Succeeded, 20).await;
    assert_eq!(e.status(&of_one).await, RunStatus::Queued);

    // The maker's cap raised: all of them start.
    let mut s = maker.spec.clone();
    s.spend_cap.daily_usd = Some(50.0);
    e.store.update_dot(&maker.id, &s).await.unwrap();
    e.runner.nudge();
    for id in [&of_maker, &of_one, &of_two] {
        wait_status(&e.store, id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 20).await;
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_made_dots_own_cap_does_not_hold_its_makers_runs() {
    let e = env(vec![finished()]).await;
    let maker = e.dot("Researcher", None).await;
    let one = e.made(&maker, "Blog Watcher").await;
    let mut s = one.spec.clone();
    s.spend_cap.daily_usd = Some(1.0);
    let one = e.store.update_dot(&one.id, &s).await.unwrap();
    let two = e.made(&maker, "Feed Reader").await;
    e.spent(&one, 1.0).await;

    let of_one = e.queue(&one).await;
    let of_maker = e.queue(&maker).await;
    let of_two = e.queue(&two).await;
    wait_status(&e.store, &of_maker, RunStatus::Succeeded, 20).await;
    wait_status(&e.store, &of_two, RunStatus::Succeeded, 20).await;
    assert_eq!(e.status(&of_one).await, RunStatus::Queued);
    assert_eq!(
        e.waits_for(&of_one).await.1.as_deref(),
        Some("Blog Watcher reached its $1.00 daily cap")
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_made_dots_run_is_stopped_when_the_shared_cap_is_crossed() {
    let e = env(vec![usage(0.6), usage(0.6), Step::WaitForCancel]).await;
    let maker = e.dot("Researcher", Some(1.0)).await;
    let one = e.made(&maker, "Blog Watcher").await;
    let id = e.queue(&one).await;
    let run = wait_status(&e.store, &id, RunStatus::Failed, 20).await;
    assert_eq!(
        run.error.as_deref(),
        Some("stopped: Researcher reached its $1.00 daily cap, shared with the dots it made")
    );
    assert!((run.cost_usd.unwrap() - 1.2).abs() < 1e-9);
    // The maker's next run waits, and so does the made dot's.
    let of_maker = e.queue(&maker).await;
    let next = e.queue(&one).await;
    e.settle().await;
    assert_eq!(e.status(&of_maker).await, RunStatus::Queued);
    assert_eq!(e.status(&next).await, RunStatus::Queued);
    assert_eq!(
        e.waits_for(&of_maker).await.1.as_deref(),
        Some("Researcher reached its $1.00 daily cap")
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_makers_run_is_stopped_by_what_it_and_its_made_dot_spent() {
    let e = env(vec![usage(0.6), Step::WaitForCancel]).await;
    let maker = e.dot("Researcher", Some(1.0)).await;
    let one = e.made(&maker, "Blog Watcher").await;
    e.spent(&one, 0.5).await;
    let id = e.queue(&maker).await;
    let run = wait_status(&e.store, &id, RunStatus::Failed, 20).await;
    assert_eq!(
        run.error.as_deref(),
        Some("stopped: Researcher reached its $1.00 daily cap")
    );
}

// The runtime: the person's delete and the maker's.

struct T {
    dir: TempDir,
    rt: Runtime,
}

/// As `making_manage_test.rs` has it: no queued run starts, so a run is put in the running
/// state by hand.
async fn start() -> T {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let mut cfg = Config::new(dir.path().join("data"));
    cfg.port = 0;
    cfg.claude_path = Some(PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake-claude")));
    cfg.new_dot_root = dir.path().join("Dots");
    cfg.secrets = Some(Arc::new(MemorySecrets::new()));
    cfg.max_concurrent_runs = 0;
    let rt = Runtime::start(cfg).await.unwrap();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path().join("work")).unwrap();
    T { dir, rt }
}

/// A maker named Researcher with a $2.00 daily cap, created as the person creates a dot, and
/// a run of it that is running.
async fn capped_maker(t: &T) -> (Dot, Run) {
    let mut s = spec("Researcher");
    s.workdir = t.dir.path().join("work").to_string_lossy().to_string();
    s.workspace_mode = WorkspaceMode::Folder;
    s.making.on = true;
    s.spend_cap = usd_cap(2.0);
    let maker = t.rt.create_dot(s, None, None).await.unwrap();
    let mut new = NewRun::new(&maker.id, TriggerKind::Chat);
    new.payload = Some(json!({"message": "watch three blogs", "typed": true}));
    let run = t.rt.store().create_run(&new).await.unwrap();
    assert!(t.rt.store().claim_run(&run.id).await.unwrap());
    (maker, run)
}

/// Makes the dot through the maker's tool; it must be within reach and within the limits.
async fn make(t: &T, run: &Run, name: &str) -> Dot {
    let asked = MakeDot {
        purpose: "Reads the feeds".into(),
        wanted: Wanted {
            name: Some(name.into()),
            instructions: Some("Read the three blogs and list what is new.".into()),
            ..Wanted::default()
        },
        first_job: None,
    };
    match t.rt.makers().make_dot(&run.id, asked).await.unwrap() {
        MakeOutcome::Made { dot, .. } => dot,
        other => panic!("{name} was not made: {other:?}"),
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_dot_made_by_a_capped_maker_starts_with_no_cap_of_its_own() {
    let t = start().await;
    let (_maker, run) = capped_maker(&t).await;
    let one = make(&t, &run, "Blog Watcher").await;
    assert_eq!(one.spec.spend_cap, DotCaps::default());
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_persons_delete_of_a_made_dot_does_not_lower_the_shared_total() {
    let t = start().await;
    let (maker, run) = capped_maker(&t).await;
    let one = make(&t, &run, "Blog Watcher").await;
    let two = make(&t, &run, "Feed Reader").await;
    let store = t.rt.store();
    let now = Utc::now();
    run_at(store, &one, now, 2.0, 100).await;
    let before = shared(store, &maker, now).await;
    assert_eq!(before, spent(2.0, 100));

    t.rt.delete_dot(&one.id).await.unwrap();

    assert!(matches!(
        store.get_dot(&one.id).await,
        Err(Error::NotFound(_))
    ));
    assert_eq!(shared(store, &maker, now).await, before);
    assert_eq!(
        hit(store, &maker, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("Researcher reached its $2.00 daily cap")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        hit(store, &two, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("Researcher reached its $2.00 daily cap, shared with the dots it made")
    );
    let today = t.rt.spend_today().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(row(&today.dots, &maker).shared_today, Some(before));
    assert_eq!(today.today, before);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_maker_cannot_clear_its_cap_by_deleting_the_dot_it_made() {
    let t = start().await;
    let (maker, run) = capped_maker(&t).await;
    let one = make(&t, &run, "Blog Watcher").await;
    let store = t.rt.store();
    let now = Utc::now();
    run_at(store, &one, now, 2.0, 100).await;
    let before = shared(store, &maker, now).await;
    assert_eq!(before, spent(2.0, 100));

    t.rt.makers()
        .delete_dot(&run.id, "Blog Watcher")
        .await
        .unwrap();

    assert!(matches!(
        store.get_dot(&one.id).await,
        Err(Error::NotFound(_))
    ));
    assert_eq!(shared(store, &maker, now).await, before);
    assert_eq!(
        hit(store, &maker, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("Researcher reached its $2.00 daily cap")
    );
    // A dot it makes now is held by the same cap.
    let two = make(&t, &run, "Feed Reader").await;
    assert_eq!(
        hit(store, &two, now).await.as_deref(),
        Some("Researcher reached its $2.00 daily cap, shared with the dots it made")
    );
    assert_eq!(hit(store, &maker, next_day(now)).await, None);
}
```

```sql
-- What deleted dots spent, kept so it still counts toward their makers' caps (dots-make-dots
-- design section 6, Spend survives a delete). A dot's spend is summed from its runs, and
-- deleting a dot deletes its runs; so the transaction that deletes a dot with a maker first
-- writes one row here per run of this month that spent anything, for each maker up the chain as
-- it is then (`dot_id`), and once more with `dot_id` NULL, which is the copy that counts toward
-- the caps for every dot together. The runs of the living dots below the deleted one are kept
-- for the makers above it in the same way, since those dots stop sharing with them from then
-- on. `started_at` is the run's own, so the day and the month are bounded as they are for runs;
-- `tokens` is in + out. A maker's rows go with the maker; rows older than this month are
-- removed at the next delete of a dot.
CREATE TABLE made_spend_kept (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    dot_id      TEXT REFERENCES dots(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    started_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
    cost_usd    REAL NOT NULL,
    tokens      INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX made_spend_kept_dot ON made_spend_kept(dot_id, started_at);
```

```rust
async fn all_between(store: &Store, start: &str, end: &str) -> Result<Spend> {
    let runs = store.spend_between(None, start, end).await?;
    let kept = store.kept_spend_between(None, start, end).await?;
    Ok(Spend {
        cost_usd: runs.cost_usd + kept.cost_usd,
        tokens: runs.tokens + kept.tokens,
    })
}
```

**with:**

```rust

/// Keeps what the dot `id`, about to be deleted, spent in the runs started this local month, so
/// it still counts toward its makers' caps (dots-make-dots design section 6, Spend survives a
/// delete; migration 0053): one row per run that spent anything for each maker up the chain as
/// it is now, and one that counts toward the caps for every dot together, since the runs go
/// with the dot. The runs of the living dots below it are kept for the makers above it too:
/// those dots have no maker once it is gone, so without this a maker could shed their spend by
/// deleting the dot between them. A dot with no maker keeps nothing. Rows older than the month
/// count toward no cap and are removed here.
async fn keep_spend(tx: &mut sqlx::SqliteConnection, id: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let (month_start, _) = crate::spend::month_bounds_in(Utc::now(), &Local);
    sqlx::query("DELETE FROM made_spend_kept WHERE started_at < ?")
        .bind(&month_start)
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?;
    sqlx::query(
        "WITH RECURSIVE up(maker, depth) AS ( \
         SELECT made_by_dot_id, 1 FROM dots WHERE id = ?1 AND made_by_dot_id IS NOT NULL \
         UNION ALL \
         SELECT d.made_by_dot_id, up.depth + 1 FROM dots d JOIN up ON d.id = up.maker \
         WHERE d.made_by_dot_id IS NOT NULL AND up.depth < ?3), \
         tree(dot, depth) AS ( \
         SELECT ?1, 0 \
         UNION ALL \
         SELECT d.id, tree.depth + 1 FROM dots d JOIN tree ON d.made_by_dot_id = tree.dot \
         WHERE tree.depth < ?3), \
         holders(maker) AS ( \
         SELECT maker FROM up UNION ALL SELECT NULL WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM up)) \
         INSERT INTO made_spend_kept (dot_id, started_at, cost_usd, tokens) \
         SELECT holders.maker, r.started_at, COALESCE(r.cost_usd, 0.0), \
         r.tokens_in + r.tokens_out \
         FROM holders JOIN runs r ON (holders.maker IS NOT NULL OR r.dot_id = ?1) \
         WHERE r.dot_id IN (SELECT dot FROM tree) AND r.started_at >= ?2 \
         AND (COALESCE(r.cost_usd, 0.0) > 0 OR r.tokens_in + r.tokens_out > 0)",
    )
    .bind(id)
    .bind(&month_start)
    .bind(crate::spend::MAKER_DEPTH)
    .execute(&mut *tx)
    .await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Task 11: A maker's run on the Claude engine gets the five making tools

`making::tools` holds the five tools' names, descriptions, schemas, the offer rule, the policy input and the call into `Makers`, for both engines. The runner offers them to a run only when the policy does not deny `MakeDots`, the makers are wired, and `may_make` would not refuse the run. Dots' own MCP server lists them and dispatches a call: read the arguments (unknown ones are refused), ask the policy under `MakeDots` with `{"tool", "input"}` (so an approval for one tool cannot be used for another), then call the service. `guard::classify` guards `delete_dot`, so a dot with "Always ask before sending or deleting" asks the person first.

CLI names `mcp__dots__make_dot`, `mcp__dots__change_dot`, `mcp__dots__delete_dot`, `mcp__dots__give_job`, `mcp__dots__list_made_dots`. `delete_dot` takes `{dot}`; `give_job` takes `{dot, message}`.
