```rust
//! The tools for making dots on the local engine (dots-make-dots design sections 5 and 7 to
//! 10): a run of a maker is offered `make_dot`, `change_dot`, `delete_dot`, `give_job` and
//! `list_made_dots` as built-in functions, with the arguments and words Dots' own `dots` MCP
//! server gives a Claude run, and no other run is. Each call is checked against the dot's policy
//! under `MakeDots` and performed by the makers' service; a call that waited for the person is
//! performed by Dots when the run is resumed, as every approved call of the local engine is.

mod common;
mod llm;

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use common::{init_repo, spec, wait_status};
use dots_core::approvals::grant_key;
use dots_core::making::jobs::gave_text;
use dots_core::making::tools::Tool;
use dots_core::model::{
    ApplyState, Approval, Dot, DotSpec, EngineKind, MemberSpec, ProjectSpec, Run, RunStatus,
    TeamSpec, WorkflowRun, WorkflowRunStatus, WorkflowSpec, WorkflowTrigger, WorkspaceMode,
};
use dots_core::policy::{Action, GuardKind, Rule};
use dots_core::vault::MemorySecrets;
use dots_core::workflow::{Budget, Definition, Step, StepKind, Trigger};
use dots_core::{Config, Runtime};
use llm::{call, messages, text, tool_result, Llm};
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use tempfile::TempDir;

/// The five tools as the local engine names them, in its order.
const NAMES: [&str; 5] = [
    "make_dot",
    "change_dot",
    "delete_dot",
    "give_job",
    "list_made_dots",
];

/// What `make_dot` tells the run of a dot made at once, with no schedule and no first job.
const MADE: &str =
    "Made the dot \"Blog Watcher\". It is on and ready; give it a job with give_job.";

/// How a tool the run does not have is refused.
const UNKNOWN: &str = "unknown tool 'make_dot'. Available tools: ";

struct T {
    dir: TempDir,
    rt: Runtime,
}

async fn start() -> T {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let mut cfg = Config::new(dir.path().join("data"));
    cfg.port = 0;
    cfg.claude_path = Some(PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake-claude")));
    cfg.local_retry_delays = vec![Duration::ZERO; 2];
    cfg.new_dot_root = dir.path().join("Dots");
    cfg.secrets = Some(Arc::new(MemorySecrets::new()));
    cfg.max_concurrent_runs = 4;
    let rt = Runtime::start(cfg).await.unwrap();
    T { dir, rt }
}

/// A local dot named `name` that may make dots, in a folder of its own, whose model is `llm`.
/// A call that asks parks at once.
async fn create(t: &T, llm: &Llm, name: &str, edit: impl FnOnce(&mut DotSpec)) -> Dot {
    let folder = t.dir.path().join("work").join(name);
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&folder).unwrap();
    let mut s = spec(name);
    s.workdir = folder.to_string_lossy().to_string();
    s.workspace_mode = WorkspaceMode::Folder;
    s.engine = EngineKind::Local;
    s.endpoint_url = Some(format!("{}/v1", llm.endpoint()));
    s.model = "test-model".into();
    s.making.on = true;
    s.approval_wait_secs = 0;
    edit(&mut s);
    t.rt.create_dot(s, None, None).await.unwrap()
}

/// The arguments of a `make_dot` for a dot named `name`, with nothing but what a new dot needs.
fn asks(name: &str) -> Value {
    json!({
        "name": name,
        "instructions": "Read the three blogs and list what is new.",
        "purpose": "Reads the feeds"
    })
}

/// The functions a recorded request offered the model.
fn offered(req: &Value) -> Vec<Value> {
    req["tools"].as_array().unwrap().clone()
}

fn names(tools: &[Value]) -> Vec<&str> {
    tools
        .iter()
        .map(|t| t["function"]["name"].as_str().unwrap())
        .collect()
}

fn keys(object: &Value) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut keys: Vec<String> = object.as_object().unwrap().keys().cloned().collect();
    keys.sort();
    keys
}

/// The dot named `name` that `maker` made, if it exists.
async fn made_dot(t: &T, maker: &Dot, name: &str) -> Option<Dot> {
    t.rt.store().made_dot_named(&maker.id, name).await.unwrap()
}

/// The names of all dots, sorted.
async fn dot_names(t: &T) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut names: Vec<String> =
        t.rt.store()
            .list_dots()
            .await
            .unwrap()
            .into_iter()
            .map(|d| d.spec.name)
            .collect();
    names.sort();
    names
}

/// What the run's call `id` was answered: the text, and whether it is an error.
async fn result(t: &T, run: &Run, id: &str) -> (String, bool) {
    let events = t.rt.store().list_events(&run.id, 0).await.unwrap();
    let found = events
        .iter()
        .find(|e| e.kind == "tool_result" && e.data["id"] == id)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no result for {id}"));
    (
        found.data["output"].as_str().unwrap().to_string(),
        found.data["is_error"].as_bool().unwrap(),
    )
}

/// The text of the run's call `id`, which is no error.
async fn done(t: &T, run: &Run, id: &str) -> String {
    let (output, is_error) = result(t, run, id).await;
    assert!(!is_error, "{id}: {output}");
    output
}

/// The text of the run's call `id`, which is an error.
async fn refused(t: &T, run: &Run, id: &str) -> String {
    let (output, is_error) = result(t, run, id).await;
    assert!(is_error, "{id}: {output}");
    output
}

/// How the run's call `id` was shown: the tool and its input.
async fn shown(t: &T, run: &Run, id: &str) -> (String, Value) {
    let events = t.rt.store().list_events(&run.id, 0).await.unwrap();
    let found = events
        .iter()
        .find(|e| e.kind == "tool_call" && e.data["id"] == id)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no call {id}"));
    (
        found.data["tool"].as_str().unwrap().to_string(),
        found.data["input"].clone(),
    )
}

/// The resume run of `parent`, once the runner made it.
async fn resume_child(t: &T, parent: &Run) -> Run {
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(20);
    loop {
        let runs =
            t.rt.store()
                .list_runs(Some(&parent.dot_id), 10)
                .await
                .unwrap();
        if let Some(r) = runs
            .into_iter()
            .find(|r| r.parent_run_id.as_deref() == Some(parent.id.as_str()))
        {
            return r;
        }
        assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "no resume run appeared");
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
    }
}

/// The one approval the run waits on, once it has parked.
async fn parked(t: &T, run: &Run) -> Approval {
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &run.id, RunStatus::AwaitingApproval, 30).await;
    let mut approvals = t.rt.store().approvals_for_run(&run.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(approvals.len(), 1, "{approvals:#?}");
    approvals.remove(0)
}

/// Says yes to `approval`, and waits until the resume run of `parent` has ended as `status`.
async fn approve(t: &T, approval: &Approval, parent: &Run, status: RunStatus) -> Run {
    t.rt.decide_approval(&approval.id, true, None, None)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let child = resume_child(t, parent).await;
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &child.id, status, 30).await
}

/// What the resume run told the model first: the report of the calls Dots performed.
fn report(req: &Value) -> String {
    messages(req)
        .last()
        .filter(|m| m["role"] == "user")
        .and_then(|m| m["content"].as_str())
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .to_string()
}

#[test]
fn an_approvals_call_names_its_tool_and_none_is_a_workspace_tool() {
    use dots_core::engine::local::tools;
    use dots_core::making::tools::policy_input;
    for (tool, name) in Tool::ALL.into_iter().zip(NAMES) {
        assert_eq!(tool.model_name(EngineKind::Local), name);
        let checked = policy_input(tool, &json!({"dot": "Blog Watcher"}));
        assert_eq!(tools::local_name_for("MakeDots", &checked), Some(name));
        // The engine checks and performs them itself: `prepare`, which drops the arguments it
        // does not know, never sees one.
        assert_eq!(tools::alias(name), None);
    }
    assert_eq!(tools::local_name("MakeDots"), None);
    assert_eq!(tools::local_name_for("MakeDots", &json!({})), None);
    assert_eq!(
        tools::local_name_for("MakeDots", &json!({"tool": "shell"})),
        None
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn only_a_makers_run_is_offered_the_five_tools() {
    let t = start().await;
    let llm = Llm::start(vec![
        call("p1", "make_dot", asks("Blog Watcher")),
        text("Plain is done."),
        text("The maker is done."),
        call("d1", "make_dot", asks("Blog Watcher")),
        text("Denied is done."),
    ])
    .await;
    // The same dot with the switch off. It calls `make_dot` by name all the same.
    let plain = create(&t, &llm, "Plain", |s| s.making.on = false).await;
    let plain_chat = t.rt.chat(&plain.id, "hello plain", None).await.unwrap();
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &plain_chat.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 30).await;
    let maker = create(&t, &llm, "Researcher", |_| {}).await;
    let maker_chat = t.rt.chat(&maker.id, "hello maker", None).await.unwrap();
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &maker_chat.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 30).await;
    // A maker whose policy denies `MakeDots`.
    let denied = create(&t, &llm, "Denied", |s| {
        s.policy
            .rules
            .insert(0, Rule::new("MakeDots", Action::Deny));
    })
    .await;
    let denied_chat = t.rt.chat(&denied.id, "hello denied", None).await.unwrap();
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &denied_chat.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 30).await;

    let reqs = llm.requests();
    assert_eq!(reqs.len(), 5);
    let plain_tools = offered(&reqs[0]);
    for name in NAMES {
        assert!(!names(&plain_tools).contains(&name), "{plain_tools:?}");
    }
    // Everything the other run has, as it has it, and then the five.
    let maker_tools = offered(&reqs[2]);
    assert_eq!(maker_tools.len(), plain_tools.len() + 5, "{maker_tools:?}");
    assert_eq!(maker_tools[..plain_tools.len()], plain_tools[..]);
    let five = &maker_tools[plain_tools.len()..];
    assert_eq!(names(five), NAMES);
    for (tool, listed) in Tool::ALL.into_iter().zip(five) {
        // The same arguments and the same words as on the Claude engine.
        let mcp = tool.mcp_schema(&maker.spec.making);
        assert_eq!(listed["type"], "function");
        let function = &listed["function"];
        assert_eq!(function["name"], tool.model_name(EngineKind::Local));
        assert_eq!(function["description"], mcp["description"]);
        let parameters = &function["parameters"];
        assert_eq!(parameters["type"], "object");
        assert_eq!(
            keys(&parameters["properties"]),
            keys(&mcp["inputSchema"]["properties"]),
            "{tool:?}"
        );
        assert_eq!(parameters["properties"], mcp["inputSchema"]["properties"]);
        assert_eq!(parameters["required"], mcp["inputSchema"]["required"]);
    }
    assert_eq!(
        five[0]["function"]["parameters"]["required"],
        json!(["name", "instructions", "purpose"])
    );
    // A maker whose policy denies `MakeDots` is offered what a dot with the switch off is.
    assert_eq!(offered(&reqs[3]), plain_tools);

    // A call by name from a run that was not offered the tool is refused as any tool the
    // engine does not have, and makes nothing.
    for (req, id) in [(&reqs[1], "p1"), (&reqs[4], "d1")] {
        let told = tool_result(req, id);
        // The tools it names in their place are the ones every run has.
        let available = told.strip_prefix(UNKNOWN).expect(&told);
        for name in NAMES {
            assert!(!available.contains(name), "{told}");
        }
    }
    assert!(refused(&t, &plain_chat, "p1").await.starts_with(UNKNOWN));
    assert!(refused(&t, &denied_chat, "d1").await.starts_with(UNKNOWN));
    assert_eq!(dot_names(&t).await, ["Denied", "Plain", "Researcher"]);
    t.rt.shutdown();
}

/// A team of `member` with the project "Dots" and a manual workflow "Steps" of one agent step
/// of that member; starts a run of it.
async fn run_step(t: &T, member: &Dot) -> WorkflowRun {
    let team =
        t.rt.teams()
            .create(&TeamSpec {
                org_id: None,
                workspace_id: "default".into(),
                name: "Dots management".into(),
                description: String::new(),
                members: vec![MemberSpec {
                    dot_id: member.id.clone(),
                    role: "researcher".into(),
                }],
            })
            .await
            .unwrap();
    let repo = t.dir.path().join("repo");
    init_repo(&repo);
    t.rt.teams()
        .add_project(
            &team.id,
            &ProjectSpec {
                name: "Dots".into(),
                repo_path: repo.to_string_lossy().to_string(),
                default_branch: None,
                remote: "origin".into(),
            },
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let step = Step {
        id: "research".into(),
        name: "Research it".into(),
        kind: StepKind::Agent {
            member: member.id.clone(),
            job: "Research it.".into(),
            can_send_back_to: Vec::new(),
            outcomes: Vec::new(),
            delegate: None,
        },
    };
    let flow =
        t.rt.teams()
            .create_workflow(
                &team.id,
                &WorkflowSpec {
                    name: "Steps".into(),
                    definition: Definition {
                        trigger: Trigger::Manual,
                        steps: vec![step],
                        budget: Budget::default(),
                    },
                    enabled: true,
                },
            )
            .await
            .unwrap();
    let project =
        t.rt.store()
            .get_team_project_id(&flow.id, "Dots")
            .await
            .unwrap();
    t.rt.workflows()
        .start(dots_core::workflows::StartRequest {
            workflow_id: flow.id,
            project_id: project,
            task: "Watch three blogs.".into(),
            trigger: WorkflowTrigger::Manual,
            origin_run_id: None,
            test: false,
        })
        .await
        .unwrap()
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_workflow_steps_run_of_a_maker_is_not_offered_the_tools() {
    let t = start().await;
    let llm = Llm::start(vec![
        call("s1", "make_dot", asks("Blog Watcher")),
        text("Researched."),
    ])
    .await;
    let maker = create(&t, &llm, "Researcher", |_| {}).await;
    let started = run_step(&t, &maker).await;
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(60);
    let ended = loop {
        let wr = t.rt.workflows().get(&started.id).await.unwrap();
        if wr.status == WorkflowRunStatus::Succeeded {
            break wr;
        }
        assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "{wr:#?}");
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
    };
    let run =
        t.rt.store()
            .runs_of_step_run(&ended.steps[0].id)
            .await
            .unwrap()
            .remove(0);
    assert_eq!(run.dot_id, maker.id);

    // The model was not given the functions, and its call by name was answered as an unknown
    // tool and made nothing.
    let reqs = llm.requests();
    assert_eq!(reqs.len(), 2);
    let listed = offered(&reqs[0]);
    assert!(names(&listed).contains(&"notify"), "{listed:?}");
    for name in NAMES {
        assert!(!names(&listed).contains(&name), "{listed:?}");
    }
    assert!(refused(&t, &run, "s1").await.starts_with(UNKNOWN));
    assert_eq!(dot_names(&t).await, ["Researcher"]);
    t.rt.shutdown();
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_makers_run_makes_changes_lists_jobs_and_deletes_on_the_local_engine() {
    let t = start().await;
    let mut more = asks("Browser Dot");
    more["browser"] = json!(true);
    let mut sneaky = asks("Sneaky");
    sneaky["can_make_dots"] = json!(true);
    let llm = Llm::start(vec![
        call("c1", "make_dot", asks("Blog Watcher")),
        call("c2", "make_dot", more),
        call("c3", "make_dot", sneaky),
        call("c4", "list_made_dots", json!({})),
        call(
            "c5",
            "change_dot",
            json!({"dot": "Blog Watcher", "purpose": "Reads four feeds", "max_turns": 10}),
        ),
        call("c6", "make_dot", asks("Second")),
        call("c7", "delete_dot", json!({"dot": "Second"})),
        call(
            "c8",
            "give_job",
            json!({"dot": "Nobody", "message": "Read the feeds now."}),
        ),
        call(
            "c9",
            "give_job",
            json!({"dot": "Blog Watcher", "message": "Read the feeds now."}),
        ),
        // From here the maker's run, the job's run and the maker's wake each read one.
        text("Done."),
        text("Done."),
        text("Done."),
        text("Done."),
    ])
    .await;
    // Without "Always ask before sending or deleting", so its `delete_dot` does not ask.
    let maker = create(&t, &llm, "Researcher", |s| {
        s.policy.ask_send_delete = false;
    })
    .await;
    let chat =
        t.rt.chat(&maker.id, "watch three blogs", None)
            .await
            .unwrap();
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &chat.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 60).await;

    // Within reach: made at once, and the result is the service's text. The call is shown as
    // the policy checked it.
    assert_eq!(done(&t, &chat, "c1").await, MADE);
    assert_eq!(
        shown(&t, &chat, "c1").await,
        (
            "MakeDots".to_string(),
            json!({"tool": "make_dot", "input": asks("Blog Watcher")})
        )
    );
    let dot = made_dot(&t, &maker, "Blog Watcher").await.expect("made");
    let by = dot.made.clone().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(by.by_dot_id.as_deref(), Some(maker.id.as_str()));
    assert_eq!(by.by_name, "Researcher");
    assert_eq!(by.run_id, chat.id);
    assert_eq!(dot.spec.engine, EngineKind::Local);
    assert!(!dot.spec.making.on);

    // Beyond reach: nothing is made, the request waits, and the run is told to carry on.
    let told = done(&t, &chat, "c2").await;
    assert!(
        told.starts_with("Not made yet: \"Browser Dot\" needs the person's say-so"),
        "{told}"
    );
    assert!(
        told.contains("you will be woken with their answer"),
        "{told}"
    );
    assert!(made_dot(&t, &maker, "Browser Dot").await.is_none());
    let requests =
        t.rt.store()
            .list_make_requests(Some(&maker.id), true)
            .await
            .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(requests.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(requests[0].name, "Browser Dot");
    assert_eq!(requests[0].run_id, chat.id);

    // An argument the tool does not have is refused in a sentence, and nothing is made.
    let told = refused(&t, &chat, "c3").await;
    assert!(
        told.starts_with("make_dot cannot read its arguments: unknown field `can_make_dots`"),
        "{told}"
    );
    assert!(
        told.ends_with("Send only the arguments the tool lists."),
        "{told}"
    );
    assert!(made_dot(&t, &maker, "Sneaky").await.is_none());

    // `list_made_dots` is the service's list: the made dot and the request that waits.
    let listed = done(&t, &chat, "c4").await;
    assert!(
        listed.starts_with("\"Blog Watcher\": Reads the feeds; no schedule"),
        "{listed}"
    );
    assert!(
        listed.ends_with("Waiting for the person: \"Browser Dot\""),
        "{listed}"
    );

    // `change_dot` changes what it names.
    let changed = done(&t, &chat, "c5").await;
    assert!(
        changed.starts_with("Changed \"Blog Watcher\": "),
        "{changed}"
    );
    assert_eq!(dot.spec.max_turns, 10);
    assert_eq!(by.purpose, "Reads four feeds");

    // A second dot, deleted again at once.
    assert!(done(&t, &chat, "c6").await.contains("\"Second\""));
    assert!(done(&t, &chat, "c7").await.contains("Second"));
    assert!(made_dot(&t, &maker, "Second").await.is_none());

    // What the service refuses is a tool error with the service's bare sentence.
    assert_eq!(
        refused(&t, &chat, "c8").await,
        "Researcher did not make a dot named \"Nobody\". list_made_dots shows the dots it made."
    );

    // `give_job` returns at once, and the made dot has a run.
    assert_eq!(done(&t, &chat, "c9").await, gave_text("Blog Watcher"));
    let jobs = t.rt.store().list_runs(Some(&dot.id), 10).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(jobs.len(), 1);

    // No call asked the person anything.
    assert!(t
        .rt
        .store()
        .approvals_for_run(&chat.id)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .is_empty());
    assert_eq!(dot_names(&t).await, ["Blog Watcher", "Researcher"]);
    t.rt.shutdown();
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn arguments_the_tool_cannot_read_are_refused_before_the_policy_is_asked() {
    let t = start().await;
    let mut sneaky = asks("Sneaky");
    sneaky["can_make_dots"] = json!(true);
    let llm = Llm::start(vec![
        call("c1", "make_dot", sneaky),
        call("c2", "give_job", json!({"dot": "Sneaky"})),
        text("Done."),
    ])
    .await;
    // Every call the policy is asked about would wait for the person.
    let maker = create(&t, &llm, "Researcher", |s| {
        s.policy.rules.push(Rule::new("MakeDots", Action::Ask));
    })
    .await;
    let chat =
        t.rt.chat(&maker.id, "watch three blogs", None)
            .await
            .unwrap();
    // The run ends; it does not wait on an approval.
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &chat.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 30).await;
    let told = refused(&t, &chat, "c1").await;
    assert!(
        told.starts_with("make_dot cannot read its arguments: unknown field `can_make_dots`"),
        "{told}"
    );
    let told = refused(&t, &chat, "c2").await;
    assert!(told.contains("missing field `message`"), "{told}");
    assert!(t
        .rt
        .store()
        .approvals_for_run(&chat.id)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .is_empty());
    assert_eq!(dot_names(&t).await, ["Researcher"]);
    t.rt.shutdown();
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn deleting_a_made_dot_asks_first_and_dots_deletes_it_once_approved() {
    let t = start().await;
    let llm = Llm::start(vec![
        call("c1", "make_dot", asks("Blog Watcher")),
        call("c2", "delete_dot", json!({"dot": "Blog Watcher"})),
        text("Queued."),
        text("Deleted after approval."),
    ])
    .await;
    // Every preset starts with "Always ask before sending or deleting" on.
    let maker = create(&t, &llm, "Researcher", |_| {}).await;
    assert!(maker.spec.policy.ask_send_delete);
    let chat =
        t.rt.chat(&maker.id, "watch three blogs", None)
            .await
            .unwrap();
    // Making does not ask; deleting does: the call parks on an approval, and the dot stays.
    let approval = parked(&t, &chat).await;
    assert_eq!(done(&t, &chat, "c1").await, MADE);
    assert!(refused(&t, &chat, "c2")
        .await
        .contains("Queued for human approval"));
    assert_eq!(approval.tool, "MakeDots");
    assert_eq!(
        approval.input,
        json!({"tool": "delete_dot", "input": {"dot": "Blog Watcher"}})
    );
    // Dots performs it, not the model.
    assert!(approval.self_apply);
    let guard =
        t.rt.approval_guard(&approval.id)
            .await
            .unwrap()
            .expect("a guarded call");
    assert_eq!(guard.kind, GuardKind::Delete);
    assert_eq!(
        guard.summary,
        "delete the dot \"Blog Watcher\" and its history"
    );
    assert!(made_dot(&t, &maker, "Blog Watcher").await.is_some());

    // Approved: the resume run deletes the dot first and tells the model what the service said.
    let child = approve(&t, &approval, &chat, RunStatus::Succeeded).await;
    assert!(made_dot(&t, &maker, "Blog Watcher").await.is_none());
    let applied = t.rt.store().get_approval(&approval.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(applied.apply_state, Some(ApplyState::Applied));
    let reqs = llm.requests();
    assert_eq!(reqs.len(), 4);
    let told = report(&reqs[3]);
    let (output, is_error) = result(&t, &child, &format!("approval:{}", approval.id)).await;
    assert!(!is_error, "{output}");
    assert!(output.contains("Blog Watcher"), "{output}");
    assert!(
        told.contains(&format!(
            "- Approval #{}, MakeDots {}: done.\n{output}",
            approval.id, approval.input
        )),
        "{told}"
    );
    // The resume run asked for nothing.
    assert!(t
        .rt
        .store()
        .approvals_for_run(&child.id)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .is_empty());
    assert_eq!(dot_names(&t).await, ["Researcher"]);
    t.rt.shutdown();
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_rule_that_asks_parks_each_call_and_an_approval_is_for_that_call_alone() {
    let t = start().await;
    let change = json!({"dot": "Blog Watcher", "max_turns": 10});
    let llm = Llm::start(vec![
        call("c1", "make_dot", asks("Blog Watcher")),
        text("Queued."),
        // The first resume run: the dot was made, and the model changes it.
        call("c2", "change_dot", change.clone()),
        text("Queued."),
        // The second: the change was made, and the model deletes the dot.
        call("c3", "delete_dot", json!({"dot": "Blog Watcher"})),
        text("Queued."),
    ])
    .await;
    // The ask rule wins over the preset's allow, as for Dots' other own tools. Without
    // "Always ask before sending or deleting", so only the rule makes `delete_dot` ask.
    let maker = create(&t, &llm, "Researcher", |s| {
        s.policy.ask_send_delete = false;
        s.policy.rules.push(Rule::new("MakeDots", Action::Ask));
    })
    .await;
    let chat =
        t.rt.chat(&maker.id, "watch three blogs", None)
            .await
            .unwrap();
    let first = parked(&t, &chat).await;
    // The card names the policy name, and its input the tool and what it was called with.
    assert_eq!(first.tool, "MakeDots");
    assert_eq!(
        first.input,
        json!({"tool": "make_dot", "input": asks("Blog Watcher")})
    );
    assert!(first.self_apply);
    assert!(made_dot(&t, &maker, "Blog Watcher").await.is_none());

    // Approved: the resume run makes the dot, once, as that run; its next call asks again.
    let child = approve(&t, &first, &chat, RunStatus::AwaitingApproval).await;
    let dot = made_dot(&t, &maker, "Blog Watcher").await.expect("made");
    assert_eq!(dot.made.clone().unwrap().run_id, child.id);
    assert_eq!(
        done(&t, &child, &format!("approval:{}", first.id)).await,
        MADE
    );
    assert!(report(&llm.requests()[2]).contains(MADE));
    // No grant was written: the model cannot issue the approved call a second time.
    assert!(!t
        .rt
        .store()
        .take_grant(
            &chat.root_run_id,
            "MakeDots",
            &grant_key("MakeDots", &first.input)
        )
        .await
        .unwrap());
    let second = parked(&t, &child).await;
    assert_eq!(second.input, json!({"tool": "change_dot", "input": change}));
    assert_ne!(dot.spec.max_turns, 10);

    // The approved `change_dot` changes the dot, and does not let `delete_dot` through.
    let grandchild = approve(&t, &second, &child, RunStatus::AwaitingApproval).await;
    let dot = made_dot(&t, &maker, "Blog Watcher").await.expect("kept");
    assert_eq!(dot.spec.max_turns, 10);
    let third = parked(&t, &grandchild).await;
    assert_eq!(
        third.input,
        json!({"tool": "delete_dot", "input": {"dot": "Blog Watcher"}})
    );
    assert!(refused(&t, &grandchild, "c3")
        .await
        .contains("Queued for human approval"));
    assert!(made_dot(&t, &maker, "Blog Watcher").await.is_some());
    assert_eq!(llm.requests().len(), 6);
    assert_eq!(dot_names(&t).await, ["Blog Watcher", "Researcher"]);
    t.rt.shutdown();
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

**Create `crates/dots-core/src/engine/local/making_tools.rs`:**

```rust
//! The local engine's tools for making dots (dots-make-dots design sections 5 and 7 to 10):
//! `make_dot`, `change_dot`, `delete_dot`, `give_job` and `list_made_dots` are built-in
//! functions of a maker's run, shown and checked as `MakeDots` with their policy input, as an
//! approval names them, and performed by the makers' service, which the Claude engine's `dots`
//! MCP server also uses. Their names, words and arguments are `making::tools`, so both engines
//! show a model the same.
//!
//! They do not go through `tools::prepare`: their arguments are objects and lists that it does
//! not know, and an argument a tool does not have is refused in a sentence, not dropped.

use serde_json::Value;

use super::client::ToolCallRequest;
use super::mcp_tools::arguments;
use super::tools::{self, ToolOutput};
use super::Session;
use crate::checkins::CheckIns;
use crate::engine::{EngineEvent, PermissionOutcome};
use crate::making::tools::{check_arguments, policy_input, Tool, POLICY_NAME};
use crate::model::Making;

/// The function definitions of the tools for making dots, for a maker with `limits`.
pub(super) fn schemas(limits: &Making) -> Vec<Value> {
    Tool::ALL
        .into_iter()
        .map(|tool| {
            tools::tool(
                tool.name(),
                &tool.description(limits),
                tool.properties(),
                tool.required(),
            )
        })
        .collect()
}

impl Session {
    /// The tool for making dots a model's call `name` is, when the run has them
    /// (`RunTools::making`). For every other run the name is no tool at all.
    pub(super) fn making_tool(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Tool> {
        self.ctx.tools.making().and(Tool::from_name(name))
    }

    /// Shows, checks and performs a model's call of the tool for making dots `tool`, in the
    /// order Dots' own MCP server does: arguments the tool cannot read are refused before the
    /// policy is asked, then the policy is asked about the tool by name with its arguments
    /// under `MakeDots`, then the makers' service performs it. `None` when the run must stop.
    pub(super) async fn making_output(
        &self,
        call: &ToolCallRequest,
        tool: Tool,
    ) -> Option<ToolOutput> {
        let parsed = arguments(&call.arguments);
        let shown = parsed.clone().unwrap_or_else(|_| call.arguments.clone());
        let checked = policy_input(tool, &shown);
        let event = EngineEvent::ToolCall {
            id: call.id.clone(),
            tool: POLICY_NAME.to_string(),
            input: checked.clone(),
            parent: None,
        };
        if !self.emit(event).await {
            return None;
        }
        let read = parsed
            .map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", call.name))
            .and_then(|arguments| check_arguments(tool, &arguments));
        if let Err(e) = read {
            return Some(ToolOutput::err(e));
        }
        let decided = tokio::select! {
            r = self.gate.check(&self.ctx.run_id, POLICY_NAME, checked) => r,
            _ = self.ctx.cancel.cancelled() => return None,
        };
        Some(match decided {
            Ok(PermissionOutcome::Allow { input }) => self.perform_making(&input).await,
            Ok(PermissionOutcome::Deny { message }) => ToolOutput::err(message),
            Err(e) => ToolOutput::err(format!("permission check failed: {e}")),
        })
    }

    /// Performs an allowed or approved call of a tool for making dots, as this run; `checked`
    /// is its policy input. What the service refuses is an error result with its sentence. A
    /// run that does not have the tools performs nothing: an approval is not a way around the
    /// switch.
    pub(super) async fn perform_making(&self, checked: &Value) -> ToolOutput {
        let makers = self
            .checkins
            .as_ref()
            .filter(|_| self.ctx.tools.making().is_some())
            .and_then(CheckIns::makers);
        let Some(makers) = makers else {
            return ToolOutput::err("the tools for making dots are not available in this run");
        };
        match crate::making::tools::call(&makers, &self.ctx.run_id, checked).await {
            Ok(text) => ToolOutput::ok(text),
            Err(text) => ToolOutput::err(text),
        }
    }
}
```

### Task 13: The prompt tells a maker how making works and a made dot who made it

A run that has the making tools gets a `## Making dots` section in its conversation's first prompt: how to work with made dots, the dot's real limits, the engine's tool names, and the list of the dots it made. A wake is shown under `## Report from Dots` with a note that it is not the person's message. A made dot gets `## What you were made for` under its instructions. `conversation_so_far` labels a wake `Dots reported:` and a job `Job from <maker>:`. A dot with the switch off that nobody made gets a byte-identical prompt.

The words a model reads, pinned by `engine_prompt_test` (Claude engine names shown; the local engine has the bare names):

> ## Making dots
>
> You can make dots that work for you and give them jobs.
>
> - Make a dot for work that repeats, runs on a schedule, or can go on while you do something else. Do small one-off work yourself. Reuse a dot before making another: the list below is from the start of this conversation, and `mcp__dots__list_made_dots` gives it as it is now.
> - `mcp__dots__make_dot` makes a dot at once when it is within your reach: the dot holds nothing you do not hold yourself (your folder or one below it, your permissions or a weaker preset, Library items and variables you have, limits no higher than yours). If you ask for more, or pass your limit of dots (3 in one run, 10 kept), nothing is made yet: the request waits for the person. Do not wait for it and do not ask again: carry on with other work or end your turn, and Dots wakes you with their answer. At most 3 requests can wait at once.
> - `mcp__dots__give_job` returns at once. Do not wait for the job or check on it: Dots wakes you in this conversation with how the job ended and the dot's final message. A dot does one job from this conversation at a time: a second one is refused until the first ends. At most 6 jobs between two messages of the person; after that, report to the person.
> - `mcp__dots__change_dot` changes a dot you made and `mcp__dots__delete_dot` deletes one for good. A delete may wait for the person's approval. Dots you did not make are not yours to change, delete or give jobs to.
> - What the dots you made spend counts toward your own daily spend cap.
> - Never put the value of a secret in a dot's instructions or in a job. A dot gets variables by name, through `mcp__dots__make_dot` or `mcp__dots__change_dot`.
>
> Dots you made:
>
> - "Blog Watcher": Watches three blogs; schedule: daily at 09:00

> ## Report from Dots
>
> This is a report from Dots, not a message from the person: a job you gave to a dot you made has ended, or the person answered a request of yours. Your answer is shown to the person.

> ## What you were made for
>
> You were made by the dot Researcher. You cannot make dots yourself. Your purpose: Watches three blogs

The maker is not named when it is deleted or when the run is a job (the `## Job` note names it); "You cannot make dots yourself." is left out when the person switched making on for the made dot.

```rust
/// The `## Making dots` section as a maker with the limits 2 and 7 reads it, without its list:
/// `names` are the engine's names of `make_dot`, `change_dot`, `delete_dot`, `give_job` and
/// `list_made_dots`.
fn making_rules(names: [&str; 5]) -> String {
    let [make, change, delete, give, list] = names;
    format!(
        "\n## Making dots\n\n\
         You can make dots that work for you and give them jobs.\n\n\
         - Make a dot for work that repeats, runs on a schedule, or can go on while you do \
         something else. Do small one-off work yourself. Reuse a dot before making another: the \
         list below is from the start of this conversation, and `{list}` gives it as it is now.\n\
         - `{make}` makes a dot at once when it is within your reach: the dot holds nothing you \
         do not hold yourself (your folder or one below it, your permissions or a weaker preset, \
         Library items and variables you have, limits no higher than yours). If you ask for \
         more, or pass your limit of dots (2 in one run, 7 kept), nothing is made yet: the \
         request waits for the person. Do not wait for it and do not ask again: carry on with \
         other work or end your turn, and Dots wakes you with their answer. At most 3 requests \
         can wait at once.\n\
         - `{give}` returns at once. Do not wait for the job or check on it: Dots wakes you in \
         this conversation with how the job ended and the dot's final message. A dot does one \
         job from this conversation at a time: a second one is refused until the first ends. At \
         most 6 jobs between two messages of the person; after that, report to the person.\n\
         - `{change}` changes a dot you made and `{delete}` deletes one for good. A delete may \
         wait for the person's approval. Dots you did not make are not yours to change, delete \
         or give jobs to.\n\
         - What the dots you made spend counts toward your own daily spend cap.\n\
         - Never put the value of a secret in a dot's instructions or in a job. A dot gets \
         variables by name, through `{make}` or `{change}`.\n\n"
    )
}

/// A dot `maker` made, for `purpose`.
fn made_by(maker: &dots_core::model::Dot, name: &str, purpose: &str) -> dots_core::model::Dot {
    let mut dot = fake_dot(name, Path::new("C:/repo"), WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    dot.spec.name = name.to_string();
    dot.made = Some(Made {
        by_dot_id: Some(maker.id.clone()),
        by_name: maker.spec.name.clone(),
        run_id: "RUN0".into(),
        purpose: purpose.to_string(),
    });
    dot
}

/// A maker's first prompt ends with how making works (dots-make-dots design section 11): the
/// rules in a few lines, with the dot's own limits and the engine's names of the tools, and
/// the dots it made. Nothing else in the prompt changes.
#[test]
fn a_makers_first_prompt_says_how_making_works_in_its_engines_names() {
    let limits = Making {
        on: true,
        per_run: 2,
        total: 7,
    };
    let cases = [
        (
            EngineKind::Claude,
            [
                "mcp__dots__make_dot",
                "mcp__dots__change_dot",
                "mcp__dots__delete_dot",
                "mcp__dots__give_job",
                "mcp__dots__list_made_dots",
            ],
        ),
        (
            EngineKind::Local,
            [
                "make_dot",
                "change_dot",
                "delete_dot",
                "give_job",
                "list_made_dots",
            ],
        ),
    ];
    for (engine, names) in cases {
        let mut maker = fake_dot("Researcher", Path::new("C:/repo"), WorkspaceMode::Folder);
        maker.spec.engine = engine;
        maker.spec.making = limits;
        let mut watcher = made_by(&maker, "Blog Watcher", "Watches three blogs");
        watcher.spec.schedule = Some(
            serde_json::from_value(json!({"rule": {"kind": "daily", "time": "09:00"}})).unwrap(),
        );
        let mut sorter = made_by(&maker, "Sorter", "Sorts the inbox");
        sorter.spec.enabled = false;
        let made = [watcher, sorter];
        let run = fake_run(
            TriggerKind::Chat,
            Some(json!({"message": "watch three blogs", "typed": true})),
            None,
        );
        let prompt = |parts| build_prompt_full(&maker, &run, Path::new("C:/ws"), at(), "", parts);
        let plain = prompt(PromptParts::default());
        assert!(!plain.contains("## Making dots"), "{plain}");
        assert!(!plain.contains("make_dot"), "{plain}");

        let with_dots = prompt(PromptParts {
            making: Some(MakerPart {
                limits,
                made: &made,
            }),
            ..PromptParts::default()
        });
        assert_eq!(
            with_dots,
            format!(
                "{plain}{}Dots you made:\n\n\
                 - \"Blog Watcher\": Watches three blogs; schedule: daily at 09:00\n\
                 - \"Sorter\": Sorts the inbox; no schedule; switched off\n",
                making_rules(names)
            ),
            "{engine:?}"
        );
        if engine == EngineKind::Local {
            assert!(!with_dots.contains("mcp__dots__"), "{with_dots}");
        }

        let none_yet = prompt(PromptParts {
            making: Some(MakerPart { limits, made: &[] }),
            ..PromptParts::default()
        });
        assert_eq!(
            none_yet,
            format!("{plain}{}You have made no dots yet.\n", making_rules(names)),
            "{engine:?}"
        );

        // A run that goes on in a session has the section from its first prompt.
        let next = fake_run(
            TriggerKind::Chat,
            Some(json!({"message": "and a fourth", "typed": true})),
            Some("s"),
        );
        let p = build_prompt_full(
            &maker,
            &next,
            Path::new("C:/ws"),
            at(),
            "",
            PromptParts {
                making: Some(MakerPart {
                    limits,
                    made: &made,
                }),
                ..PromptParts::default()
            },
        );
        assert_eq!(p, "and a fourth");
    }
}

/// A wake (dots-make-dots design sections 7.2 and 8) is Dots' own report, and the maker's
/// prompt says so, in a first prompt and in one that goes on in a session.
#[test]
fn a_wake_is_shown_as_a_report_from_dots_not_as_the_persons_message() {
    let dot = fake_dot("d", Path::new("C:/repo"), WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    let payload = json!({"message": "\"Blog Watcher\" finished the job.", "wake_id": "W1"});
    let note = "This is a report from Dots, not a message from the person: a job you gave to a \
                dot you made has ended, or the person answered a request of yours. Your answer \
                is shown to the person.";
    assert_eq!(WAKE_NOTE, note);

    let first = fake_run(TriggerKind::Chat, Some(payload.clone()), None);
    let p = build_prompt(&dot, &first, Path::new("C:/ws"), at(), "", &[]);
    assert!(
        p.starts_with("Do the thing.\n\n---\n\n## Report from Dots\n\n"),
        "{p}"
    );
    assert!(
        p.contains(&format!(
            "## Report from Dots\n\n{note}\n\n\"Blog Watcher\" finished the job.\n\n## Standing \
             rules"
        )),
        "{p}"
    );
    assert!(!p.contains("## Message from the user"), "{p}");
    assert!(!p.contains("## Chat with the person"), "{p}");

    let next = fake_run(TriggerKind::Chat, Some(payload.clone()), Some("s"));
    assert_eq!(
        build_prompt(&dot, &next, Path::new("C:/ws"), at(), "", &[]),
        format!("{note}\n\n\"Blog Watcher\" finished the job.")
    );

    // A webhook's payload may hold any key: it is no wake.
    let webhook = fake_run(TriggerKind::Webhook, Some(payload), None);
    let p = build_prompt(&dot, &webhook, Path::new("C:/ws"), at(), "", &[]);
    assert!(!p.contains("Report from Dots"), "{p}");
    assert!(!p.contains("not a message from the person"), "{p}");
}

/// A made dot's first prompt says, after its instructions, who made it and what for
/// (dots-make-dots design sections 3 and 9), and that it cannot make dots.
#[test]
fn a_made_dot_is_told_who_made_it_and_what_for() {
    let maker = fake_dot("Researcher", Path::new("C:/repo"), WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    let plain = fake_dot("Blog Watcher", Path::new("C:/repo"), WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    let made = made_by(&maker, "Blog Watcher", "Watches three blogs");
    let run = fake_run(TriggerKind::Manual, None, None);
    let prompt = |dot: &dots_core::model::Dot, run: &Run, global: &str| {
        build_prompt(dot, run, Path::new("C:/ws"), at(), global, &[])
    };

    // The whole prompt of the same dot that nobody made, with the one section added.
    let before = prompt(&plain, &run, "");
    let (instructions, rest) = before.split_once("\n\n---\n\n").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(instructions, "Do the thing.");
    assert_eq!(
        prompt(&made, &run, ""),
        format!(
            "Do the thing.\n\n## What you were made for\n\nYou were made by the dot Researcher. \
             You cannot make dots yourself. Your purpose: Watches three blogs\n\n---\n\n{rest}"
        )
    );
    // Under the dot's own instructions, also when every dot's come first.
    let p = prompt(&made, &run, "Be brief.");
    assert!(
        p.starts_with(
            "## Instructions for every dot\n\nBe brief.\n\n## Instructions for this dot\n\nDo \
             the thing.\n\n## What you were made for\n\nYou were made by the dot Researcher."
        ),
        "{p}"
    );

    // The maker is deleted: only what the dot is for.
    let mut orphan = made.clone();
    orphan.made.as_mut().unwrap().by_dot_id = None;
    let p = prompt(&orphan, &run, "");
    assert!(
        p.starts_with(
            "Do the thing.\n\n## What you were made for\n\nYou cannot make dots yourself. Your \
             purpose: Watches three blogs\n\n---\n\n"
        ),
        "{p}"
    );
    assert!(!p.contains("Researcher"), "{p}");

    // A job names the maker itself (`job_note`), so the section does not name it again.
    let job = fake_run(
        TriggerKind::Chat,
        Some(json!({"message": "Read the blogs.", "job_id": "J1", "job_from": "Researcher"})),
        None,
    );
    let p = prompt(&made, &job, "");
    assert!(
        p.starts_with(
            "Do the thing.\n\n## What you were made for\n\nYou cannot make dots yourself. Your \
             purpose: Watches three blogs\n\n---\n\n## Job\n\nJob from Researcher (the dot that \
             made you)."
        ),
        "{p}"
    );
    assert_eq!(p.matches("made you").count(), 1, "{p}");
    assert_eq!(p.matches("You were made by").count(), 0, "{p}");

    // The person switched "Can make dots" on for it: its run has the tools, so the prompt does
    // not say it has none.
    let p = build_prompt_full(
        &made,
        &run,
        Path::new("C:/ws"),
        at(),
        "",
        PromptParts {
            making: Some(MakerPart {
                limits: Making {
                    on: true,
                    ..Making::default()
                },
                made: &[],
            }),
            ..PromptParts::default()
        },
    );
    assert!(
        p.starts_with(
            "Do the thing.\n\n## What you were made for\n\nYou were made by the dot Researcher. \
             Your purpose: Watches three blogs\n\n---\n\n"
        ),
        "{p}"
    );
    assert!(!p.contains("cannot make dots"), "{p}");
    assert!(p.contains("## Making dots"), "{p}");

    // A run that goes on in a session sends its message alone, as for any dot.
    let next = fake_run(
        TriggerKind::Chat,
        Some(json!({"message": "go on"})),
        Some("s"),
    );
    assert_eq!(prompt(&made, &next, ""), "go on");
    assert_eq!(prompt(&made, &next, ""), prompt(&plain, &next, ""));
}

/// A topic's conversation so far (topic tools spec section 4.4) does not put Dots' reports or
/// a maker's jobs in the person's mouth.
#[test]
fn a_conversation_so_far_names_a_wake_and_a_job_as_what_they_are() {
    let wake = fake_run(
        TriggerKind::Chat,
        Some(json!({"message": "\"Blog Watcher\" finished the job.", "wake_id": "W1"})),
        None,
    );
    let job = fake_run(
        TriggerKind::Chat,
        Some(json!({"message": "Read the blogs.", "job_id": "J1", "job_from": "Researcher"})),
        None,
    );
    let said = fake_run(
        TriggerKind::Chat,
        Some(json!({"message": "thanks", "typed": true})),
        None,
    );
    let text = dots_core::prompt::conversation_so_far(&[wake, job, said]);
    assert_eq!(
        text,
        "- Dots reported: \"Blog Watcher\" finished the job.\n\
         - Job from Researcher: Read the blogs.\n\
         - The person: thanks\n"
    );
}
```

```rust
/// What a recorded request's run was told last: its prompt.
fn told(req: &Value) -> String {
    messages(req)
        .iter()
        .rfind(|m| m["role"] == "user")
        .and_then(|m| m["content"].as_str())
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .to_string()
}

/// The prompt of the one recorded request whose run was told `part`.
fn told_with(reqs: &[Value], part: &str) -> String {
    let with: Vec<String> = reqs.iter().map(told).filter(|p| p.contains(part)).collect();
    assert_eq!(with.len(), 1, "{part:?}: {with:#?}");
    with.into_iter().next().unwrap()
}

/// The prompt says how making works (dots-make-dots design section 11) exactly where the run
/// has the tools: a maker's run, with its own limits and the local engine's names; not a dot
/// with the switch off, and not a maker whose policy denies `MakeDots`.
#[tokio::test]
async fn only_a_makers_prompt_says_how_making_works() {
    let t = start().await;
    let llm = Llm::start(vec![
        text("Plain is done."),
        text("The maker is done."),
        text("Denied is done."),
    ])
    .await;
    let plain = create(&t, &llm, "Plain", |s| s.making.on = false).await;
    let plain_chat = t.rt.chat(&plain.id, "hello plain", None).await.unwrap();
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &plain_chat.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 30).await;
    let maker = create(&t, &llm, "Researcher", |s| {
        s.making.per_run = 2;
        s.making.total = 7;
    })
    .await;
    let maker_chat = t.rt.chat(&maker.id, "hello maker", None).await.unwrap();
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &maker_chat.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 30).await;
    let denied = create(&t, &llm, "Denied", |s| {
        s.policy
            .rules
            .insert(0, Rule::new("MakeDots", Action::Deny));
    })
    .await;
    let denied_chat = t.rt.chat(&denied.id, "hello denied", None).await.unwrap();
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &denied_chat.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 30).await;

    let reqs = llm.requests();
    assert_eq!(reqs.len(), 3);
    let section = making_section(
        EngineKind::Local,
        &MakerPart {
            limits: maker.spec.making,
            made: &[],
        },
    );
    let prompt = told(&reqs[1]);
    assert!(
        prompt.contains(&format!("\n## Making dots\n\n{section}")),
        "{prompt}"
    );
    assert!(
        prompt.contains("`make_dot` makes a dot at once"),
        "{prompt}"
    );
    assert!(prompt.contains("(2 in one run, 7 kept)"), "{prompt}");
    assert!(prompt.contains("You have made no dots yet.\n"), "{prompt}");
    assert!(!prompt.contains("mcp__dots__make_dot"), "{prompt}");
    for other in [&reqs[0], &reqs[2]] {
        let prompt = told(other);
        assert!(prompt.contains("## Standing rules"), "{prompt}");
        assert!(!prompt.contains("## Making dots"), "{prompt}");
        for name in NAMES {
            assert!(!prompt.contains(name), "{prompt}");
        }
    }
    t.rt.shutdown();
}

/// A workflow step's run of a maker has no tools for making dots (design section 5), so its
/// prompt does not name them.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_workflow_steps_prompt_of_a_maker_does_not_say_how_making_works() {
    let t = start().await;
    let llm = Llm::start(vec![text("Researched.")]).await;
    let maker = create(&t, &llm, "Researcher", |_| {}).await;
    let started = run_step(&t, &maker).await;
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(60);
    loop {
        let wr = t.rt.workflows().get(&started.id).await.unwrap();
        if wr.status == WorkflowRunStatus::Succeeded {
            break;
        }
        assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "{wr:#?}");
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
    }
    let reqs = llm.requests();
    assert_eq!(reqs.len(), 1);
    let prompt = told(&reqs[0]);
    assert!(prompt.contains("## Standing rules"), "{prompt}");
    assert!(!prompt.contains("## Making dots"), "{prompt}");
    for name in NAMES {
        assert!(!prompt.contains(name), "{prompt}");
    }
    t.rt.shutdown();
}

/// From making to the wake, what each run is told (design sections 8 and 11): the made dot's
/// job says who made it once; the maker's wake is a report from Dots, not the person's
/// message; the maker's next conversation lists the dot it made; and the made dot's own chat
/// with the person says who made it.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_made_dot_and_its_maker_are_told_who_is_who() {
    let t = start().await;
    // The maker's second request and the made dot's first come in either order.
    let llm = Llm::start(vec![
        call(
            "m1",
            "make_dot",
            json!({
                "name": "Blog Watcher",
                "instructions": "Read the three blogs and list what is new.",
                "purpose": "Reads the feeds",
                "first_job": "Read them now."
            }),
        ),
        text("ok"),
        text("ok"),
        text("ok"),
        text("ok"),
        text("ok"),
    ])
    .await;
    let maker = create(&t, &llm, "Researcher", |_| {}).await;
    let chat = t.rt.chat(&maker.id, "hello maker", None).await.unwrap();
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &chat.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 30).await;
    // The job ends and the maker is woken in the same topic: one more run of it.
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(60);
    let woken = loop {
        let thread = t.rt.store().list_thread(&chat.root_run_id).await.unwrap();
        if thread.len() == 2 && thread[1].status == RunStatus::Succeeded {
            break thread[1].clone();
        }
        assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "{thread:#?}");
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
    };
    assert!(woken.payload.as_ref().unwrap().get("wake_id").is_some());
    let watcher = made_dot(&t, &maker, "Blog Watcher").await.expect("made");

    let again = t.rt.chat(&maker.id, "hello again", None).await.unwrap();
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &again.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 30).await;
    let direct = t.rt.chat(&watcher.id, "hello watcher", None).await.unwrap();
    wait_status(t.rt.store(), &direct.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, 30).await;

    let reqs = llm.requests();
    assert_eq!(reqs.len(), 6);
    // The job: under the made dot's instructions, what it is for; the job's note names the
    // maker, once.
    let job = told_with(&reqs, "## Job");
    assert!(
        job.starts_with(
            "Read the three blogs and list what is new.\n\n## What you were made for\n\nYou \
             cannot make dots yourself. Your purpose: Reads the feeds\n\n---\n\n## Job\n\nJob \
             from Researcher (the dot that made you). When you finish, your final message goes \
             back to Researcher.\n\nRead them now.\n\n## Standing rules"
        ),
        "{job}"
    );
    assert_eq!(job.matches("made you").count(), 1, "{job}");
    assert!(!job.contains("## Making dots"), "{job}");

    // The wake goes on in the maker's session: Dots' note, then the report.
    let wake = told_with(&reqs, "finished the job");
    assert!(
        wake.starts_with(&format!(
            "{WAKE_NOTE}\n\n\"Blog Watcher\" finished the job.\n\nIts final message:\nok"
        )),
        "{wake}"
    );
    assert!(!wake.contains("Message from the user"), "{wake}");

    // The maker's next conversation lists the dot it made.
    let next = told_with(&reqs, "hello again");
    assert!(
        next.ends_with(
            "variables by name, through `make_dot` or `change_dot`.\n\nDots you made:\n\n- \
             \"Blog Watcher\": Reads the feeds; no schedule\n"
        ),
        "{next}"
    );

    // The person's own chat with the made dot names its maker.
    let direct = told_with(&reqs, "hello watcher");
    assert!(
        direct.starts_with(
            "Read the three blogs and list what is new.\n\n## What you were made for\n\nYou \
             were made by the dot Researcher. You cannot make dots yourself. Your purpose: Reads \
             the feeds\n\n## Your recent runs\n\n"
        ),
        "{direct}"
    );
    assert!(!direct.contains("## Making dots"), "{direct}");
    t.rt.shutdown();
}
```

```rust
/// The prompt of the started CLI whose prompt holds `message`.
async fn prompt_of(t: &T, message: &str) -> String {
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(60);
    loop {
        let prompt = std::fs::read_to_string(&t.args_out)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|text| serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&text).ok())
            .and_then(|r| r["prompt"].as_str().map(str::to_string))
            .filter(|p| p.contains(message));
        if let Some(prompt) = prompt {
            return prompt;
        }
        assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "no CLI started for {message:?}");
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
    }
}

/// The prompt says how making works (dots-make-dots design section 11) exactly where the run
/// has the tools: a maker's run, with its own limits and the names the `claude` CLI knows the
/// tools by; not a dot with the switch off, and not a maker whose policy denies `MakeDots`.
#[tokio::test]
async fn only_a_makers_prompt_says_how_making_works() {
    let t = start(held()).await;
    let plain = create(&t, "Plain", |s| s.making.on = false).await;
    let plain_chat = t.rt.chat(&plain.id, "hello plain", None).await.unwrap();
    let plain_prompt = prompt_of(&t, "hello plain").await;
    let maker = create(&t, "Researcher", |s| {
        s.making.per_run = 2;
        s.making.total = 7;
    })
    .await;
    let maker_chat = t.rt.chat(&maker.id, "hello maker", None).await.unwrap();
    let maker_prompt = prompt_of(&t, "hello maker").await;
    let denied = create(&t, "Denied", |s| {
        s.policy
            .rules
            .insert(0, Rule::new("MakeDots", Action::Deny));
    })
    .await;
    let denied_chat = t.rt.chat(&denied.id, "hello denied", None).await.unwrap();
    let denied_prompt = prompt_of(&t, "hello denied").await;

    let section = making_section(
        EngineKind::Claude,
        &MakerPart {
            limits: maker.spec.making,
            made: &[],
        },
    );
    assert!(
        maker_prompt.contains(&format!("\n## Making dots\n\n{section}")),
        "{maker_prompt}"
    );
    assert!(
        maker_prompt.contains("`mcp__dots__make_dot` makes a dot at once"),
        "{maker_prompt}"
    );
    assert!(
        maker_prompt.contains("(2 in one run, 7 kept)"),
        "{maker_prompt}"
    );
    for name in CLI_NAMES {
        assert!(maker_prompt.contains(&format!("`{name}`")), "{name}");
    }
    for prompt in [&plain_prompt, &denied_prompt] {
        assert!(prompt.contains("## Standing rules"), "{prompt}");
        assert!(!prompt.contains("## Making dots"), "{prompt}");
        for name in NAMES {
            assert!(!prompt.contains(name), "{prompt}");
        }
    }
    finish(&t, &[&plain_chat, &maker_chat, &denied_chat]).await;
}

/// A workflow step's run of a maker has no tools for making dots (design section 5), so its
/// prompt does not name them.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_workflow_steps_prompt_of_a_maker_does_not_say_how_making_works() {
    let t = start(json!([init(), success()])).await;
    let maker = create(&t, "Researcher", |_| {}).await;
    let started = run_step(&t, &maker).await;
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(60);
    loop {
        let wr = t.rt.workflows().get(&started.id).await.unwrap();
        if wr.status == WorkflowRunStatus::Succeeded {
            break;
        }
        assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "{wr:#?}");
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
    }
    let recorded: Value =
        serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(&t.args_out).unwrap()).unwrap();
    let prompt = recorded["prompt"].as_str().unwrap();
    assert!(prompt.contains("## Standing rules"), "{prompt}");
    assert!(!prompt.contains("## Making dots"), "{prompt}");
    for name in NAMES {
        assert!(!prompt.contains(name), "{prompt}");
    }
    t.rt.shutdown();
}
```

```rust
/// What the `## Making dots` section of a maker's prompt is written from (dots-make-dots design
/// section 11).
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct MakerPart<'a> {
    /// The maker's limits, as the run's tools have them (`RunTools::making`).
    pub limits: Making,
    /// The dots the maker made that exist now (`Store::list_made_dots`), for the list that
    /// lets it reuse a dot before making another.
    pub made: &'a [Dot],
}

/// What opens a wake's message for the maker (dots-make-dots design sections 7.2 and 8): the
/// words are Dots' own, not the person's.
pub const WAKE_NOTE: &str = "This is a report from Dots, not a message from the person: a job \
    you gave to a dot you made has ended, or the person answered a request of yours. Your answer \
    is shown to the person.";

/// The chat run `run` is a wake of a maker (`Makers::wake`): its message is Dots' own.
fn is_wake(run: &Run) -> bool {
    run.trigger == TriggerKind::Chat && run.payload.as_ref().and_then(|p| p.get(WAKE_ID)).is_some()
}

/// The `## Making dots` section of a maker's first prompt (dots-make-dots design section 11):
/// how making works in a few lines, with the maker's own limits and the names `engine`'s model
/// calls the tools by, then the dots it made with purpose and schedule. The tools' own
/// descriptions (`making::tools::Tool::description`) hold the detail, and the core enforces
/// every rule named here (design section 12); the prompt only explains them. It ends with a
/// newline.
pub fn making_section(engine: EngineKind, part: &MakerPart<'_>) -> String {
    let make = MakingTool::MakeDot.model_name(engine);
    let change = MakingTool::ChangeDot.model_name(engine);
    let delete = MakingTool::DeleteDot.model_name(engine);
    let give = MakingTool::GiveJob.model_name(engine);
    let list = MakingTool::ListMadeDots.model_name(engine);
    let Making { per_run, total, .. } = part.limits;
    let mut out = format!(
        "You can make dots that work for you and give them jobs.\n\n\
         - Make a dot for work that repeats, runs on a schedule, or can go on while you do \
         something else. Do small one-off work yourself. Reuse a dot before making another: the \
         list below is from the start of this conversation, and `{list}` gives it as it is now.\n\
         - `{make}` makes a dot at once when it is within your reach: the dot holds nothing you \
         do not hold yourself (your folder or one below it, your permissions or a weaker preset, \
         Library items and variables you have, limits no higher than yours). If you ask for \
         more, or pass your limit of dots ({per_run} in one run, {total} kept), nothing is made \
         yet: the request waits for the person. Do not wait for it and do not ask again: carry \
         on with other work or end your turn, and Dots wakes you with their answer. At most \
         {MAX_WAITING_REQUESTS} requests can wait at once.\n\
         - `{give}` returns at once. Do not wait for the job or check on it: Dots wakes you in \
         this conversation with how the job ended and the dot's final message. A dot does one \
         job from this conversation at a time: a second one is refused until the first ends. At \
         most {MAX_JOBS_BETWEEN_TYPED} jobs between two messages of the person; after that, \
         report to the person.\n\
         - `{change}` changes a dot you made and `{delete}` deletes one for good. A delete may \
         wait for the person's approval. Dots you did not make are not yours to change, delete \
         or give jobs to.\n\
         - What the dots you made spend counts toward your own daily spend cap.\n\
         - Never put the value of a secret in a dot's instructions or in a job. A dot gets \
         variables by name, through `{make}` or `{change}`.\n\n"
    );
    if part.made.is_empty() {
        out.push_str("You have made no dots yet.\n");
        return out;
    }
    out.push_str("Dots you made:\n\n");
    for dot in part.made {
        let purpose = dot.made.as_ref().map(|made| made.purpose.as_str());
        out.push_str(&format!(
            "- \"{}\": {}; {}",
            dot.spec.name,
            purpose.unwrap_or_default(),
            match &dot.spec.schedule {
                Some(schedule) => format!("schedule: {}", schedule_words(schedule)),
                None => "no schedule".to_string(),
            }
        ));
        if !dot.spec.enabled {
            out.push_str("; switched off");
        }
        out.push('\n');
    }
    out
}

/// What a made dot's first prompt says under its instructions (dots-make-dots design sections
/// 3 and 9): who made it, that it cannot make dots, and what it is for, in the maker's own
/// line. `named` is false when the maker is not to be named: it is deleted, or the run is a job
/// whose note names it (`job_note`). `can_make` is true when the person switched "Can make
/// dots" on for the made dot and the run has the tools.
fn made_section(made: &Made, named: bool, can_make: bool) -> String {
    let mut out = String::from("## What you were made for\n\n");
    if named {
        out.push_str(&format!("You were made by the dot {}. ", made.by_name));
    }
    if !can_make {
        out.push_str("You cannot make dots yourself. ");
    }
    out.push_str(&format!("Your purpose: {}", made.purpose.trim()));
    out
}
```

### Task 14: The runtime gives the app make requests, the making cards of a topic, and Inbox items

Everything plan B's commands and screens need, so plan B touches no core logic: the ask card and the person's answer on `Runtime`; a topic's making log as cards that carry what each card shows; waiting requests in the Inbox and its count; "N of M" for a maker's row; two events the app turns into notifications. It also closes what earlier tasks left open when the person deletes a made dot: its open job ends and wakes the maker once, its waiting change request goes, and every topic that showed the dot is told.
