```rust
//! What the app needs of making, on `Runtime` (dots-make-dots design section 11): the ask card
//! and the person's answer, the waiting requests in the Inbox and its count, the cards of a
//! maker's chat topic, the "uses" sentence of a made dot, a maker's count of kept dots, the
//! events the app notifies on, and what a person's delete of a made dot or of a maker leaves.

mod common;

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;

use chrono::{TimeDelta, Utc};
use common::clock::FakeClock;
use common::fake_openbao::FakeOpenBao;
use common::orgs::{
    at, code, keys, openbao, policy, public_key, roster, sign, sign_roster, token, ACME, ACME_NAME,
    ISSUED, START, TOKEN,
};
use common::{fake_dot, spec};
use dots_core::accounts::identity;
use dots_core::events::RuntimeEvent;
use dots_core::inbox::{InboxKey, InboxKind};
use dots_core::library::Uses;
use dots_core::making::cards::{uses_line, CardWhat, JobCard, MakingCard};
use dots_core::making::jobs::{deleted_message, JobEnd, JobStatus, MakingJob};
use dots_core::making::log::{MakingEvent, MakingEventKind};
use dots_core::making::manage::{ChangeDot, ChangeOutcome};
use dots_core::making::reach::Wanted;
use dots_core::making::requests::{
    MakeDecision, MakeRequest, PendingMakeRequest, RequestKind, RequestStatus,
};
use dots_core::making::service::{MakeDot, MakeOutcome};
use dots_core::model::{Dot, DotSpec, Making, NewRun, Run, RunStatus, TriggerKind, WorkspaceMode};
use dots_core::schedule::Schedule;
use dots_core::vault::{Grants, MemorySecrets};
use dots_core::{Config, Error, Runtime};
use serde_json::json;
use tempfile::TempDir;
use tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver;

struct T {
    dir: TempDir,
    rt: Runtime,
}

impl T {
    /// The maker's folder.
    fn work(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.dir.path().join("work")
    }
}

/// As `making_request_test.rs` has it: no queued run starts, so a run is put in the state a
/// test needs by hand, and a wake of a busy topic waits where a test can read it.
fn config(dir: &TempDir) -> Config {
    let mut cfg = Config::new(dir.path().join("data"));
    cfg.port = 0;
    cfg.claude_path = Some(PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake-claude")));
    cfg.new_dot_root = dir.path().join("Dots");
    cfg.secrets = Some(Arc::new(MemorySecrets::new()));
    cfg.max_concurrent_runs = 0;
    cfg
}

async fn start() -> T {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let rt = Runtime::start(config(&dir)).await.unwrap();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path().join("work")).unwrap();
    T { dir, rt }
}

/// The spec of a dot named Researcher that works in the test's `work` folder itself and may
/// make dots.
fn maker_spec(t: &T) -> DotSpec {
    let mut s = spec("Researcher");
    s.workdir = t.work().to_string_lossy().to_string();
    s.workspace_mode = WorkspaceMode::Folder;
    s.making.on = true;
    s
}

/// A maker named Researcher, created as the person creates a dot.
async fn maker(t: &T) -> Dot {
    t.rt.create_dot(maker_spec(t), None, None).await.unwrap()
}

/// Puts the queued run `run_id` in the running state by hand, with a session, as a run the
/// runner started.
async fn started(t: &T, run_id: &str) -> Run {
    assert!(t.rt.store().claim_run(run_id).await.unwrap());
    t.rt.store()
        .set_session(run_id, &format!("session-{run_id}"))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    t.rt.store().get_run(run_id).await.unwrap()
}

/// A run of `dot` that is running and starts a topic, with `payload`.
async fn live_run_with(t: &T, dot: &Dot, trigger: TriggerKind, payload: serde_json::Value) -> Run {
    let mut new = NewRun::new(&dot.id, trigger);
    new.payload = Some(payload);
    let run = t.rt.store().create_run(&new).await.unwrap();
    started(t, &run.id).await
}

/// A run of `dot` that is running: a chat the person started with a typed message.
async fn live_run(t: &T, dot: &Dot) -> Run {
    let typed = json!({"message": "watch three blogs", "typed": true});
    live_run_with(t, dot, TriggerKind::Chat, typed).await
}

/// What a maker asks for a dot named `name`, with nothing but what a new dot needs.
fn ask(name: &str) -> MakeDot {
    MakeDot {
        purpose: "Reads the feeds".into(),
        wanted: Wanted {
            name: Some(name.into()),
            instructions: Some("Read the three blogs and list what is new.".into()),
            ..Wanted::default()
        },
        first_job: None,
    }
}

/// The same with the browser, which no maker of these tests has: one extra.
fn ask_browser(name: &str) -> MakeDot {
    let mut asked = ask(name);
    asked.wanted.browser = Some(true);
    asked
}

/// Makes the dot `asked`, which must be within reach and within the limits.
async fn make_as(t: &T, run: &Run, asked: MakeDot) -> Dot {
    match t.rt.makers().make_dot(&run.id, asked).await.unwrap() {
        MakeOutcome::Made { dot, .. } => dot,
        other => panic!("not made: {other:?}"),
    }
}

async fn make(t: &T, run: &Run, name: &str) -> Dot {
    make_as(t, run, ask(name)).await
}

/// Asks for a dot that must come back waiting for the person: its request.
async fn request(t: &T, run: &Run, ask: MakeDot) -> MakeRequest {
    match t.rt.makers().make_dot(&run.id, ask).await.unwrap() {
        MakeOutcome::Waiting { request, .. } => request,
        other => panic!("made: {other:?}"),
    }
}

/// Asks to give the made dot `name` the browser, which must come back waiting for the person:
/// the change request.
async fn change_request(t: &T, run: &Run, name: &str) -> MakeRequest {
    let change = ChangeDot {
        dot: name.into(),
        purpose: None,
        wanted: Wanted {
            browser: Some(true),
            ..Wanted::default()
        },
    };
    match t.rt.makers().change_dot(&run.id, change).await.unwrap() {
        ChangeOutcome::Waiting { request, .. } => request,
        other => panic!("changed: {other:?}"),
    }
}

/// Every `minutes`, as a tool call carries it.
fn every(minutes: u32) -> Schedule {
    serde_json::from_value(json!({
        "rule": {"kind": "every", "minutes": minutes},
        "catch_up": true,
        "until": null
    }))
    .unwrap()
}

/// The makers' log of the topic `run` belongs to.
async fn log(t: &T, run: &Run) -> Vec<MakingEvent> {
    t.rt.store()
        .list_making_events(&run.root_run_id)
        .await
        .unwrap()
}

/// The cards of the topic `run` belongs to.
async fn cards(t: &T, run: &Run) -> Vec<MakingCard> {
    t.rt.making_cards(&run.root_run_id).await.unwrap()
}

/// The jobs given in the maker's topic `run` belongs to, oldest first.
async fn jobs(t: &T, run: &Run) -> Vec<MakingJob> {
    t.rt.store()
        .making_jobs_of_topic(&run.root_run_id)
        .await
        .unwrap()
}

/// Gives the made dot `name` a job from the maker's run `run` and starts its run by hand: the
/// job and its run.
async fn working_job(t: &T, run: &Run, name: &str) -> (MakingJob, Run) {
    t.rt.makers()
        .give_job(&run.id, name, "Read the blogs now.")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let job = jobs(t, run).await.pop().expect("a job was stored");
    let its = started(t, job.last_run_id.as_deref().expect("the job has a run")).await;
    (job, its)
}

/// The messages of the wakes that wait, oldest first.
async fn wakes(t: &T) -> Vec<String> {
    let wakes = t.rt.store().waiting_making_wakes().await.unwrap();
    wakes.into_iter().map(|w| w.message).collect()
}

/// The topics named by the `MakingUpdated` events published since the last call.
fn updated(rx: &mut Receiver<RuntimeEvent>) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let mut seen = Vec::new();
    while let Ok(ev) = rx.try_recv() {
        if let RuntimeEvent::MakingUpdated {
            dot_id,
            root_run_id,
        } = ev
        {
            seen.push((dot_id, root_run_id));
        }
    }
    seen
}

/// The events the app notifies on that were published since the last call, as JSON.
fn notices(rx: &mut Receiver<RuntimeEvent>) -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
    let mut seen = Vec::new();
    while let Ok(ev) = rx.try_recv() {
        if matches!(
            ev,
            RuntimeEvent::MakeRequested { .. } | RuntimeEvent::DotMade { .. }
        ) {
            seen.push(serde_json::to_value(&ev).unwrap());
        }
    }
    seen
}

/// The card's part every card has, without what its kind adds.
fn head(card: &MakingCard) -> (&str, &str, &str, &str, Option<&str>, &str, &str) {
    (
        card.id.as_str(),
        card.maker_dot_id.as_str(),
        card.maker_name.as_str(),
        card.run_id.as_str(),
        card.dot_id.as_deref(),
        card.dot_name.as_str(),
        card.created_at.as_str(),
    )
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn waiting_requests_are_in_the_inbox_and_its_count_until_each_is_answered() {
    let t = start().await;
    let mut s = maker_spec(&t);
    s.making = Making {
        on: true,
        per_run: 1,
        total: 10,
    };
    let maker = t.rt.create_dot(s, None, None).await.unwrap();
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    make(&t, &run, "One").await;
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox_count().await.unwrap(), 0);

    let two = request(&t, &run, ask("Two")).await;
    let watcher = request(&t, &run, ask_browser("Blog Watcher")).await;
    let change = change_request(&t, &run, "One").await;

    // Newest first, each with what the Inbox sorts, links and titles it by.
    let inbox = t.rt.inbox().await.unwrap();
    let item = |request: &MakeRequest, title: &str, lines: &[&str]| PendingMakeRequest {
        id: request.id.clone(),
        dot_id: maker.id.clone(),
        dot_name: "Researcher".into(),
        root_run_id: run.root_run_id.clone(),
        kind: request.kind,
        name: request.name.clone(),
        purpose: "Reads the feeds".into(),
        title: title.into(),
        lines: lines.iter().map(|l| l.to_string()).collect(),
        status: RequestStatus::Waiting,
        created_at: request.created_at.clone(),
    };
    let limit = "2nd dot in this run; the limit is 1";
    assert_eq!(
        inbox.make_requests,
        [
            item(
                &change,
                "Researcher wants to give One more than it has",
                &["The browser"]
            ),
            item(
                &watcher,
                "Researcher wants to make a dot with more than it has",
                &["The browser", limit]
            ),
            item(&two, "Researcher wants to make one more dot", &[limit]),
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!(change.kind, RequestKind::Change);
    assert_eq!(
        serde_json::to_value(&inbox.make_requests[2]).unwrap(),
        json!({
            "id": two.id,
            "dot_id": maker.id,
            "dot_name": "Researcher",
            "root_run_id": run.root_run_id,
            "kind": "make",
            "name": "Two",
            "purpose": "Reads the feeds",
            "title": "Researcher wants to make one more dot",
            "lines": [limit],
            "status": "waiting",
            "created_at": two.created_at,
        })
    );
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox_count().await.unwrap(), 3);
    // They count as what the maker has for the person, as a proposal's card does.
    let overview = t.rt.dot_overview().await.unwrap();
    let row = overview.iter().find(|row| row.dot.id == maker.id).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(row.needs_you, 3);

    // The same requests as whole cards, for the Inbox's section, newest first.
    let waiting = t.rt.waiting_make_requests().await.unwrap();
    let ids: Vec<&str> = waiting.iter().map(|c| c.request.id.as_str()).collect();
    assert_eq!(ids, [&change.id, &watcher.id, &two.id]);
    assert_eq!(
        waiting[1],
        t.rt.make_request_card(&watcher.id).await.unwrap()
    );
    assert_eq!(waiting[1].maker_name, "Researcher");
    assert!(waiting[1].can_allow && waiting[1].can_without);
    assert!(waiting[2].can_allow && !waiting[2].can_without);

    // Each of the three answers takes its request out of the Inbox and the count.
    let answers = [
        (&two, MakeDecision::Allow, RequestStatus::Allowed),
        (&watcher, MakeDecision::Without, RequestStatus::MadeWithout),
        (&change, MakeDecision::Refuse, RequestStatus::Refused),
    ];
    let mut left = 3;
    for (request, decision, status) in answers {
        let after = t.rt.decide_make_request(&request.id, decision).await;
        assert_eq!(after.unwrap().status, status);
        left -= 1;
        let inbox = t.rt.inbox().await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(inbox.make_requests.len(), left);
        assert!(inbox.make_requests.iter().all(|r| r.id != request.id));
        assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox_count().await.unwrap(), left);
    }
    assert!(t.rt.waiting_make_requests().await.unwrap().is_empty());
    let overview = t.rt.dot_overview().await.unwrap();
    let row = overview.iter().find(|row| row.dot.id == maker.id).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(row.needs_you, 0);
    // An answer given twice is refused as the makers refuse it.
    assert!(matches!(
        t.rt.decide_make_request(&two.id, MakeDecision::Refuse)
            .await,
        Err(Error::Conflict(_))
    ));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_request_is_snoozed_and_marked_done_as_a_proposal_is() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    let request = request(&t, &run, ask_browser("Blog Watcher")).await;
    let key = InboxKey::new(InboxKind::MakeRequest, request.id.clone());
    let title = "Researcher wants to make a dot with more than it has";

    t.rt.inbox_snooze(std::slice::from_ref(&key), Utc::now() + TimeDelta::hours(1))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let inbox = t.rt.inbox().await.unwrap();
    assert!(inbox.make_requests.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(inbox.snoozed.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(inbox.snoozed[0].key(), key);
    assert_eq!(inbox.snoozed[0].title, title);
    assert_eq!(inbox.snoozed[0].dot_id.as_deref(), Some(maker.id.as_str()));
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox_count().await.unwrap(), 0);
    let overview = t.rt.dot_overview().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(overview[0].needs_you, 0);

    t.rt.inbox_unsnooze(&key).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox().await.unwrap().make_requests.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox_count().await.unwrap(), 1);

    // Done hides it too, as it hides a proposal; the request itself still waits.
    t.rt.inbox_done(&key).await.unwrap();
    let inbox = t.rt.inbox().await.unwrap();
    assert!(inbox.make_requests.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(inbox.done.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(inbox.done[0].title, title);
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox_count().await.unwrap(), 0);
    let card = t.rt.make_request_card(&request.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(card.request.status, RequestStatus::Waiting);
    t.rt.inbox_undo_done(&key).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox_count().await.unwrap(), 1);

    // A key of a request that is answered is no longer in the Inbox.
    t.rt.decide_make_request(&request.id, MakeDecision::Refuse)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        t.rt.inbox_done(&key).await,
        Err(Error::NotFound(_))
    ));
}

/// A runtime joined to Acme, whose signed member list the fake OpenBao serves, as
/// `making_request_test.rs` sets it up, with no run starting.
struct Acme {
    t: T,
    bao: FakeOpenBao,
    keys: minisign::KeyPair,
}

impl Acme {
    async fn start() -> Acme {
        let bao = FakeOpenBao::start().await;
        bao.allow_token(TOKEN, false);
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let mut cfg = config(&dir);
        cfg.clock = FakeClock::new(at(START));
        let rt = Runtime::start(cfg).await.unwrap();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path().join("work")).unwrap();
        Acme {
            t: T { dir, rt },
            bao,
            keys: keys(),
        }
    }

    /// Serves a member list at `seq` with an owner who is not this PC, and this PC as `role`.
    async fn serve_list(&self, seq: u64, role: &str) {
        let me = identity(self.t.rt.store()).await.unwrap().public_key;
        let member = |id: &str, email: &str, role: &str, key: &str| {
            json!({
                "id": id, "name": email, "email": email, "role": role, "keys": [key],
                "workspaces": {"default": "member"}, "added_at": "2026-10-28T09:00:00Z"
            })
        };
        let members = json!([
            member("01OWNER", "owner@acme.com", "owner", &public_key(&keys())),
            member("01ME", "me@acme.com", role, &me),
        ]);
        let extra = json!({"v": 2, "roster": "required", "admins": [], "offline_hours": 0});
        let signed = sign(&self.keys, &policy(ACME, ISSUED, extra));
        self.bao.put_env("secret", "dots", json!({}));
        self.bao.put_policy("secret", "dots", &signed);
        let list = sign_roster(&self.keys, &roster(ACME, seq, members));
        self.bao.put_roster("secret", "dots", &list);
    }

    /// Joins Acme with this PC on its member list as `role`.
    async fn join_as(&self, role: &str) {
        self.serve_list(1, role).await;
        let code = code(
            ACME,
            ACME_NAME,
            openbao(&self.bao.address(), "dots"),
            &self.keys,
        );
        let orgs = self.t.rt.vault().orgs().expect("the runtime's orgs");
        orgs.join(&code, Some(token())).await.unwrap();
    }

    /// Serves the list again at `seq` with this PC as `role`, and fetches it.
    async fn become_(&self, seq: u64, role: &str) {
        self.serve_list(seq, role).await;
        self.t.rt.refresh_org(ACME).await.unwrap();
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_viewer_sees_the_card_and_why_it_cannot_allow() {
    let a = Acme::start().await;
    let t = &a.t;
    a.join_as("member").await;
    let maker =
        t.rt.create_dot(maker_spec(t), Some(ACME.into()), None)
            .await
            .unwrap();
    let run = live_run(t, &maker).await;
    let request = request(t, &run, ask_browser("Blog Watcher")).await;
    a.become_(2, "viewer").await;

    // The request is in the Inbox for a Viewer too, and its card says why Allow is off.
    let why = "Acme Engineering: a Viewer can't create or change dots. Ask an Admin or Owner.";
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox().await.unwrap().make_requests.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox_count().await.unwrap(), 1);
    let card = t.rt.make_request_card(&request.id).await.unwrap();
    assert!(!card.can_allow && !card.can_without);
    assert_eq!(card.blocked.as_deref(), Some(why));
    assert_eq!(t.rt.waiting_make_requests().await.unwrap(), [card]);
    for decision in [MakeDecision::Allow, MakeDecision::Without] {
        match t.rt.decide_make_request(&request.id, decision).await {
            Err(Error::NotAllowed(text)) => assert_eq!(text, why),
            other => panic!("expected NotAllowed, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }
    // Nothing was made, and the request still waits for someone who may answer.
    assert_eq!(t.rt.store().list_dots().await.unwrap().len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox_count().await.unwrap(), 1);

    a.become_(3, "member").await;
    let after = t.rt.decide_make_request(&request.id, MakeDecision::Allow);
    assert_eq!(after.await.unwrap().status, RequestStatus::Allowed);
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox_count().await.unwrap(), 0);
    t.rt.shutdown();
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_topics_cards_tell_a_make_a_job_an_ask_a_change_and_a_delete() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    assert!(cards(&t, &run).await.is_empty());

    // Make: a dot in a folder below the maker's, with a schedule.
    let mut asked = ask("Blog Watcher");
    asked.wanted.folder = Some("research/blogs".into());
    asked.wanted.schedule = Some(Some(every(120)));
    let made = make_as(&t, &run, asked).await;
    // Job: given, and ended by its run.
    let (job, its) = working_job(&t, &run, "Blog Watcher").await;
    let working = cards(&t, &run).await;
    t.rt.store()
        .finish_run(
            &its.id,
            RunStatus::Succeeded,
            Some("Three new posts."),
            None,
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    t.rt.makers().settle_jobs().await.unwrap();
    // Ask: a change that gives the dot the browser, which the maker does not have.
    let change = change_request(&t, &run, "Blog Watcher").await;
    let asking = cards(&t, &run).await;
    let waiting_card = t.rt.make_request_card(&change.id).await.unwrap();
    // Allow, then a change within reach.
    t.rt.decide_make_request(&change.id, MakeDecision::Allow)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let purpose = ChangeDot {
        dot: "Blog Watcher".into(),
        purpose: Some("Reads four feeds".into()),
        wanted: Wanted::default(),
    };
    t.rt.makers().change_dot(&run.id, purpose).await.unwrap();
    let before = cards(&t, &run).await;

    // One card per thing that happened, in order. The person's answer has none of its own: it
    // shows on the ask card.
    let entries = log(&t, &run).await;
    let kinds: Vec<MakingEventKind> = entries.iter().map(|e| e.kind).collect();
    assert_eq!(
        kinds,
        [
            MakingEventKind::Made,
            MakingEventKind::JobStarted,
            MakingEventKind::JobEnded,
            MakingEventKind::Asked,
            MakingEventKind::Changed,
            MakingEventKind::Answered,
            MakingEventKind::Changed,
        ]
    );
    let shown: Vec<&MakingEvent> = entries
        .iter()
        .filter(|e| e.kind != MakingEventKind::Answered)
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(before.len(), shown.len());
    for (card, entry) in before.iter().zip(&shown) {
        assert_eq!(
            head(card),
            (
                entry.id.as_str(),
                maker.id.as_str(),
                "Researcher",
                run.id.as_str(),
                Some(made.id.as_str()),
                "Blog Watcher",
                entry.created_at.as_str(),
            )
        );
        assert_eq!(card.root_run_id, run.root_run_id);
    }

    // The made card: the purpose as it is now, the schedule in words, and what the dot uses.
    assert_eq!(
        before[0].what,
        CardWhat::Made {
            purpose: "Reads four feeds".into(),
            schedule: Some("every 2 hours".into()),
            uses: Some("Uses: the browser, folder research/blogs. No secrets.".into()),
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(
        serde_json::to_value(&before[0]).unwrap(),
        json!({
            "id": entries[0].id,
            "maker_dot_id": maker.id,
            "maker_name": "Researcher",
            "run_id": run.id,
            "root_run_id": run.root_run_id,
            "dot_id": made.id,
            "dot_name": "Blog Watcher",
            "created_at": entries[0].created_at,
            "kind": "made",
            "purpose": "Reads four feeds",
            "schedule": "every 2 hours",
            "uses": "Uses: the browser, folder research/blogs. No secrets.",
        })
    );
    // Before the browser was allowed, the sentence had none.
    assert_eq!(
        working[0].what,
        CardWhat::Made {
            purpose: "Reads the feeds".into(),
            schedule: Some("every 2 hours".into()),
            uses: Some("Uses: folder research/blogs. No secrets.".into()),
        }
    );

    // The job's cards: "is working" while it works, and how it ended once it has.
    let job_card = |status: Option<JobStatus>, how: Option<JobEnd>, run_exists: bool| JobCard {
        job_id: job.id.clone(),
        message: "Read the blogs now.".into(),
        job_run_id: Some(its.id.clone()),
        run_exists,
        status,
        how,
    };
    assert_eq!(working.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(
        working[1].what,
        CardWhat::JobStarted(job_card(Some(JobStatus::Working), None, true))
    );
    let ended = job_card(Some(JobStatus::Ended), Some(JobEnd::Succeeded), true);
    assert_eq!(before[1].what, CardWhat::JobStarted(ended.clone()));
    assert_eq!(before[2].what, CardWhat::JobEnded(ended));
    assert_eq!(
        serde_json::to_value(&before[2].what).unwrap(),
        json!({
            "kind": "job_ended",
            "job_id": job.id,
            "message": "Read the blogs now.",
            "job_run_id": its.id,
            "run_exists": true,
            "status": "ended",
            "how": "succeeded",
        })
    );

    // The ask card carries the whole card: as it waited, and then how it ended.
    assert_eq!(
        waiting_card.title,
        "Researcher wants to give Blog Watcher more than it has"
    );
    assert_eq!(waiting_card.lines, ["The browser"]);
    assert!(waiting_card.can_allow && !waiting_card.can_without);
    assert_eq!(waiting_card.request.status, RequestStatus::Waiting);
    assert_eq!(
        asking[3].what,
        CardWhat::Asked {
            request_id: change.id.clone(),
            card: Some(waiting_card.clone()),
        }
    );
    let answered = t.rt.make_request_card(&change.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(answered.request.status, RequestStatus::Allowed);
    assert!(answered.request.decided_at.is_some());
    assert!(!answered.can_allow && !answered.can_without);
    assert_eq!(
        before[3].what,
        CardWhat::Asked {
            request_id: change.id.clone(),
            card: Some(answered),
        }
    );
    let as_json = serde_json::to_value(&asking[3].what).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(as_json["kind"], "asked");
    assert_eq!(as_json["request_id"], change.id.as_str());
    assert_eq!(
        as_json["card"],
        serde_json::to_value(&waiting_card).unwrap()
    );

    // The two changes, each with what changed.
    let changed = |what: &str| CardWhat::Changed {
        what: vec![what.to_string()],
    };
    assert_eq!(before[4].what, changed("browser"));
    assert_eq!(before[5].what, changed("purpose"));
    assert_eq!(
        serde_json::to_value(&before[5].what).unwrap(),
        json!({"kind": "changed", "what": ["purpose"]})
    );

    // Delete: the maker deletes the dot. Every card of it says the dot is gone.
    t.rt.makers()
        .delete_dot(&run.id, "Blog Watcher")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let after = cards(&t, &run).await;
    assert_eq!(after.len(), 7);
    assert!(after.iter().all(|card| card.dot_id.is_none()));
    assert!(after.iter().all(|card| card.dot_name == "Blog Watcher"));
    // The made card keeps the purpose the dot was made with.
    assert_eq!(
        after[0].what,
        CardWhat::Made {
            purpose: "Reads the feeds".into(),
            schedule: None,
            uses: None,
        }
    );
    // The job's rows and runs went with the dot; how it ended stays on its last card.
    assert_eq!(
        after[1].what,
        CardWhat::JobStarted(job_card(None, None, false))
    );
    assert_eq!(
        after[2].what,
        CardWhat::JobEnded(job_card(None, Some(JobEnd::Succeeded), false))
    );
    // The change request went with the dot it was for: its card says so and does not fail.
    assert_eq!(
        after[3].what,
        CardWhat::Asked {
            request_id: change.id.clone(),
            card: None,
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(after[6].what, CardWhat::Deleted);
    assert_eq!(
        serde_json::to_value(&after[6].what).unwrap(),
        json!({"kind": "deleted"})
    );
    // A card reads back as it was written.
    let text = serde_json::to_string(&before).unwrap();
    let back: Vec<MakingCard> = serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(back, before);
}

#[test]
fn the_uses_sentence_names_what_a_dot_uses_and_never_a_value() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let work = dir.path().join("work");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(work.join("research").join("blogs")).unwrap();
    let maker = fake_dot("Researcher", &work, WorkspaceMode::Folder);
    let folder = |path: &std::path::Path| path.to_string_lossy().to_string();

    // Nothing: no Library item, no browser, no folder yet, no variable.
    let mut nothing = spec("Blog Watcher");
    nothing.workdir = String::new();
    assert_eq!(
        uses_line(&nothing, Some(&maker)),
        "Uses: nothing. No secrets."
    );

    // Items, by kind, then the browser and the person's Claude settings.
    let mut items = nothing.clone();
    items.uses = Uses {
        mcp_servers: vec!["github".into()],
        skills: vec!["summarize".into()],
        plugins: vec!["formatter".into()],
        context: vec!["handbook".into()],
        apps: vec!["projects".into()],
    };
    items.browser = true;
    items.use_user_settings = true;
    assert_eq!(
        uses_line(&items, Some(&maker)),
        "Uses: MCP server github, skill summarize, plugin formatter, context collection \
         handbook, app projects, the browser, your Claude settings. No secrets."
    );

    // Variables: each name with what it is for. The sentence is built from the dot's settings,
    // which hold names only.
    let mut variables = nothing.clone();
    variables.uses.mcp_servers = vec!["github".into()];
    variables.variables = Grants(
        [
            ("mcp:github".to_string(), vec!["GITHUB_TOKEN".to_string()]),
            (
                "shell".to_string(),
                vec!["API_KEY".to_string(), "REGION".to_string()],
            ),
        ]
        .into(),
    );
    assert_eq!(
        uses_line(&variables, Some(&maker)),
        "Uses: MCP server github. Variables: GITHUB_TOKEN for the server 'github', API_KEY for \
         the shell, REGION for the shell."
    );

    // A folder below the maker's is named from there, the maker's own by its owner, and any
    // other in full.
    let mut below = nothing.clone();
    below.workdir = folder(&work.join("research").join("blogs"));
    assert_eq!(
        uses_line(&below, Some(&maker)),
        "Uses: folder research/blogs. No secrets."
    );
    let mut same = nothing.clone();
    same.workdir = folder(&work);
    assert_eq!(
        uses_line(&same, Some(&maker)),
        "Uses: Researcher's folder. No secrets."
    );
    let elsewhere = dir.path().join("Dots").join("blog-watcher");
    let mut other = nothing.clone();
    other.workdir = folder(&elsewhere);
    let full = format!("Uses: folder {}. No secrets.", folder(&elsewhere));
    assert_eq!(uses_line(&other, Some(&maker)), full);
    // Without the maker (it was deleted), every folder is named in full.
    let alone = format!("Uses: folder {}. No secrets.", below.workdir);
    assert_eq!(uses_line(&below, None), alone);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_made_dot_the_person_deletes_ends_its_job_and_takes_its_request_with_it() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    let made = make(&t, &run, "Blog Watcher").await;
    // Its job waits for the person's answer: no run of the dot is going.
    let (job, its) = working_job(&t, &run, "Blog Watcher").await;
    t.rt.store()
        .add_question(&made.id, &its.id, "Which of the three first?", None)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .expect("the run's first question");
    t.rt.store()
        .finish_run(&its.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, Some("Which first?"), None)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    t.rt.makers().settle_jobs().await.unwrap();
    let waiting = t.rt.store().get_making_job(&job.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(waiting.status, JobStatus::WaitingAnswer);
    // A change the maker asked for it waits too.
    let change = change_request(&t, &run, "Blog Watcher").await;
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox().await.unwrap().make_requests.len(), 1);
    assert!(wakes(&t).await.is_empty());
    let mut rx = t.rt.subscribe();

    t.rt.delete_dot(&made.id).await.unwrap();

    // The topic's cards are told to read again.
    let topic = (maker.id.clone(), run.root_run_id.clone());
    let told = updated(&mut rx);
    assert!(!told.is_empty(), "no MakingUpdated was published");
    assert!(told.iter().all(|seen| *seen == topic), "{told:?}");
    // The change request went with the dot, out of the Inbox and its count.
    assert!(matches!(
        t.rt.store().get_make_request(&change.id).await,
        Err(Error::NotFound(_))
    ));
    assert!(t.rt.inbox().await.unwrap().make_requests.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox_count().await.unwrap(), 0);
    assert!(matches!(
        t.rt.make_request_card(&change.id).await,
        Err(Error::NotFound(_))
    ));
    // The job ended with the dot, and the maker is woken for it once.
    assert_eq!(wakes(&t).await, [deleted_message("Blog Watcher")]);
    assert_eq!(
        wakes(&t).await,
        ["\"Blog Watcher\" was deleted before the job ended."]
    );
    t.rt.makers().settle_jobs().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(wakes(&t).await.len(), 1);
    assert!(t
        .rt
        .store()
        .open_making_jobs(None)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .is_empty());

    // The cards say the dot is gone, and none fails to read.
    let after = cards(&t, &run).await;
    let kinds: Vec<&str> = after
        .iter()
        .map(|card| match &card.what {
            CardWhat::Made { .. } => "made",
            CardWhat::Asked { .. } => "asked",
            CardWhat::Changed { .. } => "changed",
            CardWhat::Deleted => "deleted",
            CardWhat::JobStarted(_) => "job_started",
            CardWhat::JobWaiting(_) => "job_waiting",
            CardWhat::JobEnded(_) => "job_ended",
        })
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        kinds,
        ["made", "job_started", "job_waiting", "asked", "job_ended"]
    );
    assert!(after.iter().all(|card| card.dot_id.is_none()));
    assert_eq!(
        after[0].what,
        CardWhat::Made {
            purpose: "Reads the feeds".into(),
            schedule: None,
            uses: None,
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(
        after[3].what,
        CardWhat::Asked {
            request_id: change.id.clone(),
            card: None,
        }
    );
    let gone = |how: Option<JobEnd>| JobCard {
        job_id: job.id.clone(),
        message: "Read the blogs now.".into(),
        job_run_id: Some(its.id.clone()),
        run_exists: false,
        status: None,
        how,
    };
    assert_eq!(after[1].what, CardWhat::JobStarted(gone(None)));
    assert_eq!(after[2].what, CardWhat::JobWaiting(gone(None)));
    assert_eq!(
        after[4].what,
        CardWhat::JobEnded(gone(Some(JobEnd::Deleted)))
    );
    // A place in the maker's total is free again.
    assert_eq!(t.rt.store().count_made_dots(&maker.id).await.unwrap(), 0);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_made_dot_without_a_job_is_deleted_as_any_dot_and_its_card_is_told() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    let made = make(&t, &run, "Blog Watcher").await;
    let plain = t.rt.create_dot(spec_in(&t, "Plain"), None, None).await;
    let plain = plain.unwrap();
    let mut rx = t.rt.subscribe();

    // A dot nobody made is deleted with no word to the makers.
    t.rt.delete_dot(&plain.id).await.unwrap();
    assert!(updated(&mut rx).is_empty());
    // A made dot tells the topic it was made in, once.
    t.rt.delete_dot(&made.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        updated(&mut rx),
        [(maker.id.clone(), run.root_run_id.clone())]
    );
    assert!(wakes(&t).await.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(log(&t, &run).await.len(), 1);
    // A dot that does not exist is refused as before.
    assert!(matches!(
        t.rt.delete_dot(&made.id).await,
        Err(Error::NotFound(_))
    ));
}

/// The spec of a dot named `name` that works in the test's `work` folder.
fn spec_in(t: &T, name: &str) -> DotSpec {
    let mut s = spec(name);
    s.workdir = t.work().to_string_lossy().to_string();
    s.workspace_mode = WorkspaceMode::Folder;
    s
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_deleted_maker_leaves_nothing_dangling() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    let one = make(&t, &run, "One").await;
    // A job that ended, whose wake waits behind the maker's run; and a request that waits.
    let (_, its) = working_job(&t, &run, "One").await;
    t.rt.store()
        .finish_run(&its.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, Some("Done."), None)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    t.rt.makers().settle_jobs().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(wakes(&t).await.len(), 1);
    let request = request(&t, &run, ask_browser("Two")).await;
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox_count().await.unwrap(), 1);
    assert_eq!(cards(&t, &run).await.len(), 4);
    // The maker's run ends: a dot with a run going is not deleted. The wake still waits.
    t.rt.store()
        .finish_run(&run.id, RunStatus::Succeeded, None, None)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(wakes(&t).await.len(), 1);
    let mut rx = t.rt.subscribe();

    t.rt.delete_dot(&maker.id).await.unwrap();

    // The Inbox and its count are told and no longer have the request.
    let told = updated(&mut rx);
    assert!(
        told.contains(&(maker.id.clone(), run.root_run_id.clone())),
        "{told:?}"
    );
    assert!(t.rt.inbox().await.unwrap().make_requests.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(t.rt.inbox_count().await.unwrap(), 0);
    assert!(t.rt.waiting_make_requests().await.unwrap().is_empty());
    // Its requests, cards, jobs and wakes went with it.
    let store = t.rt.store();
    assert!(store
        .list_make_requests(None, false)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .is_empty());
    assert!(cards(&t, &run).await.is_empty());
    assert!(jobs(&t, &run).await.is_empty());
    assert!(wakes(&t).await.is_empty());
    assert!(matches!(
        t.rt.make_request_card(&request.id).await,
        Err(Error::NotFound(_))
    ));
    assert!(matches!(
        t.rt.decide_make_request(&request.id, MakeDecision::Allow)
            .await,
        Err(Error::NotFound(_))
    ));
    // The dot it made stays, and still says who made it.
    let overview = t.rt.dot_overview().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(overview.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(overview[0].dot.id, one.id);
    let made = overview[0].dot.made.as_ref().expect("who made it");
    assert_eq!(made.by_dot_id, None);
    assert_eq!(made.by_name, "Researcher");
    assert_eq!(overview[0].made_dots, 0);
    // Later passes find nothing to follow.
    t.rt.makers().settle_jobs().await.unwrap();
    t.rt.makers().deliver_wakes().await.unwrap();
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_ask_is_always_announced_and_a_made_dot_says_whether_the_person_typed() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let mut rx = t.rt.subscribe();

    // A run the person started by typing: the made dot is announced as typed.
    let typed = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    let one = make(&t, &typed, "One").await;
    assert_eq!(
        notices(&mut rx),
        [json!({
            "type": "dot_made",
            "dot_id": maker.id,
            "root_run_id": typed.root_run_id,
            "maker_name": "Researcher",
            "made_dot_id": one.id,
            "name": "One",
            "purpose": "Reads the feeds",
            "typed": true,
        })]
    );
    // An ask is announced whoever started the run, with what its notification says.
    let asked = request(&t, &typed, ask_browser("Blog Watcher")).await;
    assert_eq!(
        notices(&mut rx),
        [json!({
            "type": "make_requested",
            "request_id": asked.id,
            "dot_id": maker.id,
            "root_run_id": typed.root_run_id,
            "title": "Researcher wants to make a dot with more than it has",
            "name": "Blog Watcher",
            "purpose": "Reads the feeds",
        })]
    );
    let change = change_request(&t, &typed, "One").await;
    let said = notices(&mut rx);
    assert_eq!(said.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(said[0]["type"], "make_requested");
    assert_eq!(said[0]["request_id"], change.id.as_str());
    assert_eq!(
        said[0]["title"],
        "Researcher wants to give One more than it has"
    );
    assert_eq!(said[0]["name"], "One");
    // The dot the person's own answer makes is not announced: they made it happen.
    t.rt.decide_make_request(&asked.id, MakeDecision::Allow)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert!(notices(&mut rx).is_empty());

    // A run that resumes the typed one after an approval is the same turn.
    let mut resume = NewRun::new(&maker.id, TriggerKind::Resume);
    resume.parent_run_id = Some(typed.id.clone());
    resume.root_run_id = Some(typed.root_run_id.clone());
    let resume = t.rt.store().create_run(&resume).await.unwrap();
    let resume = started(&t, &resume.id).await;
    make(&t, &resume, "Two").await;
    let said = notices(&mut rx);
    assert_eq!(said.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(said[0]["typed"], true);

    // A wake, a scheduled run and an answer to a question are not typed.
    let wake = json!({"message": "\"One\" finished the job.", "wake_id": "w1"});
    let woken = live_run_with(&t, &maker, TriggerKind::Chat, wake).await;
    make(&t, &woken, "Three").await;
    let scheduled = live_run_with(&t, &maker, TriggerKind::Schedule, json!({})).await;
    make(&t, &scheduled, "Four").await;
    let said = notices(&mut rx);
    assert_eq!(said.len(), 2);
    for (event, name, run) in [(&said[0], "Three", &woken), (&said[1], "Four", &scheduled)] {
        assert_eq!(event["type"], "dot_made");
        assert_eq!(event["name"], name);
        assert_eq!(event["root_run_id"], run.root_run_id.as_str());
        assert_eq!(event["typed"], false);
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_makers_row_counts_the_dots_it_keeps() {
    let t = start().await;
    let maker = maker(&t).await;
    let run = live_run(&t, &maker).await;
    let one = make(&t, &run, "One").await;
    make(&t, &run, "Two").await;
    // A request that waits is no dot yet.
    request(&t, &run, ask_browser("Three")).await;

    let rows = t.rt.dot_overview().await.unwrap();
    let count = |rows: &[dots_core::model::DotOverview], id: &str| {
        let row = rows.iter().find(|row| row.dot.id == id).unwrap();
        (row.made_dots, row.dot.spec.making.total)
    };
    // "2 of 10" for the maker; a made dot has made none, and says who made it.
    assert_eq!(count(&rows, &maker.id), (2, 10));
    assert_eq!(count(&rows, &one.id), (0, 10));
    let row = rows.iter().find(|row| row.dot.id == one.id).unwrap();
    let made = row.dot.made.as_ref().expect("who made it");
    assert_eq!(made.by_dot_id.as_deref(), Some(maker.id.as_str()));
    assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(row).unwrap()["made_dots"], json!(0));

    t.rt.delete_dot(&one.id).await.unwrap();
    let rows = t.rt.dot_overview().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(count(&rows, &maker.id), (1, 10));
}
```

```rust
    /// The core's event for a dot the maker `d` made in the topic `root`.
    fn dot_made(typed: bool) -> RuntimeEvent {
        RuntimeEvent::DotMade {
            dot_id: "d".into(),
            root_run_id: "root".into(),
            maker_name: "Researcher".into(),
            made_dot_id: "m".into(),
            name: "Blog Watcher".into(),
            purpose: "Reads the feeds".into(),
            typed,
        }
    }

    /// Dots-make-dots design section 11: the ask card notifies like an approval, each time
    /// the core says a request waits.
    #[test]
    fn a_makers_ask_always_notifies_and_opens_its_topic() {
        let mut n = Notifier::default();
        let ev = RuntimeEvent::MakeRequested {
            request_id: "q1".into(),
            dot_id: "d".into(),
            root_run_id: "root".into(),
            title: "Researcher wants to make a dot with more than it has".into(),
            name: "Blog Watcher".into(),
            purpose: "Reads the feeds\nand more".into(),
        };
        let notice = n.decide(&ev).expect("an ask notifies");
        assert_eq!(
            notice,
            Notice::MakeAsked {
                dot_id: "d".into(),
                root_run_id: "root".into(),
                title: "Researcher wants to make a dot with more than it has".into(),
                name: "Blog Watcher".into(),
                purpose: "Reads the feeds\nand more".into(),
            }
        );
        // The title is the card's own, whatever name the dot is looked up by.
        assert_eq!(
            notice_text(&notice, "A dot"),
            (
                "Researcher wants to make a dot with more than it has".into(),
                "Blog Watcher: Reads the feeds".into()
            )
        );
        assert_eq!(notice_route(&notice, "d"), "/chat/d/root");
        assert_eq!(click_route(&notice, Some("d")), "/chat/d/root");
        assert_eq!(notice_dot(&notice), Some("d"));
        // Quiet only while the person reads the maker's conversation, as an approval is.
        assert!(quiet(notice_dot(&notice), Some("d")));
        assert!(!quiet(notice_dot(&notice), Some("other")));
        assert!(affects_inbox(&ev));
        // A second request is told too; the log's own event tells nothing.
        assert!(n.decide(&ev).is_some());
        let updated = RuntimeEvent::MakingUpdated {
            dot_id: "d".into(),
            root_run_id: "root".into(),
        };
        assert_eq!(n.decide(&updated), None);
        assert!(affects_inbox(&updated));
    }

    /// Dots-make-dots design section 11: "<maker> made a dot: <name>" notifies when the
    /// maker's run was not started by a message the person just typed, and follows the
    /// setting a note follows.
    #[test]
    fn a_made_dot_notifies_only_when_the_person_did_not_type_and_notes_notify() {
        let mut n = Notifier::default();
        assert_eq!(n.decide(&dot_made(true)), None);
        let notice = n.decide(&dot_made(false)).expect("an untyped run's dot");
        assert_eq!(
            notice,
            Notice::DotMade {
                dot_id: "d".into(),
                root_run_id: "root".into(),
                maker_name: "Researcher".into(),
                name: "Blog Watcher".into(),
                purpose: "Reads the feeds".into(),
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            notice_text(&notice, "A dot"),
            (
                "Researcher made a dot: Blog Watcher".into(),
                "Reads the feeds".into()
            )
        );
        assert_eq!(notice_route(&notice, "d"), "/chat/d/root");
        assert_eq!(notice_dot(&notice), Some("d"));
        assert!(quiet(notice_dot(&notice), Some("d")));
        // Silent while notes are switched off in Settings; the ask has no such switch.
        assert!(made_notifies(true));
        assert!(!made_notifies(false));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! What the app shows of making (dots-make-dots design section 11): the cards of a maker's chat
//! topic, built from the makers' log with what each card says, and the sentence that says what
//! a made dot uses. They are built here, in the core, so every screen words them the same.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::Path;

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use super::jobs::{JobEnd, JobStatus, MakingJob};
use super::log::{MakingEvent, MakingEventKind};
use super::manage::schedule_words;
use super::reach::{folded, real_path};
use super::requests::MakeRequestCard;
use super::service::Makers;
use crate::library::LibraryKind;
use crate::model::{Dot, DotSpec};
use crate::vault::Consumer;
use crate::{Error, Result};

/// One card of a maker's chat topic (design section 11): one thing the maker did there, in the
/// order things happened. In JSON the fields of `what` lie beside the others, and `kind` says
/// which card it is.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct MakingCard {
    /// The id of the log's entry the card is built from: it stays the same from read to read.
    pub id: String,
    /// The maker.
    pub maker_dot_id: String,
    /// The maker's name now, for "made by <maker>" and "<maker> changed <name>".
    pub maker_name: String,
    /// The maker's run that did it: the card shows after that run's message.
    pub run_id: String,
    /// The maker's chat topic.
    pub root_run_id: String,
    /// The made dot the card is about, while it exists: `None` says the dot is gone, and for
    /// an ask for a new dot, that there is none yet.
    pub dot_id: Option<String>,
    /// The made dot's name when it happened; for an ask for a new dot, the name asked for.
    pub dot_name: String,
    pub created_at: String,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub what: CardWhat,
}

/// What a card says besides, by its kind (design section 11).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]
pub enum CardWhat {
    /// "Made dot: <name>". While the dot exists: its purpose and schedule as they are now, and
    /// what it uses (`uses_line`). Once it is gone: the purpose it was made with, and no
    /// schedule and no `uses`.
    Made {
        purpose: String,
        /// The schedule in plain words (`schedule_words`); `None` without one.
        schedule: Option<String>,
        uses: Option<String>,
    },
    /// The ask card (design section 7.2). `card` is the whole card as it is now, waiting or
    /// answered (`Makers::request_card`); `None` when the request is gone: the made dot a
    /// change was asked for was deleted.
    Asked {
        request_id: String,
        card: Option<MakeRequestCard>,
    },
    /// "<maker> changed <name>", with the settings that changed, in plain words.
    Changed { what: Vec<String> },
    /// "<maker> deleted <name>".
    Deleted,
    /// "<name> is working" (design section 8).
    JobStarted(JobCard),
    /// "<name> is waiting for your answer".
    JobWaiting(JobCard),
    /// "<name> finished", failed or was stopped: `how` says which.
    JobEnded(JobCard),
}

/// What a job's card says (design section 8).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct JobCard {
    pub job_id: String,
    /// The job's text.
    pub message: String,
    /// The made dot's run the card opens: the run the job started, the run that asked the
    /// person, or the job's last run.
    pub job_run_id: Option<String>,
    /// Whether that run still exists: a made dot's runs go with it.
    pub run_exists: bool,
    /// Where the job stands now, so a card of a job that has moved on can say so; `None` when
    /// the job went with its made dot.
    pub status: Option<JobStatus>,
    /// How the job ended, once it has; `None` for a job that went with its made dot, except
    /// on the card of its end.
    pub how: Option<JobEnd>,
}

/// What a made dot uses, in one line for its card (design section 11): "Uses: MCP server
/// github, folder research/blogs. No secrets." It names the Library items the dot names, by
/// kind, the browser, the person's Claude settings, and its folder; then its variables, each
/// with what it is for. It is built from the dot's settings, which hold the names of variables
/// and never a value. Items switched to "every dot" are not named: every dot has them.
///
/// The folder is named from the maker's when it lies below it ("folder research/blogs"), as
/// "<maker>'s folder" when it is the maker's own, and in full otherwise, or without `maker`.
pub fn uses_line(spec: &DotSpec, maker: Option<&Dot>) -> String {
    let mut parts: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for kind in LibraryKind::ALL {
        for name in spec.uses.names(*kind) {
            parts.push(format!("{} {name}", kind.label()));
        }
    }
    if spec.browser {
        parts.push("the browser".to_string());
    }
    if spec.use_user_settings {
        parts.push("your Claude settings".to_string());
    }
    parts.extend(folder_words(spec.workdir.trim(), maker));
    let mut line = if parts.is_empty() {
        "Uses: nothing.".to_string()
    } else {
        format!("Uses: {}.", parts.join(", "))
    };
    let mut variables: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for (consumer, names) in &spec.variables.0 {
        let what_for = match Consumer::parse(consumer) {
            Ok(Consumer::Mcp(server)) => format!("the server '{server}'"),
            Ok(Consumer::Shell) => "the shell".to_string(),
            Err(_) => consumer.clone(),
        };
        variables.extend(names.iter().map(|name| format!("{name} for {what_for}")));
    }
    if variables.is_empty() {
        line.push_str(" No secrets.");
    } else {
        line.push_str(&format!(" Variables: {}.", variables.join(", ")));
    }
    line
}

/// The folder `folder` of a made dot in words; `None` for a blank one.
fn folder_words(folder: &str, maker: Option<&Dot>) -> Option<String> {
    if folder.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let makers = maker.filter(|maker| !maker.spec.workdir.trim().is_empty());
    if let Some(maker) = makers {
        let real = real_path(Path::new(folder));
        let makers = real_path(Path::new(maker.spec.workdir.trim()));
        if let Ok(below) = folded(&real).strip_prefix(folded(&makers)) {
            let depth = below.components().count();
            if depth == 0 {
                return Some(format!("{}'s folder", maker.spec.name));
            }
            // The parts below the maker's folder, in the case the folder has.
            let parts: Vec<String> = real
                .components()
                .map(|part| part.as_os_str().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
                .collect();
            let below = parts[parts.len().saturating_sub(depth)..].join("/");
            return Some(format!("folder {below}"));
        }
    }
    Some(format!("folder {folder}"))
}

/// The text `key` of a log entry's detail, when it has one.
fn text(entry: &MakingEvent, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
    entry
        .detail
        .get(key)
        .and_then(|value| value.as_str())
        .map(str::to_string)
}

impl Makers {
    /// The cards of the maker's chat topic `root_run_id`, oldest first (design section 11):
    /// one per entry of the topic's log, each with what its card shows, so the chat draws them
    /// with no further call. The person's answer to a request has no card of its own: it shows
    /// on the ask card, which carries the request as it is now. Empty for a topic no maker
    /// did anything in, and once the maker is deleted.
    ///
    /// A waiting request is checked again as its card is built (`request_card`), so reading
    /// the cards may mark a request gone. A made dot, a request or a job that is gone is said
    /// on its card and fails nothing.
    pub async fn cards(&self, root_run_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<MakingCard>> {
        let store = &self.parts.store;
        let entries = store.list_making_events(root_run_id).await?;
        let Some(first) = entries.first() else {
            return Ok(Vec::new());
        };
        let maker = match store.get_dot(&first.maker_dot_id).await {
            Ok(maker) => maker,
            // The maker went since the log was read, and the log with it.
            Err(Error::NotFound(_)) => return Ok(Vec::new()),
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        };
        let jobs: HashMap<String, MakingJob> = store
            .making_jobs_of_topic(root_run_id)
            .await?
            .into_iter()
            .map(|job| (job.id.clone(), job))
            .collect();
        // A job's text is in the entry of its start; its later cards show it too.
        let messages: HashMap<String, String> = entries
            .iter()
            .filter(|entry| entry.kind == MakingEventKind::JobStarted)
            .filter_map(|entry| Some((text(entry, "job_id")?, text(entry, "message")?)))
            .collect();
        let mut cards = Vec::new();
        for entry in &entries {
            // The made dot as it is now, while it exists.
            let dot = match entry.dot_id.as_deref() {
                Some(id) => match store.get_dot(id).await {
                    Ok(dot) => Some(dot),
                    Err(Error::NotFound(_)) => None,
                    Err(e) => return Err(e),
                },
                None => None,
            };
            let what = match entry.kind {
                // Shown on its ask card.
                MakingEventKind::Answered => continue,
                MakingEventKind::Made => match &dot {
                    Some(dot) => CardWhat::Made {
                        purpose: dot
                            .made
                            .as_ref()
                            .map(|made| made.purpose.clone())
                            .unwrap_or_default(),
                        schedule: dot.spec.schedule.as_ref().map(schedule_words),
                        uses: Some(uses_line(&dot.spec, Some(&maker))),
                    },
                    None => CardWhat::Made {
                        purpose: text(entry, "purpose").unwrap_or_default(),
                        schedule: None,
                        uses: None,
                    },
                },
                MakingEventKind::Asked => {
                    let request_id = text(entry, "request_id").unwrap_or_default();
                    let card = match self.request_card(&request_id).await {
                        Ok(card) => Some(card),
                        Err(Error::NotFound(_)) => None,
                        Err(e) => return Err(e),
                    };
                    CardWhat::Asked { request_id, card }
                }
                MakingEventKind::Changed => CardWhat::Changed {
                    what: entry
                        .detail
                        .get("what")
                        .and_then(|what| serde_json::from_value(what.clone()).ok())
                        .unwrap_or_default(),
                },
                MakingEventKind::Deleted => CardWhat::Deleted,
                MakingEventKind::JobStarted => {
                    CardWhat::JobStarted(self.job_card(entry, &jobs, &messages).await?)
                }
                MakingEventKind::JobWaiting => {
                    CardWhat::JobWaiting(self.job_card(entry, &jobs, &messages).await?)
                }
                MakingEventKind::JobEnded => {
                    CardWhat::JobEnded(self.job_card(entry, &jobs, &messages).await?)
                }
            };
            cards.push(MakingCard {
                id: entry.id.clone(),
                maker_dot_id: entry.maker_dot_id.clone(),
                maker_name: maker.spec.name.clone(),
                run_id: entry.run_id.clone(),
                root_run_id: entry.root_run_id.clone(),
                dot_id: dot.map(|dot| dot.id),
                dot_name: entry.dot_name.clone(),
                created_at: entry.created_at.clone(),
                what,
            });
        }
        Ok(cards)
    }

    /// What the card of the job entry `entry` says: `jobs` are the topic's jobs that exist,
    /// by id, and `messages` the texts of the jobs the topic's log saw start.
    async fn job_card(
        &self,
        entry: &MakingEvent,
        jobs: &HashMap<String, MakingJob>,
        messages: &HashMap<String, String>,
    ) -> Result<JobCard> {
        let job_id = text(entry, "job_id").unwrap_or_default();
        let job = jobs.get(&job_id);
        let job_run_id = text(entry, "run_id");
        let run_exists = match job_run_id.as_deref() {
            Some(id) => match self.parts.store.get_run(id).await {
                Ok(_) => true,
                Err(Error::NotFound(_)) => false,
                Err(e) => return Err(e),
            },
            None => false,
        };
        // The entry of a job's end says how it ended, also once the job is gone.
        let how = text(entry, "how")
            .and_then(|how| JobEnd::parse(&how).ok())
            .or(job.and_then(|job| job.ended_how));
        Ok(JobCard {
            message: messages
                .get(&job_id)
                .cloned()
                .or(job.map(|job| job.message.clone()))
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            job_id,
            job_run_id,
            run_exists,
            status: job.map(|job| job.status),
            how,
        })
    }
}
```

```rust
    /// The person deletes the dot `dot_id` (design sections 9 and 11): any dot goes through
    /// here, so that what the makers show of it is told. The dot goes as `DotAdmin::delete`
    /// takes it, with its checks and its refusals.
    ///
    /// For a made dot: a job of it that waits for the person's answer ends with it, its
    /// maker's topic gets a `job_ended` entry (`deleted`), and the maker is woken once with
    /// `jobs::deleted_message`, as when the maker deletes the dot itself; a job whose run has
    /// ended is settled first, so its result is not lost. A change request that waited for
    /// the dot goes with it. For a maker: its log, requests, jobs and wakes go with it, and
    /// the dots it made stay. Every topic that showed the dot, or a waiting request of the
    /// deleted maker, gets a `MakingUpdated`, so open cards, the Inbox and its count read
    /// again. The log gets no `deleted` entry: that card says the maker deleted the dot.
    pub async fn person_deletes(&self, dot_id: &str) -> Result<()> {

            if let Err(e) = self.settle_jobs().await {
                tracing::warn!(dot = %dot_id, "settling the jobs before a delete failed: {e}");

        }

        // the dot goes.
        let one_at_a_time = p.one_at_a_time.lock().await;

        let (open_jobs, topics) = self.delete_and_tell(&dot).await?;
        for (maker_id, topic) in &topics {

    }
```

```rust
/// A make request, or a request to change a made dot, that waits for the person, as the Inbox
/// lists it (design section 11): what the Inbox sorts, links and titles it by. The whole card,
/// with its buttons, is `Makers::request_card`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct PendingMakeRequest {
    /// The request's id.
    pub id: String,
    /// The maker that asked.
    pub dot_id: String,
    /// The maker's name.

    /// The maker's chat topic, where the ask card shows.

    pub created_at: String,
}

impl PendingMakeRequest {
    /// The Inbox's item for `request`, whose maker is named `maker`.
    pub fn of(request: &MakeRequest, maker: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            id: request.id.clone(),
            dot_id: request.maker_dot_id.clone(),
            dot_name: maker.to_string(),
            root_run_id: request.root_run_id.clone(),
            kind: request.kind,
            name: request.name.clone(),
            purpose: request.purpose.clone(),
            title: request.title(maker),
            lines: request.lines(maker),
            status: request.status,
            created_at: request.created_at.clone(),
        }
    }
}

    /// The ask cards of every request the person has not answered, of every maker, newest
    /// first: the Inbox's section (design section 11). Each is checked again as `request_card`
    /// checks it. A request that went while the list was read is left out.
    pub async fn waiting_cards(&self) -> Result<Vec<MakeRequestCard>> {
        let mut cards = Vec::new();
        let waiting = self.parts.store.list_make_requests(None, true).await?;
        for request in waiting.iter().rev() {
            match self.request_card(&request.id).await {
                Ok(card) => cards.push(card),
                Err(Error::NotFound(_)) => {}
                Err(e) => return Err(e),
            }
        }
        Ok(cards)
    }
```

```rust
    /// Whether the person started the turn `run` belongs to by typing a message (design
    /// section 11): `run` carries a typed message (`prompt::is_typed`), or it resumes, after
    /// an approval, a run that does. A wake, a job, a scheduled run and an answer to a
    /// question are not typed.
    async fn started_by_typing(&self, run: &Run) -> bool {
        let mut at = run.clone();
        // A turn has far fewer resumes than this.
        for _ in 0..50 {
            if is_typed(&at) {
                return true;
            }
            let parent = match (at.trigger, at.parent_run_id.as_deref()) {
                (TriggerKind::Resume, Some(parent)) => parent,
                _ => return false,
            };
            at = match self.parts.store.get_run(parent).await {
                Ok(run) => run,
                Err(_) => return false,
            };
        }
        false
    }
```

### Task 15: The spec says what plan A built

Section 15 of the spec records the names, where the code differs from sections 6 to 11 and why, what plan B must know, and what is left open.

**Files:**
- Modify: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-dots-make-dots-design.md`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Tasks 1 to 14 as built. If a fix during execution changed a behaviour the section describes, change the sentence to match.
- Produces: spec section 15, which plan B is written from.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the section**

**In `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-dots-make-dots-design.md`, replace:**

```markdown
- The trigger kind of a job run, which decides whether the usage holds treat it as background.
```

**with:**

```markdown
- The trigger kind of a job run, which decides whether the usage holds treat it as background.

## 15. What plan A built

Plan A (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-10-dots-make-dots-a.md`) built the core: everything above except the screens of section 11, which are plan B's. This section records where the code differs from the sections above, and what plan B must know. Where this section and an earlier one disagree, this section says what the code does.

### Names

- Module `dots_core::making`: `reach` (the check of section 6), `service` (`Makers`, `make_dot`, the limits), `requests` (the ask card and its three answers), `manage` (list, change, delete), `jobs`, `wake`, `log` (the making log of a topic), `cards` (the log as the chat's cards), `tools` (the five tools, shared by both engines).
- Tools: `make_dot`, `change_dot`, `delete_dot`, `give_job`, `list_made_dots`; on the Claude engine `mcp__dots__<name>`. Policy name `MakeDots`.
- Migrations `0046` to `0053`: the dot's making columns, the `MakeDots` rule for existing policies, `making_events`, `making_wakes`, `make_requests` (and its `ask` column for a change), `making_jobs`, `made_spend_kept`.
- Limits: `MAKE_PER_RUN_DEFAULT` 3 (at most 10), `MAKE_TOTAL_DEFAULT` 10 (at most 50), `MAX_WAITING_REQUESTS` 3, `MAX_JOBS_BETWEEN_TYPED` 6, `MAX_JOB` 4,000 characters, `MAX_JOB_RESULT` 8,000, `MAX_PURPOSE` 200.

### Where the code differs

| Section | The code | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 6, spend "and month, for the monthly cap" | A dot has daily caps only. A deleted made dot's spend counts for the day toward its makers' caps, and for the month toward the global monthly cap | No per-dot monthly cap exists |
| 6, spend (silent on a deleted middle maker) | Deleting a maker that was itself made keeps, for the makers above it, what the living dots below it spent so far this month. Later spend of those dots is their own | Otherwise A could shed C's spend by deleting B |
| 8 "If the made dot is busy, the job queues behind its current run" | True when the made dot is busy in another topic. A second job from the same maker conversation to the same dot is refused until the first ends, with a sentence that says the maker will be woken | Jobs of one conversation share one topic of the made dot, and a topic takes one run at a time |
| 8 "the person can stop it from the made dot's topic" | Stopping a job that waits on a question is dismissing the question. A question never answered or dismissed keeps the job open, and that dot takes no further job from that conversation | The product has no other stop for a topic whose run has ended |
| 8 "counts as background or not as the maker's run did" | A job's run is a chat run with `"background": true` in its payload when the maker's run was background. A resume run after an approval and a wake run are foreground | Resume runs are foreground for every dot today; wakes are plain chat runs |
| 8 loop guard | Counted from the `job_started` entries of the making log since the newest typed run of the topic | Job rows go with a deleted dot; the log does not |
| 9 `delete_dot` | With "Always ask before sending or deleting" on (it is on in every preset), a maker's `delete_dot` waits for the person's approval like any other delete a dot does. With the setting off it deletes at once | The setting is the person's, and a dot's delete of an app's data or a file already asks |
| 9 (silent) a person's delete of a made dot | A job of that dot that was still open ends as `deleted` and its maker is woken once; a waiting change request for it goes, and the topics that showed the dot are told | A maker waiting on a job should learn the dot is gone |
| 11.2 "Uses: web fetch, …" | The line names Library items by kind, the browser, the person's Claude settings, the folder, and variables by name: `Uses: the browser, folder research/blogs. No secrets.` or `… Variables: API_KEY for the shell.` `Uses: nothing.` when empty | A dot has a permission preset, not a list of tools; a variable may be plain, so "No secrets." is said only when there are none |
| 11.5 "Both follow the existing notification settings" | The ask notifies always, as an approval does. "<maker> made a dot: <name>" follows `notify_on_notes` and is not sent for a typed run, or for a dot made by the person's own Allow | The one setting that exists is for notes, and it does not silence approvals |
| 11, the prompt section | In a conversation's first prompt only, as every prompt section. The list of made dots is from that moment; `list_made_dots` gives it as it is now | A resumed session already holds it |
| 7.2, who may answer | Allow and "without the extras" need `EditDots` (and `GrantEntries` when a variable is granted). Refuse needs no right | App proposals ask `AnswerApprovals` for every answer; plan B decides whether Refuse should too |

### For plan B

- `Runtime`: `make_request_card(id)`, `waiting_make_requests()`, `decide_make_request(id, decision)`, `making_cards(root_run_id)`. `Inbox.make_requests` (kind `make_request`) is slim; the Inbox section reads the full cards with `waiting_make_requests()`. `DotOverview.made_dots` with `dot.making.total` gives "N of M". `DotSpend.shared_today` is the maker's shared total.
- Events: `making_updated` (re-read a topic's cards), `make_requested`, `dot_made`. The UI's `runtime-events.ts` handles none of them yet.
- The UI schemas for the new fields are optional until plan B updates the test mocks; then they become required. The Inbox contract sample has no make request, because the UI's `inboxKeys` does not know the kind yet.
- A job's run and a wake's run are chat runs. Their payloads carry `job_id` and `job_from`, or `wake_id`; the chat must not draw them as the person's messages, and delivery tracking must not offer Retry for them as for a typed message.
- On the local engine a making call shows as tool `MakeDots` with input `{"tool", "input"}`; on the Claude engine as `mcp__dots__make_dot`. A local approval is applied by the resume run, so the made dot's `made.run_id` is that run.
- A held run of a made dot names the maker's cap in its text only (`<maker> reached its $2.00 daily cap, shared with the dots it made`); no field says whose cap it is.
- `spend_today` lists a maker only when it has a cap or a run of its own today.
- No screen turns "Can make dots" on until plan B: until then the feature is reachable only through the store.

### Left open

- The making log and jobs are keyed by the topic's root run when written. Moving or merging a topic's runs does not move them: the cards stay with the old root, and the loop guard counts from the new one.
- A wake lands in a new topic when the maker's topic has no session to resume.
- "Another model of the same engine" is not checked: a made dot may name any model its engine accepts.
- A run still going when the person deletes a maker above it has only its spend so far kept for the makers further up.
```
